name: Ace Attorney
scope: The ten mainline courtroom games across four sub-series. The crossover Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright and the mobile-only re-releases are excluded.
caveat: Within each sub-series, chronology matches release order. Across them it does not: The Great Ace Attorney is a Meiji-era prequel about Phoenix's ancestor, and the two Investigations games slot between Trials and Tribulations and Apollo Justice, which jumps forward seven years. Everything is now sold in four collections rather than as individual games, and Investigations 2 had no official English release until the 2024 collection.

arcs.name: The Great Ace Attorney
arcs.blurb: A Meiji-era prequel following Ryunosuke Naruhodo between Japan and London.

arcs.name: Phoenix Wright Trilogy
arcs.blurb: The original three games establishing Phoenix, Maya and Edgeworth.

arcs.name: Investigations
arcs.blurb: Two spin-offs where Miles Edgeworth works crime scenes instead of courtrooms.

arcs.name: Apollo Justice Era
arcs.blurb: The later trilogy handing the series to Apollo Justice and Athena Cykes.

name: Alan Wake / Remedy Connected Universe
scope: The games Remedy has confirmed share a universe: Alan Wake, Alan Wake's American Nightmare, Control and Alan Wake 2. The co-op shooter FBC: Firebreak is set in the same building but carries no campaign and is excluded. Max Payne and Quantum Break are adjacent at most and are not listed.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. The trap is that the connection runs through downloadable content: Control's AWE expansion is the bridge into Alan Wake 2, and Alan Wake 2 opens assuming you have seen it. Alan Wake 2 also cuts between two protagonists in different years, and the Alex Casey character is a deliberate nod to Max Payne without making that series part of this one.

games.title: Alan Wake
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Bright Falls, the Dark Presence and the manuscript pages that rewrite reality. The Remastered version includes both original DLC episodes, The Signal and The Writer, which sit right after the main story and set up where Alan spends the next thirteen years.

editions.name: Alan Wake's American Nightmare

games.title: Control
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

editions.note: Base game; digital-only at launch.

editions.name: Alan Wake 2 Deluxe Edition
editions.note: Includes the Night Springs and The Lake House expansions, the latter tying back to Control.

name: Amnesia
scope: The four Amnesia games. The free Justine expansion is treated as part of The Dark Descent, and Frictional's Penumbra and SOMA games are excluded.
caveat: Ordered by in-universe date, which has nothing to do with release order: 1839, 1899, 1916, then 1937. Only two of the four are actually connected. The Dark Descent and Rebirth share the same orbs, the same Shadow and the same underlying history; A Machine for Pigs, made by another studio, and The Bunker are standalone stories that borrow the setting's ideas rather than continue a plot.

games.title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Castle Brennenburg in 1839, and the origin of the orbs and the Shadow that Rebirth builds on directly. The free Justine expansion is included on PC; on console the Amnesia: Collection bundles it with A Machine for Pigs.

editions.name: Amnesia: The Dark Descent
editions.note: Includes the Justine expansion; source code has since been released, so mods run well.

editions.name: Amnesia: Collection

games.title: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs

editions.name: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs

games.title: Amnesia: The Bunker
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A French bunker in 1916, standalone in plot but the most mechanically different game in the series: one semi-open map, a noise-driven monster and a generator you have to keep fuelled. Nothing carries over from the others.

name: Assassin’s Creed
scope: Mainline only. No Chronicles, no mobile entries, no Liberation or Freedom Cry standalones.
caveat: This is the tab where chronology and play order pull hardest in opposite directions. Rows are sorted by historical setting. The modern-day frame — Desmond across AC1–III, Layla across Origins–Valhalla — runs in release order and is a continuous story of its own. Recommended play order is therefore release order: AC1 → II → Brotherhood → Revelations → III → Black Flag → Rogue → Unity → Syndicate → Origins → Odyssey → Valhalla → Mirage → Shadows.

name: Atelier
scope: The four modern Atelier sub-series that form self-contained storylines: Arland, Dusk, Mysterious and Secret. The older Salburg, Gramnad and Iris games, the Nelke spin-off and Atelier Resleriana are excluded.
caveat: Atelier is organised into sub-series, and that is the only structure that matters — each one is a closed storyline in its own world, and no sub-series references another. Within a sub-series the games run in release order and carry characters forward directly, so Atelier Totori assumes Rorona and Ryza 2 assumes Ryza. Pick a sub-series, start at its first game, and ignore the rest.

arcs.name: Arland

arcs.name: Dusk
arcs.blurb: A trilogy in a world slowly running out of water and life.

arcs.name: Mysterious

arcs.name: Secret
arcs.blurb: Ryza and her friends across three summers, the series' best-selling arc.

name: Baldur's Gate
scope: The three mainline games, with Throne of Bhaal folded into the Baldur's Gate II row it expands. The interquel expansion Siege of Dragonspear, the Dark Alliance action spin-offs and Icewind Dale are excluded.
caveat: In-universe chronology follows release order, but the gap is not small: the first two games run back to back in 1368-1369 DR, while Baldur's Gate 3 is set in 1492 DR, about 120 years later, with a new cast. That gap means the third game needs no knowledge of the first two beyond a few returning immortals and place names.

games.title: Baldur's Gate
games.note: The Bhaalspawn story starts here, in the Sword Coast north of the city. The Enhanced Edition includes the Tales of the Sword Coast expansion and runs on modern resolutions; the underlying 2nd Edition AD&D rules are still unforgiving.

editions.name: Baldur's Gate
editions.note: Original release; needs community patches to run at all today.

editions.name: Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Includes Tales of the Sword Coast plus new companions; sold on console only inside the two-game Enhanced Edition bundle.

games.title: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn
games.note: Continues immediately from the first game and imports its save. The Enhanced Edition includes Throne of Bhaal, the 2001 expansion that closes the Bhaalspawn story, so it is one purchase rather than two.

editions.name: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn
editions.note: Base game; Throne of Bhaal was a separate 2001 expansion.

editions.name: Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Shadows of Amn plus Throne of Bhaal, widescreen support and extra companions.

games.title: Baldur's Gate 3
games.note: Set about 120 years after Throne of Bhaal, on 5th Edition rules, with no returning party members. It is the right starting point for anyone new: the older games' plot is background colour here, not prerequisite.

editions.name: Baldur's Gate 3
editions.note: One release, patched substantially since launch; the Deluxe edition adds cosmetics and a soundtrack.

name: Batman: Arkham
scope: The four mainline Rocksteady and WB Montréal games. No Blackgate, Arkham VR, Shadow, or Suicide Squad.
caveat: Origins is a prequel released third, and it is the one entry where chronology and play order genuinely disagree. It leans on relationships that Asylum and City establish and lands flat as a first game. Recommended play order is Asylum → City → Origins → Knight, or simply Asylum → City → Knight with Origins dropped.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Origins
games.note: Different studio (WB Games Montréal). Chronologically first, but written for players who already know the others. Multiplayer servers are long dead and some save-corruption bugs were never fixed.

editions.name: Batman: Arkham Origins
editions.note: Base game; Cold, Cold Heart story DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Adds the Cold, Cold Heart story DLC and all season pass content.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
games.note: Game of the Year Edition on PC. The Return to Arkham remaster is console-only and generally considered a downgrade — the 2009 PC build is the better version.

editions.name: Batman: Arkham Asylum
editions.note: Original release; PS3 added a playable Joker challenge exclusive.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds all challenge maps and 3D mode; story was already complete.

editions.name: Batman: Return to Arkham
editions.note: Unreal 4 remaster of Asylum and City with DLC; uneven performance.

games.title: Batman: Arkham City
games.note: Game of the Year Edition. Direct sequel to Asylum and the peak of the series.

editions.name: Batman: Arkham City
editions.note: Original release; Harley Quinn's Revenge came later as paid DLC.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds Harley Quinn's Revenge plus Catwoman, skins and challenge packs.

editions.name: Armored Edition
editions.note: Wii U rework with GamePad gadgets and armored suits; weaker visuals.

editions.name: Batman: Return to Arkham
editions.note: Remaster bundling Asylum and City with all DLC; performance is uneven.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Knight
games.note: Premium / GOTY Edition. The 2015 PC launch was pulled from sale and rebuilt — it runs fine now, but it is still a 4GB-VRAM-era build. Heavy on the Batmobile.

editions.name: Batman: Arkham Knight
editions.note: Base game only; the PC launch was pulled from sale for months.

editions.name: Premium Edition
editions.note: Base game plus the season pass, bought before all DLC had shipped.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Everything included: Season of Infamy, all story DLC and every pack.

editions.name: Batman: Arkham Collection
editions.note: Trilogy bundle; console version uses the weaker Return to Arkham ports.

name: Bayonetta
scope: The three numbered PlatinumGames action titles plus the prequel Bayonetta Origins. The Bayonetta: Bloody Fate anime film and crossover appearances in other games are excluded.
caveat: The three numbered games run in release order, one straight line. The exception is Bayonetta Origins, released last but set centuries before the first game. Bayonetta 2 opens with a long detour into the past and Bayonetta 3 moves between parallel worlds, but both sit after the first game on the main timeline.

games.title: Bayonetta Origins: Cereza and the Lost Demon
games.version: Bayonetta Origins: Cereza and the Lost Demon
games.query: Bayonetta Origins Cereza and the Lost Demon
games.note: A prequel about Cereza as a child, long before the events of the first game. It is a storybook-styled puzzle adventure rather than an action game, and nothing in the numbered trilogy requires it.

editions.name: Bayonetta Origins: Cereza and the Lost Demon
editions.note: The only release; runs on Switch 2 through backward compatibility.

games.title: Bayonetta
games.note: The start of the story and the only entry with a good version outside Nintendo hardware. The PC port runs at uncapped frame rates and is the best-performing version of the game.

editions.name: Bayonetta
editions.note: The PS3 version has significant frame-rate problems.

editions.name: Bayonetta (PC)
editions.note: 4K support, uncapped frame rate, cheapest version.

editions.name: Bayonetta (Switch)
editions.note: Portable version; sold separately from Bayonetta 2.

games.title: Bayonetta 2
games.note: Set shortly after the first game and built on knowing who Jeanne and Rodin are. Much of it takes place five hundred years in the past, but the framing story follows directly from Bayonetta.

editions.name: Bayonetta 2
editions.note: Original release; the retail copy bundled the first game.

editions.name: Bayonetta 2 (Switch)
editions.note: Higher resolution port with a download code for Bayonetta 1 in the physical edition.

games.title: Bayonetta 3
games.note: Follows Bayonetta 2 and resolves the trilogy, with an ending that reframes what came before. Introduces Viola, who leads the next thread; a different voice actor plays Bayonetta here.

editions.name: Bayonetta 3
editions.note: The only release; the Trinity Masquerade edition adds an art book.

name: BioShock
scope: The three mainline games and their story DLC; the unreleased next entry and the mobile port of the first game are excluded.
caveat: In-universe order is the reverse of what most people play. Infinite is set in 1912, the first two games in 1960 and 1968, but Infinite's Burial at Sea DLC and its ending only land if you have already played Rapture. The listed order is chronological; the recommended play order is BioShock, BioShock 2, then Infinite.

arcs.name: Columbia
arcs.blurb: Booker DeWitt in the floating city of Columbia, 1912.

arcs.name: Rapture
arcs.blurb: The undersea city built by Andrew Ryan and what is left of it by 1960.

games.title: BioShock Infinite
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Chronologically first at 1912, but written to be played last: its Burial at Sea DLC is set in Rapture in 1958 and connects the two cities directly. Standalone otherwise.

editions.name: BioShock Infinite
editions.note: Base game; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: BioShock Infinite: The Complete Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Adds Clash in the Clouds and both Burial at Sea episodes; also inside BioShock: The Collection.

games.title: BioShock
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Rapture in 1960, and the entry point for the whole series. The remaster is the default, though some PC players prefer the original 2007 build, which is still bundled on Steam.

editions.name: BioShock
editions.note: Original release; still included alongside the remaster on PC.

editions.name: BioShock Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Higher-resolution art and the developer commentary; part of BioShock: The Collection.

games.title: BioShock 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set eight years after the first game, back in Rapture as a Big Daddy. Its Minerva's Den DLC is a self-contained story that is the best-regarded part of the game.

editions.name: BioShock 2
editions.note: Original release; had a multiplayer mode later dropped.

editions.name: BioShock 2 Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Single-player only, with Minerva's Den included; part of BioShock: The Collection.

name: Borderlands
scope: The four numbered games, The Pre-Sequel, both Telltale-style adventure games and the Tiny Tina's Wonderlands spin-off; the mobile card game and the film are outside scope.
caveat: Mostly release order, with one inversion: The Pre-Sequel came out after Borderlands 2 but is set between the first two games. It is framed as a story being told to the Crimson Raiders after Borderlands 2, so its bookends sit later than its body. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is a spin-off in a tabletop fantasy setting and only touches the timeline through its framing.

games.title: Borderlands
games.version: Borderlands: Game of the Year Enhanced
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced
games.note: The first trip to Pandora. Its writing and quest design are much thinner than what follows, so it is skippable if you would rather start with Borderlands 2. The Enhanced version adds a minimap and modern matchmaking.

editions.name: Borderlands
editions.note: Original release; no minimap, four DLC packs sold separately.

editions.name: Borderlands: Game of the Year Enhanced
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: All four DLCs, quality-of-life changes and higher resolution art.

games.title: Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set between the first two games, on Pandora's moon, and it explains how Handsome Jack became Borderlands 2's villain. Playing it after Borderlands 2 costs you nothing and arguably reads better that way.

editions.name: Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Borderlands: The Handsome Collection
editions.platforms: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Bundles The Pre-Sequel and Borderlands 2 with all DLC; the PC equivalent is the standalone listing with its season pass.

games.title: Borderlands 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The best entry point: it stands on its own and is where the series' characters and tone settled. Its DLC campaigns, particularly Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, matter to later games.

editions.name: Borderlands 2
editions.note: Base game; large DLC catalogue sold separately.

editions.name: Borderlands 2: Game of the Year Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: All campaign DLC included; also inside The Handsome Collection.

games.title: Tales from the Borderlands
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: An adventure game rather than a shooter, set after Borderlands 2 with Rhys and Fiona, both of whom turn up again in Borderlands 3. It was delisted for a stretch after Telltale closed and returned to sale in 2021.

editions.name: Tales from the Borderlands
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Original episodic release.

editions.name: Tales from the Borderlands
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Re-release with all five episodes in one purchase.

games.title: Borderlands 3
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Follows on from Borderlands 2 and Tales, and leaves Pandora for several planets. Expects you to know the returning cast, so it is a poor first game despite being the newest of the trilogy at the time.

editions.name: Borderlands 3
editions.note: Base game; Epic-exclusive on PC for six months.

editions.name: Borderlands 3: Ultimate Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Both season passes and all campaign add-ons included.

games.title: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands
games.version: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Chaotic Great Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series

editions.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game; Epic-exclusive on PC at launch.

editions.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Chaotic Great Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Includes the season pass and post-launch dungeon content.

games.title: New Tales from the Borderlands
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: A separate adventure game with a new cast, set shortly after Borderlands 3 and made without Telltale. It was poorly received and nothing later builds on it.

editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Only version; sold as a complete five-episode story.

games.title: Borderlands 4
games.note: The latest point on the timeline, set on the new planet Kairos after Borderlands 3. It picks up threads from the previous game's ending rather than starting clean.

editions.name: Borderlands 4
editions.note: Deluxe and Super Deluxe listings add cosmetic packs and the post-launch add-ons.

name: Castlevania
scope: The story-load-bearing entries of the main Konami continuity, ordered by the in-universe year each is set. The Lords of Shadow reboot trilogy is a separate continuity and is excluded, as are Judgment, the mobile games and the several entries whose events later games ignore.
caveat: Konami dates almost every game to a specific year, so an in-universe order exists and looks nothing like release order: the 2003 prequel Lament of Innocence opens the timeline in 1094 while the 1986 original sits in 1691. Games are spaced decades or centuries apart and rarely share a protagonist, so playing chronologically costs little.

arcs.name: Belmont Line
arcs.blurb: Nine centuries of the Belmont clan and its allies against Dracula's recurring resurrections.

arcs.name: Sorrow Arc
arcs.blurb: A 21st-century pair of games about Soma Cruz, a schoolboy who is Dracula's reincarnation.

games.title: Castlevania: Lament of Innocence
games.note: Set in 1094 and the earliest point on the timeline: how Leon Belmont came by the Vampire Killer whip and how Mathias became Dracula. Never rereleased in any collection, which makes it the hardest chronological starting point to obtain.

editions.name: Castlevania: Lament of Innocence
editions.note: The only version; PS2 disc or emulation.

games.title: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse
games.note: Set in 1476, following Trevor Belmont and introducing Alucard and Sypha, both of whom matter to later games. Branching stages and three recruitable companions make it the most substantial of the NES entries.

editions.name: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse
editions.note: Original release; the Japanese version has a superior sound chip.

editions.name: Castlevania Anniversary Collection
editions.note: Eight games with save states; includes both regional versions of this one.

games.title: Castlevania
games.note: Set in 1691 with Simon Belmont, two centuries after Dracula's Curse. Short and stiff by modern standards, and later games recap what happens here.

editions.name: Castlevania
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Castlevania Anniversary Collection
editions.note: Included in the eight-game bundle.

games.title: Castlevania: Rondo of Blood
games.note: Set in 1792 with Richter Belmont, and the direct prologue to Symphony of the Night; its ending determines what Symphony opens with. Japan-only for fifteen years, and still awkward to buy outside the PlayStation Requiem bundle.

editions.name: Akumajo Dracula X: Chi no Rondo
editions.note: Japan-only original.

editions.name: Castlevania: The Dracula X Chronicles
editions.note: 3D remake that also unlocks the original and Symphony of the Night.

editions.name: Castlevania Requiem
editions.note: Bundles Rondo of Blood and Symphony of the Night; PlayStation only.

games.title: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night
games.note: Set in 1797, five years after Rondo of Blood, with Alucard as the lead. The game that turned the series into an exploration format, and the usual recommendation for a first Castlevania despite sitting mid-timeline.

editions.name: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night
editions.note: Original release; the Saturn port is worse.

editions.name: Castlevania Requiem
editions.note: Paired with Rondo of Blood, which its opening assumes you have played.

games.title: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set in the early 1800s, when the Belmont clan has vanished and an order of researchers takes over the job. Harder than the other exploration entries and structured around discrete areas rather than one castle.

editions.name: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Bundles the three DS games with rewind and a save-anywhere option.

games.title: Castlevania: Bloodlines
games.note: Set in 1917 across Europe rather than a single castle, following John Morris, a descendant of the Belmont line. Portrait of Ruin picks up his family's story a generation later.

editions.name: Castlevania: Bloodlines
editions.note: Original; released as Castlevania: The New Generation in Europe.

editions.name: Castlevania Anniversary Collection
editions.note: Included in the eight-game bundle.

games.title: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set in 1944 and a direct follow-up to Bloodlines, with John Morris's son Jonathan as one of two playable leads. The last game on the timeline before the two-century jump to the Sorrow games.

editions.name: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Included in the three-game bundle.

games.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
games.note: Set in 2035, the furthest point on the timeline, and the only entry that requires knowing the ending of Symphony of the Night to land properly. Introduces Soma Cruz and the soul-absorption system the sequel expands.

editions.name: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Castlevania Advance Collection
editions.note: Four games with rewind, save states and a music player.

games.title: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: A direct sequel set a year after Aria of Sorrow and the only game in the series to continue a protagonist's story immediately. The collection replaces the DS touchscreen seal-drawing with a button-based alternative.

editions.name: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow
editions.note: Original release; boss kills required drawing magic seals on the touchscreen.

editions.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Included in the three-game bundle with reworked seal controls.

name: Chrono
scope: Chrono Trigger, the text adventure Radical Dreamers and Chrono Cross. There is nothing else in the series.
caveat: Chrono Trigger moves through several eras but is one self-contained story. Radical Dreamers and Chrono Cross are both sequels set a couple of decades after it, and they tell overlapping versions of the same events — Chrono Cross reworks the Radical Dreamers material and supersedes it, so playing Radical Dreamers first spoils parts of Cross rather than preparing you for it. Cross also treats Chrono Trigger's ending in a way many players find hostile, and it will not make sense without it.

games.title: Chrono Trigger
games.note: Complete on its own and the only required entry. The Steam version launched as a poor mobile port and has since been patched back into shape; the DS version adds two dungeons and a better translation but needs a cartridge.

editions.name: Chrono Trigger
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Chrono Trigger (DS)
editions.note: New translation, extra dungeons and an arena; cartridge only.

editions.name: Chrono Trigger (PC)
editions.note: Contains the DS extras; heavily patched after a bad launch.

games.query: Chrono Cross The Radical Dreamers Edition
games.note: A short illustrated text adventure, Japan-only on the Satellaview until 2022. It covers ground Chrono Cross later retells differently, so it works better as an epilogue than a prologue.

editions.name: Radical Dreamers
editions.note: Japan-only broadcast release; no standalone English version.

editions.name: Chrono Cross: The Radical Dreamers Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

editions.name: Chrono Cross
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Chrono Cross: The Radical Dreamers Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

name: Command & Conquer
scope: The Tiberium and Red Alert games and their expansions. Command & Conquer: Generals and its Zero Hour expansion are a separate continuity with no link to either saga, and the mobile titles Rivals and Tiberium Alliances are excluded.
caveat: Two sagas that are alternate timelines rather than one sequence. Red Alert began as a prequel: its Allied ending was originally meant to lead into the first Command & Conquer. From Red Alert 2 onward the two split for good, and Red Alert 3 splits again when the Soviets change history a second time. Within each saga the games run in release order.

arcs.name: Red Alert Saga
arcs.blurb: An alternate twentieth century where Einstein removes Hitler and the Soviet Union invades Europe instead.

arcs.name: Tiberium Saga
arcs.blurb: GDI against Kane's Brotherhood of Nod over the alien mineral Tiberium, from the 1990s to 2062.

games.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert
games.note: Set in an alternate 1946 and the earliest point in either saga. The 2020 Remastered Collection rebuilds it at high resolution with both expansions, working online play and the original cutscenes, and is the only version worth buying.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert
editions.note: Original release; hard to run without community tools.

editions.name: Command & Conquer Remastered Collection
editions.note: Red Alert and Tiberian Dawn with all expansion missions, remastered art and a map editor.

games.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2
games.note: Set in the 1970s of the Red Alert timeline, and the point where the saga stops feeding into the Tiberium games. Its Yuri's Revenge expansion continues immediately from its ending and is part of the same purchase.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2
editions.note: Original release; needs community patches on modern Windows.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: The Ultimate Collection
editions.note: Bundles the non-remastered games including Yuri's Revenge; sold on EA App and Steam.

games.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3
games.note: Opens with the Soviets travelling back to kill Einstein, which rewrites the timeline again and adds the Empire of the Rising Sun. Its co-op-structured campaign and the Uprising expansion are the last entries in this saga.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3
editions.note: Console versions cut the co-op commander system down.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: The Ultimate Collection
editions.note: Includes Red Alert 3 and the standalone Uprising expansion.

games.title: Command & Conquer
games.note: Retroactively called Tiberian Dawn, and the start of the Kane storyline. Bundled with Red Alert in the Remastered Collection, so one purchase covers the first game of each saga.

editions.name: Command & Conquer
editions.note: Original release, with the Covert Operations expansion sold separately.

editions.name: Command & Conquer Remastered Collection

games.title: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun
games.note: Set in 2030, thirty years after the first game, with Tiberium having reshaped the planet. The Firestorm expansion continues directly from it and is included in the same collection.

editions.name: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun

editions.name: Command & Conquer: The Ultimate Collection

games.title: Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars

editions.name: Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars

editions.name: Command & Conquer: The Ultimate Collection

editions.name: Command & Conquer 4: Tiberian Twilight
editions.note: Only version; included in the Ultimate Collection.

name: Danganronpa
scope: The three main games plus the action spin-off Ultra Despair Girls. The board-game spin-off Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp and the anime series are excluded.
caveat: Release order is the correct play order, but it is not quite chronological order: Ultra Despair Girls runs at the same time as Goodbye Despair rather than after it, and playing it before Goodbye Despair gives away that game's central reveal. Every entry spoils the one before it structurally — these are mystery games whose whole appeal is not knowing — so there is no safe way to start in the middle. V3 has a new cast and a new setting, but its ending depends entirely on you having played the first two.

games.title: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc
games.note: The only sensible starting point. On Switch it is sold inside Danganronpa Decadence, which bundles the three main games; on PC and PS4 it is sold separately.

editions.name: Danganronpa: Kibou no Gakuen to Zetsubou no Koukousei
editions.note: Japan-only original.

editions.name: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc
editions.note: First English release; later ports are the same game with control changes.

games.title: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair
games.note: A direct sequel with a new cast that resolves the first game's larger mystery. Its final chapter is unreadable without Trigger Happy Havoc.

editions.name: Super Danganronpa 2
editions.note: Japan-only original.

editions.name: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair
editions.note: First English release; included in Danganronpa Decadence on Switch.

games.title: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls
games.version: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls
games.query: Danganronpa Another Episode Ultra Despair Girls
games.note: A third-person shooter rather than a mystery, running concurrently with Goodbye Despair and following a survivor of the first game. It fills in background for the third game but is not required, and it was left out of Danganronpa Decadence.

editions.name: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls
editions.note: The only versions still sold; no Switch release.

games.title: Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony
games.note: A new cast and a clean setup that looks like a fresh start, then spends its ending arguing with the two games before it. Last in the series and the last one to play.

editions.name: Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony
editions.note: Switch version arrived in 2021 inside Danganronpa Decadence.

name: Dark Souls
scope: The three Dark Souls games and their expansions. Demon's Souls, Bloodborne, Sekiro and Elden Ring are separate series by the same studio and are not part of this chronology.
caveat: The timeline is cyclical rather than linear: each game takes place in a later turn of the same repeating age of fire and dark, and the series is deliberately vague about how much time passes. Dark Souls II is the loosest fit and barely references the first game. Playing in release order works, and no game requires the previous one.

games.title: Dark Souls
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Lordran, the first turn of the cycle, and the entry point. The Remastered version replaced the delisted Prepare to Die Edition and fixed that release's frame rate and netcode problems; the Artorias of the Abyss content is included.

editions.name: Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition
editions.note: Delisted PC version; needed community fixes to run properly.

editions.name: Dark Souls: Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: 60fps, reworked online, DLC included.

games.title: Dark Souls II
games.version: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Dark Souls II Scholar of the First Sin
games.note: Set in Drangleic an unspecified long time after the first game, with a different development team and a noticeably different feel. Scholar of the First Sin is a rebuilt version with all three DLCs and rearranged enemy placement, not just a patch.

editions.name: Dark Souls II
editions.note: Original release; a separate game from Scholar, with different enemy layouts.

editions.name: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: All DLC, revised encounter design and a newer engine build.

games.title: Dark Souls III
games.version: Dark Souls III: The Fire Fades Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Dark Souls III The Fire Fades Edition
games.note: The last turn of the cycle, with the fire nearly out, and the game that closes out the first game's threads most directly. Faster and more forgiving than the first two, which makes it a reasonable alternative starting point.

editions.name: Dark Souls III
editions.note: Base game; two DLCs sold as a season pass.

editions.name: Dark Souls III: The Fire Fades Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Includes Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City.

name: Darksiders
scope: The four games: Darksiders, Darksiders II, Darksiders III and the prequel Darksiders Genesis. Each is listed in its current definitive version rather than its original release.
caveat: This is the interesting case: the sequels are not sequels. Genesis is a straight prequel set before the apocalypse, but Darksiders II and III both run in parallel with the first game rather than after it, each following a different Horseman through the same century, and all three converge on the same moment at the end of Darksiders. The order below sorts them by where each story starts; release order works just as well, and no ordering removes the overlap.

games.title: Darksiders Genesis
games.note: A prequel with War and Strife in Hell, before the apocalypse and before anything the other three games deal with. It is an isometric action game rather than a Zelda-style adventure, so it plays nothing like the rest.

editions.name: Darksiders Genesis
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Switch / Stadia
editions.note: Only version; supports two-player co-op.

games.title: Darksiders
games.note: War is blamed for the early apocalypse, held by the Charred Council, then returned to a ruined Earth a century later. Its opening sets up the situation the other two games are reacting to, and its climax is where all three storylines meet.

editions.name: Darksiders
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Darksiders Warmastered Edition
editions.note: Higher resolution and framerate, with reworked textures.

games.title: Darksiders II
games.note: Death setting out to clear War's name, which begins after War's trial and runs alongside the first game rather than after it. The longest entry by some distance, with loot and skill trees the others do not have.

editions.name: Darksiders II
editions.note: Original release; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition
editions.note: All DLC included, rebalanced loot and reworked lighting.

games.title: Darksiders III
games.note: Fury hunting the Seven Deadly Sins on Earth, again concurrent with the first two games, with an epilogue that lands right at the end of Darksiders. Built more like a Souls game than its predecessors, which divided people.

editions.name: Darksiders III
editions.note: Base game.

editions.name: Darksiders III Blades & Whip Edition
editions.note: Bundles both story DLCs, Keepers of the Void and The Crucible.

name: Dead Island
scope: The two Techland games and the 2023 sequel by Dambuster Studios. The third-person spin-off Escape Dead Island and the free-to-play Dead Island: Epidemic are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. Riptide begins the moment the first game ends, with the same four survivors, so the two are effectively one story split in half. Dead Island 2 moves to California with an entirely new cast years later and only nods back at the earlier outbreak.

games.title: Dead Island
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The outbreak on the resort island of Banoi and the introduction of the four immune survivors. The Definitive Edition rebuilds the lighting and rebalances combat, and comes bundled with Riptide.

editions.name: Dead Island
editions.note: Original release; buggy at launch.

editions.name: Dead Island Definitive Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Remastered versions of both games plus all their DLC in one purchase.

games.title: Dead Island: Riptide
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Starts as the first game's escape fails, moving the same characters to the neighbouring island of Palanai. Close enough to a standalone expansion that it can feel like more of the first game rather than a sequel.

editions.name: Dead Island: Riptide
editions.note: Original release; save transfer from the first game was supported.

editions.name: Dead Island Definitive Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Bundled with the first game; not worth buying separately.

games.title: Dead Island 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set in a quarantined Los Angeles with six new playable survivors, and connected to the earlier games only by the virus and a few references. Spent nearly a decade in development across three studios before release.

editions.name: Dead Island 2
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Launched as an Epic exclusive on PC and reached Steam a year later; two story expansions are sold separately.

name: Dead Rising
scope: The four numbered games plus the two downloadable side stories, Case Zero and Case West. Dead Rising 2: Off the Record is excluded because it is an explicitly non-canon retelling of Dead Rising 2 with Frank West swapped in for Chuck Greene.
caveat: Chronology matches release order, with the two Case episodes slotting in around Dead Rising 2 exactly where they were released. The awkward part is availability: both Case episodes were Xbox 360 digital exclusives and became unbuyable when that store closed, so the timeline has a gap nothing fills.

games.title: Dead Rising
games.note: Frank West's three days in the Willamette mall, and the outbreak the rest of the series traces back to. The 2024 remaster rebuilds the game in RE Engine, adds full voice acting and lets you move while aiming, which the original did not.

editions.name: Dead Rising
editions.note: Original release; unreadably small text on standard-definition sets.

editions.name: Dead Rising (2016)
editions.note: Straight port at 60fps; kept the original's stiff controls.

editions.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster
editions.note: RE Engine rebuild with reworked controls and an autosave option.

games.title: Dead Rising: Case Zero
games.note: A short prologue introducing Chuck Greene and his daughter, set a couple of years before Dead Rising 2. It was an Xbox 360 digital exclusive and is no longer purchasable, though owners can still redownload it.

editions.name: Dead Rising: Case Zero
editions.note: The only version; delisted with the Xbox 360 store closure.

games.title: Dead Rising 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set five years after the first game, in Fortune City, with Chuck as the lead and Frank absent. Introduces combo weapons, which every later entry keeps.

editions.name: Dead Rising 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Dead Rising 2 (2016)
editions.note: 60fps port; the version still on sale.

games.title: Dead Rising: Case West
games.note: An epilogue to Dead Rising 2 in which Frank and Chuck work together, and the first time the two protagonists meet. Like Case Zero it stayed on Xbox 360 and is now unbuyable.

editions.name: Dead Rising: Case West
editions.note: The only version; requires Dead Rising 2 to have been meaningful at launch.

games.title: Dead Rising 3
games.note: Set ten years after Dead Rising 2 in Los Perdidos, with a new lead, Nick Ramos; Chuck appears but Frank does not. Never released on PlayStation.

editions.name: Dead Rising 3
editions.note: Launch exclusive; capped at 30fps.

editions.name: Dead Rising 3 Apocalypse Edition
editions.note: Includes all four Untold Stories episodes and runs uncapped on PC.

games.title: Dead Rising 4
games.note: Brings Frank West back to Willamette sixteen years after the first game, with a different voice actor and a lighter tone. It drops the timer that defined the earlier games, which is the main reason opinion on it is split.

editions.name: Dead Rising 4
editions.note: Launch version; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package
editions.note: Bundles all DLC including the Capcom Heroes mode.

name: Dead Space
scope: The three numbered games plus the on-rails prequel Extraction. The mobile Dead Space, the browser game Ignition and the animated films are excluded.
caveat: The three numbered games run in release order with a few years between each. The only reordering is Extraction, released after the first game but set immediately before it. The 2023 remake replaces the 2008 original outright and folds in material the original left in text logs.

games.title: Dead Space: Extraction
games.note: A prequel covering the outbreak on Aegis VII and the colony evacuation, ending just as the first game begins. It is a light-gun style rail shooter, not a survival horror game, and the remake covers the same events well enough that it is optional.

editions.name: Dead Space: Extraction
editions.note: Original release, built for the Wii Remote.

editions.name: Dead Space: Extraction (PS3)
editions.note: Bundled with the Dead Space 2 Limited Edition; supports PlayStation Move.

games.title: Dead Space
games.note: Isaac Clarke's first trip aboard the USG Ishimura and the start of the story. The remake gives Isaac a voice, removes loading screens and restores a subplot the original cut, so it is the version to play.

editions.name: Dead Space
editions.note: Original release; the PC version has mouse acceleration problems.

editions.name: Dead Space (2023)
editions.note: Rebuilt in the Frostbite engine with a seamless ship and a voiced Isaac.

games.title: Dead Space 2
games.note: Set three years after the first game, on the Sprawl, and the direct continuation of Isaac's story. No remaster exists, so the 2011 PC build is the best available version.

editions.name: Dead Space 2
editions.note: The only version; also playable on Xbox consoles through backward compatibility.

games.title: Dead Space 3
games.note: Closes Isaac's arc and explains the origin of the Markers, though it trades horror for co-op action and weapon crafting. The Awakened DLC contains the actual ending of the series and is sold separately.

editions.name: Dead Space 3
editions.note: Base game; ends on an ambiguous note without the DLC.

editions.name: Dead Space 3 with Awakened
editions.note: Adds the epilogue chapter that the series never followed up on.

name: Death Stranding
scope: The two Kojima Productions games: Death Stranding and Death Stranding 2: On the Beach. Mobile and Mac ports of the first game are the same content and are not listed separately.
caveat: Two games, chronological order equals release order. Death Stranding 2 opens about eleven months after the first game's ending and does not recap it, so playing them out of order will not work.

games.title: Death Stranding
games.note: Sam Bridges reconnecting a broken America, and the whole explanation of BTs, chiral matter and the Beach that the sequel assumes you already have. The Director's Cut adds missions and equipment but does not change the ending.

editions.name: Death Stranding
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Death Stranding
editions.note: PC port with photo mode and higher framerates.

editions.name: Death Stranding Director's Cut
editions.note: Extra missions, weapons and a firing range; the default version now.

games.title: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach
games.note: Picks up roughly eleven months later, moving from America to Mexico and Australia. It leans hard on characters and reveals from the first game with minimal reintroduction.

editions.name: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach
editions.note: PS5 release; a PC version has not shipped.

name: Destiny
scope: The two games and their expansions; the mobile companion apps and the tabletop spin-offs are outside scope.
caveat: Chronology matches release order, but the practical problem is access rather than order. Destiny 1 never came to PC and stopped receiving content in 2017. Destiny 2's story is split across paid expansions bought separately, and Bungie removed several campaigns from the game in 2020, including the original Red War campaign, so a new player cannot play the story straight through in the order it was written.

games.title: Destiny
games.platform: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Console-only and never ported to PC. Its servers are still up but it receives no updates, and Destiny 2 reintroduces most of what matters, so it is background rather than required.

editions.name: Destiny
editions.note: Base game; its story was widely criticised at launch.

editions.name: Destiny: The Collection
editions.platforms: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game with The Dark Below, House of Wolves, The Taken King and Rise of Iron; digital availability has been inconsistent.

games.title: Destiny 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Free to download, but the campaigns are separate purchases and the base free content is not the original 2017 story, which was removed. Expect to buy expansions individually; The Witch Queen and The Final Shape are the ones most often pointed to as the story high points.

editions.name: Destiny 2
editions.note: Original paid release with the Red War campaign, since removed from the game.

editions.name: Destiny 2: New Light
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The free-to-play base client; expansions are bought on top of it.

name: Deus Ex
scope: The four main games plus the spin-off Deus Ex: The Fall; the Deus Ex Go mobile puzzle game and the VR spin-off Deus Ex: Mankind Divided - Breach are excluded.
caveat: This series' chronology is almost exactly the reverse of its release order. The 2011 and 2016 prequels are set in 2027-2029, while the 2000 original is set in 2052 and its 2003 sequel in 2072. Playing chronologically works, but the prequels were written assuming you already knew the originals' conspiracies, so a lot of their nods land differently.

arcs.name: Adam Jensen Era
arcs.blurb: The 2020s augmentation backlash, twenty-five years before the original game.

arcs.name: JC Denton Era
arcs.blurb: The mid-century collapse and the conspiracies JC Denton walks into.

games.title: Deus Ex: Human Revolution
games.version: Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut
games.query: Deus Ex Human Revolution Director's Cut
games.note: Set in 2027, the earliest point in the timeline and the most approachable way in. The Director's Cut rebuilds the original's much-criticised boss fights and folds in the Missing Link DLC.

editions.name: Deus Ex: Human Revolution
editions.note: Original release; unavoidable gun-only boss fights.

editions.name: Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut
editions.note: Reworked bosses, The Missing Link integrated into the campaign.

games.title: Deus Ex: The Fall
games.note: A mobile game ported to PC, running alongside Human Revolution with Ben Saxon rather than Jensen. Its story thread was never continued and nothing later depends on it.

editions.name: Deus Ex: The Fall
editions.note: PC port is the only version still readily sold.

games.title: Deus Ex: Mankind Divided
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Two years after Human Revolution, in a Prague under segregation law. It ends on threads that were never resolved, since the series has been dormant since.

editions.name: Deus Ex: Mankind Divided
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The Digital Deluxe listing adds the Jensen's Stories side missions, including A Criminal Past.

games.title: Deus Ex
games.version: Deus Ex: Game of the Year Edition
games.query: Deus Ex Game of the Year Edition
games.note: Set in 2052 and still the centre of the series. It is a 2000 PC game: expect to add a community patch or the free Revision mod for resolution and control fixes.

editions.name: Deus Ex
editions.note: Original release; the PS2 port cuts level geometry.

editions.name: Deus Ex: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: The standard modern purchase on GOG and Steam; mod-friendly.

games.title: Deus Ex: Invisible War
games.note: Twenty years after the original and the last point on the timeline. It was cut down for console hardware, with small levels and unified ammunition, and it is the entry most players skip.

editions.name: Deus Ex: Invisible War
editions.note: Only version; needs community fixes on modern displays.

name: Devil May Cry
scope: The five numbered Capcom games that share one continuity. DmC: Devil May Cry and its Vergil's Downfall DLC are a Ninja Theory reboot in a separate continuity and are not part of this order.
caveat: Release order and in-universe order differ in one place: Devil May Cry 3 is a prequel to the first game, so it comes first. Where Devil May Cry 2 sits has been argued for years; Capcom's own published timeline places it between 1 and 4, which is the order used here.

games.title: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A prequel showing a younger Dante and his brother Vergil, and the origin of the Devil May Cry shop. Any modern version is the Special Edition, which adds Vergil as a playable character.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening
editions.note: Original release with a widely criticised difficulty curve.

editions.name: Devil May Cry HD Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Special Edition build of DMC1-3 in one purchase.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 3 Special Edition (Switch)
editions.note: Adds free style-switching and local co-op, but is sold alone.

games.title: Devil May Cry
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Dante's job on Mallet Island and his first meeting with Trish, who carries into later games. Started life as a Resident Evil 4 prototype, which shows in the fixed camera angles.

editions.name: Devil May Cry
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Devil May Cry HD Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Higher resolution port; the same game underneath.

games.title: Devil May Cry 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The weakest entry and the one nothing later depends on; Lucia never reappears and Dante's arc is untouched by it. Its timeline position is the disputed one, and skipping it costs nothing.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 2
editions.note: Two-disc original with separate Dante and Lucia campaigns.

editions.name: Devil May Cry HD Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Bundled; not sold separately.

games.title: Devil May Cry 4
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Introduces Nero, whose story DMC5 continues directly, so it is the required setup for the current games. Special Edition adds Vergil, Trish and Lady as playable characters.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 4
editions.note: Original release; Nero and Dante only.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Three extra playable characters and rebalanced difficulty.

games.title: Devil May Cry 5
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Picks up Nero's story from 4 and closes the Dante and Vergil thread opened in 3. On PC the base game plus the Vergil DLC is equivalent to the Special Edition; on consoles the Special Edition is a separate purchase.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 5
editions.note: Base release; Vergil sold as DLC on PC.

editions.name: Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition
editions.note: Adds playable Vergil, ray tracing and a 120fps mode.

name: Diablo
scope: The four numbered games and Diablo Immortal, including their expansions; the cancelled Diablo III console spin-offs and the Hellfire expansion for the first game are excluded.
caveat: Release order and chronology agree for the numbered games. The exception is Diablo Immortal, which came out in 2022 but is set in the twenty years between Diablo II and Diablo III, filling the gap around the shattered Worldstone. Diablo IV then jumps roughly fifty years past Diablo III.

games.title: Diablo
games.note: Sixteen floors under Tristram cathedral, and the origin of the story every later game refers back to. Slow and stiff compared to what followed; the GOG re-release is the only version patched to run on modern Windows.

editions.name: Diablo
editions.note: Original release; needs compatibility work on modern systems.

editions.name: Diablo
editions.note: GOG re-release with modern Windows support and working multiplayer.

games.title: Diablo II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Follows directly from the first game's ending and is the series' high point for most players. Resurrected rebuilds the visuals over the original engine and includes the Lord of Destruction expansion, whose fifth act closes the story.

editions.name: Diablo II: Lord of Destruction
editions.note: The original with its expansion; still runs but is hard to buy now.

editions.name: Diablo II: Resurrected
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Remaster with the expansion included and a toggle back to the original graphics.

games.title: Diablo Immortal
games.note: Set between Diablo II and Diablo III, covering the fragments of the Worldstone. Built as a free-to-play mobile game with a PC client and heavy monetisation around endgame gear; nothing in Diablo III or IV requires it.

editions.name: Diablo Immortal
editions.note: Free to play; the PC and mobile versions share servers and progress.

games.title: Diablo III
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Twenty years after Diablo II, and the story continues directly from it. The Reaper of Souls expansion is where the game's design settled after the auction house was removed, and the Eternal Collection bundles it with the Necromancer class.

editions.name: Diablo III
editions.note: Launch version with the since-removed real-money auction house.

editions.name: Diablo III: Eternal Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

games.title: Diablo IV
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: About fifty years after Diablo III and the best current entry point, since it opens with its own setup and is the actively supported game. Always online, with story expansions such as Vessel of Hatred sold separately.

editions.name: Diablo IV
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base campaign; also on Game Pass and Steam.

name: Dino Crisis
scope: The three Capcom games. The light-gun spin-off Dino Stalker and the Gun Survivor series it belongs to are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. The catch is availability rather than ordering: none of the three has had a modern console rerelease, so all of them require original hardware, backward compatibility or emulation. Dino Crisis 3 jumps centuries ahead and shares no characters with the first two.

games.title: Dino Crisis
games.note: Regina's first mission to Ibis Island and the origin of the Third Energy experiments the sequel follows up on. Built by the Resident Evil team using the same tank controls over real-time 3D backgrounds.

editions.name: Dino Crisis
editions.note: The reference version; also released on Dreamcast and PC in 2000.

editions.name: Dino Crisis (PC)
editions.note: Out of print and difficult to run on modern Windows.

games.title: Dino Crisis 2
games.note: A direct sequel with Regina returning, set after the first game's Third Energy incident. It abandons survival horror for score-driven action, which is why opinion on it splits.

editions.name: Dino Crisis 2
editions.note: The reference version; a 2003 PC port exists but is rarer.

games.title: Dino Crisis 3
games.note: Set centuries later aboard a colony ship, with an entirely new cast and no link to Regina's story. It was an original Xbox exclusive, was never ported, and is not backward compatible.

editions.name: Dino Crisis 3
editions.note: The only version; original Xbox hardware or emulation only.

name: Dishonored
scope: Both mainline games, the two Daud story expansions, and the standalone Death of the Outsider; the combat-only Dunwall City Trials DLC is excluded.
caveat: Chronology follows release order with one wrinkle: the Daud expansions run alongside the first game rather than after it, starting during Corvo's campaign and ending just before its finale. Dishonored 2 jumps fifteen years ahead and Death of the Outsider picks up months after that.

games.title: Dishonored
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Corvo Attano's revenge in plague-era Dunwall, and the entry point. The Definitive Edition bundles every DLC, so the two Daud chapters need no separate purchase.

editions.name: Dishonored
editions.note: Original release; DLC sold piecemeal.

editions.name: Dishonored: Definitive Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: All DLC included and a modest visual update.

games.title: Dishonored: The Knife of Dunwall
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Daud's side of the first game, running concurrently with Corvo's campaign. Play it after finishing the base game rather than in the middle, since it assumes you know how Dunwall's story is going.

editions.name: The Knife of Dunwall

name: Divinity
scope: The four story-relevant Larian RPGs set on Rivellon. Beyond Divinity, the Dragon Commander strategy game and the Divinity: Original Sin board game are excluded.
caveat: Release order and in-universe order are almost exactly reversed. The two Original Sin games are prequels set centuries before Divine Divinity, so the chronological run starts with the newest games and ends with the oldest. Playing in release order works fine too; the connections are thematic and mythological rather than plot-critical.

games.title: Divinity: Original Sin
games.note: Chronologically the earliest game in the series, set well before Divine Divinity, following two Source Hunters. The Enhanced Edition rewrites and fully voices the script and adds controller support; the original is effectively superseded.

editions.name: Divinity: Original Sin
editions.note: Original release; largely unvoiced and harder to recommend.

editions.name: Divinity: Original Sin - Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Full voice acting, reworked writing, new endgame; free to owners of the original.

games.title: Divinity: Original Sin 2
games.note: Set generations after the first Original Sin and still long before Divine Divinity. It stands alone, and its systems and writing make it the sensible entry point regardless of chronology.

editions.name: Divinity: Original Sin 2
editions.note: Launch version, superseded by the free Definitive update.

editions.name: Divinity: Original Sin 2 - Definitive Edition
editions.note: Rewritten third act, rebalanced combat, split-screen co-op.

games.title: Divine Divinity
games.note: The original game and the point where the Divine One's story begins, centuries after the Original Sin games. It plays like an isometric action RPG of its era, with an inventory and interface to match.

editions.name: Divine Divinity
editions.note: Only release; the GOG build is the one that runs cleanly on modern Windows.

games.title: Divinity II: Ego Draconis
games.note: The latest point on the in-universe timeline, following a Dragon Knight after Divine Divinity. The Developer's Cut is the version to buy: it bundles Ego Draconis with the Flames of Vengeance expansion in a single reworked campaign.

editions.name: Divinity II: Ego Draconis
editions.note: Base campaign, ends on a cliffhanger the expansion resolves.

editions.name: Divinity II: Developer's Cut
editions.note: Ego Draconis plus Flames of Vengeance, rebalanced, with a developer commentary mode.

name: Doom
scope: The classic id Software games and the modern Slayer trilogy; Doom 3 is excluded because it is a separate reboot continuity, as are the mobile and RPG spin-offs.
caveat: Two groups that barely connect. The classic games run in release order. The modern games run 2016, Eternal, and then The Dark Ages, which arrived last in 2025 but is a prequel set before Doom 2016. Eternal retroactively suggests its Slayer is the same marine from the 1993 game, but nothing in the classic games requires you to accept that.

arcs.name: Classic Doom
arcs.blurb: The 1990s games: a marine, a UAC facility on Mars, and the invasion that follows.

arcs.name: The Slayer
arcs.blurb: The modern reboot trilogy built around the Doom Slayer and Argent D'Nur.

games.title: Doom
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The starting point, on Mars and then Hell. The 2024 Doom + Doom II re-release is the current default: both games, add-on support, online play and a new episode in one purchase.

editions.name: Final Doom

editions.name: Doom + Doom II

games.title: Doom 64
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: A separate game rather than a port, set after Doom II with the marine returning to clear the remains of the invasion. The 2020 remaster adds a short new chapter that ties it toward Doom Eternal.

editions.name: Doom 64

editions.name: Doom 64

games.title: Doom: The Dark Ages

editions.name: Doom: The Dark Ages

name: Dragon Age
scope: The four mainline BioWare RPGs. The tie-in novels, comics, the Dragon Age: Absolution series and the mobile spin-off Dragon Age Legends are excluded.
caveat: In-universe chronology matches release order; each game runs a few years after the last, and Dragon Age II's frame story overlaps with Origins because Varric narrates events from a decade earlier. The series tracks decisions across games, so the order you play them in is also the order the choices carry.

games.title: Dragon Age: Origins
games.note: The Fifth Blight, and the origin point for choices the later games reference. The Ultimate Edition includes the Awakening expansion, which continues directly after and covers events the sequels assume you know.

editions.name: Dragon Age: Origins
editions.note: Base game without Awakening or the story DLC.

editions.name: Dragon Age: Origins - Ultimate Edition
editions.note: Base game, Awakening and all nine DLC packs; needs minor tweaks to run well on modern PCs.

games.title: Dragon Age II
games.note: Spans ten years in Kirkwall, beginning during the Blight of the first game and ending after it. The mage-templar war it triggers is the direct setup for Inquisition.

editions.name: Dragon Age II
editions.note: The only version; the Legacy and Mark of the Assassin DLC are sold separately.

editions.name: Dragon Age: Inquisition

editions.name: Dragon Age: The Veilguard
editions.note: Single release; the Deluxe edition adds cosmetics only.

name: Dragon Quest
scope: The single-player numbered entries that sit in a shared timeline or stand alone as mainline games. The MMO Dragon Quest X, the Monsters, Builders, Heroes and Treasures spin-offs, and Dragon Quest VII are excluded — VII has no continuity link to the others and no current English release outside the 3DS version.
caveat: Dragon Quest is three separate worlds plus loose ends. Only the Erdrick games are tightly linked, and their in-universe order is III, then I, then II — which is why the HD-2D remakes shipped III first. Dragon Quest XI's connection to that trilogy is a late-game reveal, so putting it first chronologically also spoils it; most people play it last despite its position here. The Zenithian games share a world and a set of artifacts but no cast, and the link between them is far looser than the Erdrick line.

arcs.name: Erdrick
arcs.blurb: The Loto bloodline across four games, told almost entirely out of order.

arcs.name: Zenithian
arcs.blurb: Three generations in one world, tied together by Zenithia and its equipment rather than by characters.

arcs.name: Standalone
arcs.blurb: Mainline entries with no continuity to each other or to the trilogies.

caveat: Chronology matches release order. The Following continues immediately from the first game's ending and its own ending is the one the sequel treats as canon, so it is not optional side content. Dying Light 2 jumps roughly fifteen years ahead to a different city with a different protagonist.

name: Fallout
scope: The mainline RPGs, Fallout Tactics and Fallout 76; the non-canon console spin-off Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel and the mobile game Fallout Shelter are excluded.
caveat: The games are grouped by coast because the two sets barely touch, and each set runs in its own chronological order. Across the whole series Fallout 76 is actually the earliest, set in 2102, even though it appears in the second group; the West Coast games run 2161 to 2281 and the other East Coast games sit in 2277 and 2287. No game requires another to make sense.

arcs.blurb: The original California games and the NCR's rise, from Vault 13 to the Mojave.

arcs.name: East Coast
arcs.blurb: Bethesda's Appalachia, Capital Wasteland and Commonwealth games.

games.title: Fallout

name: Far Cry
scope: The modern entries with any thread between them: Far Cry 3, Blood Dragon, Far Cry 4, Primal, Far Cry 5, New Dawn and Far Cry 6. Far Cry 1 and 2 are unrelated one-offs from before the series settled into this shape and are excluded, as are the Far Cry Instincts console spin-offs.
caveat: Be honest about this one: almost every Far Cry is a self-contained story in a new place with a new cast, so ordering them is mostly a formality. The one real connection is Far Cry 5 to New Dawn, which is a direct sequel set seventeen years later and spoils Far Cry 5's ending in its opening minutes. Primal sits ten thousand years before everything else, and Blood Dragon is a parody in its own fictional 2007 rather than part of the series' world.

games.title: Far Cry Primal

name: Fatal Frame
scope: The five main games, known as Project Zero in Europe. The 3DS spin-off Spirit Camera: The Cursed Memoir and the Wii U free-to-start Haunted House are excluded.
caveat: Each game is a self-contained haunting with its own cast, so release order works as playing order. The connective tissue is thin: the third game brings back survivors from the first two, which is the one place order genuinely matters. Only the fourth and fifth games have modern rereleases; the first three remain on PS2.

name: Final Fantasy
scope: Only the Final Fantasy games that genuinely share a continuity with another Final Fantasy game: the Ivalice titles, the Spira duology, the Fabula Nova Crystallis trilogy, and Final Fantasy IV with its sequel. The self-contained mainline entries (I, II, III, V, VI, IX, XI, XIV, XV, XVI) and the Tactics Advance games, which are set in a separate dream Ivalice, are excluded.
caveat: Final Fantasy is not one story — most numbered entries share only motifs, not a world. The four groups below are the exceptions. Within each group, release order and in-universe order match except in Ivalice, where Final Fantasy Tactics came out first but is set long after Final Fantasy XII. Nothing here requires having played any other Final Fantasy.

arcs.name: Final Fantasy IV

arcs.name: Spira

arcs.name: Fabula Nova Crystallis

name: Final Fantasy VII
scope: The Compilation of Final Fantasy VII: the 1997 original, its prequel Crisis Core, the sequel Dirge of Cerberus, and the Remake trilogy; the mobile titles Before Crisis and Ever Crisis are excluded, as is the film Advent Children, which is not a game.
caveat: In-universe order is almost the reverse of release order: the prequel Crisis Core came a decade after the original, and Dirge of Cerberus is the only game set after it. The Remake trilogy is a partial retelling of the 1997 game that deliberately diverges from it, so it does not replace the original on this list — Remake covers only the Midgar opening, Rebirth continues to roughly the game's midpoint, and the third part is unreleased. Advent Children sits between the original game and Dirge of Cerberus.

name: Fire Emblem
scope: The five continents where Fire Emblem tells a story across more than one game: Archanea, Jugdral, Elibe, Tellius and Fodlan. The standalone entries — Sacred Stones, Awakening, Fates, Engage and Echoes: Shadows of Valentia — are excluded, as are the Warriors and Heroes spin-offs, except where Fodlan's own musou entry belongs to its arc.
caveat: Every continent is a separate world with its own timeline; nothing crosses between them. Two of the pairings invert release order — Blazing Blade is a prequel to Binding Blade released a year later, and Thracia 776 takes place inside the gap between Genealogy of the Holy War's two generations. The larger obstacle is language: four of the ten games below have never been released in English in any form, and several of the rest are locked to dead hardware or a Nintendo Switch Online subscription.

name: Five Nights at Freddy's
scope: The eight entries that carry the main story. Ultimate Custom Night, the AR and mobile spin-offs, the Help Wanted 2 follow-up, the FNaF World RPG and the novels are excluded.
caveat: Be honest about this one: the chronology is not stated anywhere in the games. It is assembled from minigame fragments, newspaper clippings, paycheck dates and later interviews, and parts of it have been retconned by the developer more than once. Sister Location in particular has no agreed placement. The order below is the reading most of the community settles on, not a fact, and release order remains the sensible way to actually play them, since each game is built to reframe what the previous one showed.

games.title: Five Nights at Freddy's 4

games.note: Placed earliest because its minigames depict the bite that later material dates to 1983. It was originally read as 1987; the date was revised after release, which is a fair sample of how stable this timeline is.

editions.name: Five Nights at Freddy's 4

editions.name: Five Nights at Freddy's 2

name: Front Mission
scope: The five numbered strategy entries, which share one continuity built around Huffman Island and the wanzer arms industry. The third-person shooter Front Mission Evolved, the PSP spin-off Front Mission Alternative and the online games are excluded.
caveat: Each game follows a different conflict and cast in one continuous future history, and the numbering is not the timeline. Front Mission 4 is set six years after the first game but before the second, and Front Mission 5 spans fifty years, from before the first game to after the third — it is the capstone and belongs last regardless of its start date. Two of the five have never been released in English in their original form: Front Mission 2 only got out via its 2023 remake, and Front Mission 5 never has.

name: Ghost of Tsushima
scope: The two Sucker Punch games, Ghost of Tsushima and Ghost of Yotei. The co-op mode Ghost of Tsushima: Legends is a separate mythological side mode and is not treated as part of the story.
caveat: Chronology is release order, but the two games are barely connected: Tsushima is set during the 1274 Mongol invasion and Yotei is set on Ezo in the early 1600s with a different protagonist. They share a world and the idea of the Ghost, not a plot, so either one works as a first game.

games.title: Ghost of Tsushima
games.note: Jin Sakai during the Mongol landing on Tsushima in 1274. The Director's Cut is the version worth buying because it folds in the Iki Island chapter, which is set mid-story rather than after it.

games.title: Ghost of Yotei
games.note: Set around Mount Yotei in 1603, more than three centuries after Tsushima, following Atsu on a revenge hunt. It assumes nothing from the first game beyond the general idea of the Ghost.

editions.name: Ghost of Yotei
editions.note: Console-exclusive at launch; no PC version yet.

name: God of War
scope: Greek saga through Norse saga, handhelds included. Betrayal (2007, mobile) is excluded.
caveat: Ascension is chronologically first and was released second-to-last — it is also the weakest entry, and starting there is the standard mistake. Recommended play order is God of War (2005) → II → III, with the handhelds slotted where they sit, then the 2018 reboot. On PC only the two Norse games exist, and the 2018 game is written to work cold.

arcs.blurb: Kratos against Olympus, from Spartan soldier to god-killer.

arcs.name: Norse Saga

games.title: God of War: Ascension

name: Golden Sun
scope: All three Golden Sun games. There are no spin-offs and nothing has been released since 2010.
caveat: Golden Sun and The Lost Age are one game split across two cartridges: The Lost Age picks up around the first game's climax and retells part of it from the opposing party's side before continuing past it, and it can import a password or link cable save that carries over levels, items and Djinn. Playing The Lost Age alone means starting mid-plot with a cast the game never introduces. Dark Dawn is set thirty years later with the original characters' children, and ends on a cliffhanger that has never been resolved.

games.title: Golden Sun
games.note: Available only through the Game Boy Advance library on Nintendo Switch Online's Expansion Pack tier, not as a purchase. Ends abruptly because the story continues in The Lost Age.

editions.name: Golden Sun

editions.name: Golden Sun: The Lost Age (Nintendo Switch Online)

games.title: Golden Sun: Dark Dawn

name: Gothic
scope: The three Piranha Bytes games about the Nameless Hero, with Night of the Raven folded into the Gothic II row. The unrelated Gothic 3: Forsaken Gods and Arcania: Gothic 4, made by other studios, are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order and the games form one unbroken story: each begins within days of the last one's ending, with the same protagonist. Night of the Raven is an expansion that inserts a new chapter and new island into Gothic II rather than continuing after it, so it is played as part of that game, not after.

games.title: Gothic
games.note: The penal colony under the magic barrier, and the first meeting with almost every recurring character. The original control scheme is awkward by modern standards; the community SystemPack fix is close to mandatory on current Windows.

editions.name: Gothic
editions.note: Only release; the GOG build ships pre-patched for modern systems.

games.title: Gothic II
games.note: Begins immediately after the first game's ending, with the barrier down and the hero on the mainland. Buy the Gold Edition: it includes Night of the Raven, which is woven into the main campaign and raises the early difficulty noticeably.

editions.name: Gothic II
editions.note: Base game without the expansion content.

editions.name: Gothic II: Gold Edition

games.title: Gothic 3
