name: Grand Theft Auto
scope: The 3D-era games from GTA III through Vice City Stories and the HD-era games from GTA IV onward. The top-down originals GTA 1, GTA 2 and their London expansions are a third, unconnected continuity and are excluded, as are the handheld spin-offs GTA Advance and Chinatown Wars.
caveat: The two arcs below are separate continuities, not one long story: the HD era restarted everything, so a Liberty City or a character name appearing in both refers to different people and a different version of the world. Within each arc, release order and in-universe order disagree sharply. Vice City Stories shipped last in the 3D era but is set first, and GTA V opens with a 2004 prologue before jumping to 2013.

arcs.name: 3D Universe
arcs.blurb: The PS2-era continuity, from 1984 Vice City to 2001 Liberty City.

arcs.name: HD Universe
arcs.blurb: The rebooted continuity that starts with GTA IV, sharing place names but not history with the 3D era.

name: Hades
scope: The two Supergiant roguelikes: Hades and Hades II. Supergiant's unrelated earlier games are not part of this.
caveat: Two games, chronology equals release order. Hades II is a direct continuation rather than a reimagining: Melinoe is Zagreus's sister and the House of Hades has already fallen when it opens, so its premise is a spoiler for the first game. Both are roguelikes where the story unfolds over many runs, so the hour counts below are for reaching the credits, not for seeing everything.

games.title: Hades
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

editions.name: Hades II

name: Half-Life
scope: Mainline plus the two Gearbox expansions and Alyx. Black Mesa is a fan remake and is not counted here.
caveat: Alyx is the trap. It is set roughly five years before Half-Life 2, so it sorts here — but its final scene is a direct continuation of Episode Two’s cliffhanger and spoils it outright. Play it last. There is still no Half-Life 3 as of August 2026.

name: Halo
scope: Mainline plus Reach and ODST. No Halo Wars, no Spartan Assault, no multiplayer-only releases.
caveat: Reach is a prequel that sorts first and also works as an entry point — a rare case where chronology and a good first game agree. ODST runs concurrently with Halo 2’s Earth arc rather than after it. The real problem with this tab is Halo 5: it has never released on PC and is not in the Master Chief Collection, so a PC-only playthrough has a hole in it right before Infinite.

name: Hitman

games.note: Ends the original continuity with 47 on the run after Blood Money. The most linear game in the series and the most divisive; on console it is only sold inside the HD Enhanced Collection listed on the Blood Money row.

editions.name: Hitman: Absolution
editions.note: Original release; still sold standalone on PC.

editions.name: Hitman HD Enhanced Collection
editions.note: Remastered alongside Blood Money; one purchase covers both.

games.title: Hitman
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Restarts 47's story and is where the reboot trilogy begins. Since 2023 its levels load inside the World of Assassination client alongside the other two games, so this single purchase covers all three; the separately listed 2016 and 2018 releases are legacy storefront entries.

editions.name: Hitman
editions.note: Episodic release, later collected as the Game of the Year Edition.

editions.name: Hitman World of Assassination
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: All three reboot games plus Freelancer mode in one package and one client.

games.title: Hitman 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Continues the Providence plot immediately after the 2016 game. Not sold on its own any more in a meaningful sense: its locations are part of World of Assassination, listed on the previous row.

editions.name: Hitman 2
editions.note: Standalone release, now folded into World of Assassination.

editions.name: Hitman World of Assassination
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The current way to own and play these levels.

games.title: Hitman 3
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Closes the reboot trilogy and is the client the other two games now run inside. Also the home of Freelancer, the roguelike campaign mode added in 2023.

editions.name: Hitman 3
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch (cloud)
editions.note: Launch release; renamed and expanded into World of Assassination.

editions.name: Hitman World of Assassination
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The renamed and rebundled version of this game, including the first two.

name: Hollow Knight
scope: The two Team Cherry games: Hollow Knight, including its four free content packs, and Hollow Knight: Silksong.
caveat: Release order is settled; in-universe order is not. Silksong follows Hornet after she is captured and taken to Pharloom, but Team Cherry has never stated whether that happens before, during or after the events of Hollow Knight, and the games are set in different kingdoms with almost no shared cast. The listing below is release order, which is the safe way to play them, not a confirmed chronology.

games.title: Hollow Knight
games.note: Hallownest, the Infection and the Vessels. All four expansion packs are free and already included, so there is no edition to hunt for; the console release is labelled Voidheart Edition and contains the same content.

editions.name: Hollow Knight
editions.note: All four content packs added free; the PC version got them first.

editions.name: Hollow Knight: Voidheart Edition
editions.note: Console version with the same content under a different name.

games.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch / Switch 2
games.note: Hornet in the kingdom of Pharloom, playing faster and harder than the first game. It began as DLC before becoming a full sequel, and it explains its own world from scratch, so it is playable without Hollow Knight even if the connections read better afterwards.

editions.name: Hollow Knight: Silksong
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox / Switch / Switch 2
editions.note: Released on every platform at once; also on Game Pass.

name: Horizon
scope: Zero Dawn and Forbidden West, both expansions included. Lego Horizon Adventures and Call of the Mountain (VR) are out of scope.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree. Both expansions sit after their base game’s main story rather than alongside it.

games.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
games.note: The 2024 Remastered edition replaced the Complete Edition, which is now delisted on Steam. Existing owners were offered a paid upgrade rather than a free one.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn
editions.note: Original release; The Frozen Wilds sold separately.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Adds The Frozen Wilds expansion and bonus gear.

editions.name: Complete Edition (PC)
editions.note: First PC release; same content as the PS4 Complete Edition.

editions.name: Remastered
editions.note: Rebuilt visuals and Forbidden West systems, with The Frozen Wilds.

games.title: Horizon Zero Dawn: The Frozen Wilds
games.note: Bundled with the Remastered edition. Optional on paper, but it introduces hardware and characters Forbidden West assumes you have met.

editions.name: The Frozen Wilds
editions.note: Standalone expansion purchase; requires the base game.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the expansion with the base game; PC version in 2020.

editions.name: Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered
editions.note: Expansion included and rebuilt alongside the base game.

games.title: Horizon Forbidden West
games.note: The PC release (2024) is the Complete Edition and a good port. Picks up directly from Zero Dawn’s ending.

editions.name: Horizon Forbidden West
editions.note: Original release; Burning Shores was not yet out.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the Burning Shores expansion; PC version followed in 2024.

games.title: Horizon Forbidden West: Burning Shores
games.note: Bundled with the Complete Edition. Not optional in practice — its ending is the clearest setup for whatever comes third.

editions.name: Burning Shores
editions.note: Standalone expansion purchase; PS5 only, no PS4 version.

editions.name: Horizon Forbidden West Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the expansion with the base game; PC version followed in 2024.

name: inFAMOUS
scope: The five Sucker Punch releases: inFAMOUS, inFAMOUS 2, the standalone side story Festival of Blood, inFAMOUS: Second Son and its standalone prequel First Light. The Vita card game inFAMOUS: Paper Trail companion content is excluded.
caveat: Chronology mostly matches release order, with two exceptions. Festival of Blood came out after inFAMOUS 2 but is set during it. First Light came out alongside Second Son but is a prequel to it. The series also has branching karma endings; the sequels resolve them by treating the good-karma outcome as what happened.

arcs.name: Cole MacGrath
arcs.blurb: The PS3 arc: Empire City, New Marais, and the Beast.

arcs.name: Delsin Rowe
arcs.blurb: The PS4 arc, set seven years later in a Seattle under conduit lockdown.

games.title: inFAMOUS
games.note: Cole's origin and the Ray Sphere blast that quarantines Empire City. The twist ending is the whole setup for inFAMOUS 2, so this one is not optional. Never remastered, so it is PS3 or PS Plus Premium streaming.

games.title: inFAMOUS 2
games.note: Picks up days after the first game with Cole heading to New Marais. Its two endings are mutually exclusive and Second Son proceeds from the good-karma one, which is worth knowing before you pick.

editions.name: inFAMOUS 2
editions.note: Only version; the Special Edition added cosmetics, not story.

games.title: inFAMOUS: Festival of Blood
games.note: A short standalone set in New Marais during inFAMOUS 2, framed as a story Zeke tells in a bar, so it is explicitly an unreliable account. Play it after inFAMOUS 2 rather than during; nothing later depends on it.

editions.name: inFAMOUS: Festival of Blood
editions.note: Digital-only; does not require owning inFAMOUS 2.

games.title: inFAMOUS: First Light
games.note: Fetch's backstory, told from her cell in Curdun Cay before Second Son begins. It came out after Second Son but sits before it, and it makes her a much clearer character if you play it first.

editions.name: inFAMOUS: First Light
editions.note: Standalone download; does not require Second Son.

games.title: inFAMOUS: Second Son
games.note: Seven years after inFAMOUS 2, with a new lead in Delsin and Seattle under the DUP. It recaps enough of Cole's story to work as a first game, which is why it is the practical entry point for anyone without a PS3.

editions.name: inFAMOUS: Second Son
editions.note: Only version; runs unchanged on PS5 through backward compatibility.

name: Jak and Daxter
scope: The four Naughty Dog games: The Precursor Legacy, Jak II, Jak 3 and Jak X: Combat Racing. The handheld spin-offs Daxter and The Lost Frontier, made by other studios, are excluded.
caveat: Chronology is release order. The only wrinkle is the gap between the first and second games: Jak II opens with the pair thrown two hundred years into the future of the same world, so the tonal jump from bright platformer to grim open city is a deliberate in-story time skip, not a reboot.

games.title: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy
games.version: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (PS4)
games.query: Jak and Daxter The Precursor Legacy
games.note: Establishes the world, the Precursors and how Daxter got turned into an ottsel, which the rest of the series never re-explains. It is also the only game in the series with no guns and no voice for Jak.

editions.name: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Jak and Daxter Collection
editions.note: HD remasters of the first three games.

editions.name: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (PS4)
editions.note: Emulated PS2 version with trophies and rewind; the easiest to buy now.

games.title: Jak II
games.note: Two hundred years after the first game, in Haven City, after two years of Dark Eco experiments on Jak. Known for a difficulty spike and checkpointing that the HD versions do not soften.

editions.name: Jak II
editions.note: Original release; Jak II: Renegade in PAL regions.

editions.name: Jak and Daxter Collection
editions.note: HD remaster in the three-game collection.

editions.name: Jak II (PS4)
editions.note: Emulated PS2 version with save states, which takes the edge off the checkpoints.

games.title: Jak 3
games.note: Opens with Jak exiled to the wasteland shortly after Jak II and resolves the Precursor and Dark Eco threads from both earlier games. This is the end of the main story.

editions.name: Jak 3
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Jak and Daxter Collection
editions.note: HD remaster in the three-game collection.

editions.name: Jak 3 (PS4)
editions.note: Emulated PS2 version with trophies and save states.

games.title: Jak X: Combat Racing
games.note: A combat racer set a year after Jak 3, with the cast poisoned and forced into a racing circuit. It is the last chronological entry, but the story is thin and skipping it costs you nothing.

editions.name: Jak X: Combat Racing
editions.note: Original release; not in the HD collection.

editions.name: Jak X: Combat Racing (PS4)
editions.note: Emulated PS2 version; the only re-release the game ever got.

name: Judgment
scope: Both Judgment games, the detective series RGG Studio set in the same Kamurocho as Yakuza. The Kaito Files, a story expansion for Lost Judgment, is covered as an edition rather than a separate entry.
caveat: Two games, in release order, three years apart in the fiction. They share a city and a handful of background characters with Yakuza but tell their own story about lawyer-turned-detective Takayuki Yagami, so no Yakuza game is required first.

games.title: Judgment
games.note: Introduces Yagami and the Kamurocho serial killer case that defines his reputation in the sequel. The remaster runs at 60fps and replaces one recast character model from the original PS4 release.

editions.name: Judgment
editions.note: Original release; delisted for a period over an actor's legal issue.

editions.name: Judgment (Remastered)
editions.note: 60fps, recast model, and the version still on sale; PC arrived in 2022.

games.title: Lost Judgment
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set three years later and split between Kamurocho and Yokohama, with a case about school bullying. Assumes you know Yagami's team from the first game, so it is not a good starting point.

editions.name: Lost Judgment
editions.platforms: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Console launch; PC followed a year later.

editions.name: Lost Judgment with The Kaito Files
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Adds a several-hour campaign starring Kaito with its own combat style.

name: Killzone
scope: The six single-player Killzone releases: Killzone, Liberation, Killzone 2, Killzone 3, Mercenary and Shadow Fall. Killzone: Intercept and other tie-in fiction are excluded.
caveat: Chronology follows release order with one overlap: Mercenary came out in 2013 but its campaign runs alongside the first three games, from the Vektan invasion through the ISA assault on Helghan. Shadow Fall then jumps roughly thirty years past Killzone 3. Most of the series is stranded on PS3 and Vita, which is the real obstacle rather than the ordering.

games.title: Killzone
games.note: The Helghast invasion of Vekta in 2357, and the first sight of Rico, Templar and Luger. The HD version inside Killzone Trilogy is the only practical way to play it now.

editions.name: Killzone
editions.note: Original release, with a rough frame rate.

editions.name: Killzone HD
editions.note: Remaster sold inside Killzone Trilogy alongside Killzone 2 and 3.

games.title: Killzone: Liberation
games.note: A top-down handheld spin-off set two months after Killzone, following Templar's squad in southern Vekta. It fills the gap before Killzone 2 but nothing later requires it.

editions.name: Killzone: Liberation
editions.note: PSP release; the digital version also downloads to PS3 and PS Vita.

games.title: Killzone: Mercenary
games.note: Told from a contractor's side of the war, its missions span the whole first-trilogy period rather than sitting at one point in it. Vita-exclusive and never ported, so it is the hardest entry to reach.

editions.name: Killzone: Mercenary
editions.note: Only version; requires Vita hardware.

games.title: Killzone 2
games.note: Two years after the first game, with the ISA invading Helghan and Visari as the target. It opens with enough briefing to work as a starting point, and it is the entry the series is usually remembered for.

editions.name: Killzone 2
editions.note: Sold on its own or inside Killzone Trilogy.

games.title: Killzone 3
games.note: Starts minutes after Killzone 2 ends and resolves the Helghan campaign. Playing it without Killzone 2 makes very little sense; the opening assumes the previous ending outright.

editions.name: Killzone 3
editions.note: Sold on its own or inside Killzone Trilogy; the 3D and Move support are optional.

games.title: Killzone: Shadow Fall
games.note: About thirty years after Killzone 3, with Vektans and Helghast sharing one divided city. It is a mostly self-contained story and the only entry easily bought on current hardware.

editions.name: Killzone: Shadow Fall
editions.note: Only version; playable on PS5 through backward compatibility.

name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
scope: Both Warhorse RPGs following Henry of Skalitz in early 15th-century Bohemia. The mobile card game and tie-in tabletop material are excluded.
caveat: Two games, in release order, with no ambiguity: the second begins right where the first ends, in 1403, with the same protagonist and several returning companions. The first game's DLC episodes are side stories that sit inside its timeline rather than after it.

games.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Henry's story starts here, and the sequel opens on unresolved threads from its ending. The Royal Edition includes all four DLC, of which A Woman's Lot matters most because it sets up a character who returns in the sequel.

editions.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
editions.note: Base game; rough at launch, heavily patched since.

editions.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance - Royal Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Base game plus From the Ashes, The Amorous Adventurer, Band of Bastards and A Woman's Lot.

games.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
games.note: A direct continuation rather than a soft reboot: it starts mid-journey from the first game and expects you to know who Hans Capon and Sir Radzig are. It recaps the essentials in an opening cinematic, but the emotional weight of the first game does not transfer.

editions.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
editions.note: Single release; the Gold edition adds the post-launch expansions.

name: Kingdom Hearts
scope: The Dark Seeker saga, from Union χ through Kingdom Hearts III, including the DS and 3DS side entries that the HD collections absorbed. Kingdom Hearts Melody of Memory, a rhythm spin-off, and the mobile-only Dark Road are excluded.
caveat: Every numbered gap in this series is filled by a handheld game, and skipping them makes Kingdom Hearts III unreadable. Release order and chronology diverge badly: Birth by Sleep came out eighth but is set first, and 0.2 mostly depicts events that begin immediately after Birth by Sleep even though it was released much later. In practice you buy two collections — HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX and HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue — plus Kingdom Hearts III, and two of the games inside them are watchable cutscene movies rather than playable.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts Union χ
games.version: Kingdom Hearts Union χ Dark Road
games.note: Set centuries before every other game, in the age before the Keyblade War. Online service ended in 2021 and the offline archive only preserves the story scenes; the film χ Back Cover in HD 2.8 covers the same ground more briefly.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts Union χ
editions.note: Live service ended; an offline story archive remains.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set roughly ten years before the first game and explains most of what the later entries assume. Three campaigns plus a final episode that only unlocks after all three; the Switch versions are cloud streaming, not local.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep
editions.note: Original release; Final Mix was Japan-only.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Final Mix version bundled with five other games.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The clearest place to begin even though Birth by Sleep is set earlier, because it introduces the cast and assumes nothing. The collection uses the Final Mix version, which adds bosses and scenes the 2002 Western release did not have.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts
editions.note: Original release without Final Mix content.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Final Mix, remastered, with revised camera controls.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Begins the instant the first game ends and sets up Kingdom Hearts II's opening, so it cannot be skipped. The collection uses Re:Chain of Memories, the 3D PS2 rebuild, which keeps the card-based combat that puts many people off.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories
editions.note: Original 2D release.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Contains the Re:Chain of Memories remake.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Runs alongside the first game and Chain of Memories and ends immediately before Kingdom Hearts II. In the collection it is a three-hour cutscene film, not a playable game — the DS original is the only version you can play.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days
editions.note: The only playable version; never remade.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: HD cutscene movie covering the full story.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Opens a year after Chain of Memories and pays off both handheld games directly. Final Mix adds the Data Organization fights and several scenes that later entries reference.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts II
editions.note: Original release without Final Mix content.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Final Mix with the extra bosses and the Lingering Will.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts Re:coded
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Framed after Kingdom Hearts II, though most of it retreads the first game inside a digital journal. Only the ending matters to the wider plot, and like 358/2 Days the collection version is a cutscene movie.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts Re:coded
editions.note: The only playable version.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: HD cutscene movie.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance
games.version: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
games.note: The direct setup for Kingdom Hearts III and the point where the plot around Xehanort is finally laid out. HD 2.8 also contains the χ Back Cover film, which summarises the Union χ era.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: HD version with 0.2 and the χ Back Cover film.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts 0.2 Birth by Sleep – A Fragmentary Passage
games.version: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
games.note: Most of it takes place right after Birth by Sleep, but it was built as the immediate lead-in to Kingdom Hearts III and its closing scenes only land if you have seen Dream Drop Distance. Short, and it uses the Kingdom Hearts III engine.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Only ever released inside HD 2.8.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts III
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Ends the Dark Seeker saga and resolves threads from every game above. The Re Mind DLC adds an extended version of the finale and is where the sequel hook actually lives, so treat it as part of the game.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts III
editions.note: Base game without Re Mind.

editions.name: Kingdom Hearts III + Re Mind
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Base game plus the story DLC and extra bosses.

name: Life is Strange
scope: The five full-length games in the series. The free short The Awesome Adventures of Captain Spirit and the mobile-only Life is Strange: Wavelengths standalone listing are excluded; Wavelengths is treated as True Colors DLC.
caveat: Listed in in-universe order, which is not the order to play them in. Before the Storm is a prequel set three years before the first game, but it was written for people who already know how that story ends, so playing it first drains most of its meaning. The games otherwise share a world rather than a plot: only Double Exposure is a direct sequel, picking up Max's story years after the first game.

games.title: Life is Strange: Before the Storm
games.version: Life is Strange: Before the Storm Remastered
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set three years before the first game, following Chloe and Rachel, with no time-rewind mechanic. Play it after the original despite its position here; it is written as a companion piece, not an introduction. The Farewell bonus episode is included in the Deluxe and Remastered versions.

editions.name: Life is Strange: Before the Storm
editions.note: Original episodic release.

editions.name: Life is Strange: Before the Storm Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Updated models and animation; sold on its own or in the Remastered Collection with the first game.

games.title: Life is Strange
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Max, Chloe and Arcadia Bay in October 2013, and the game every later entry is measured against. Start here: it sets up the prequel's payoff and is the direct setup for Double Exposure.

editions.name: Life is Strange
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Original episodic release; still sold and still fine.

editions.name: Life is Strange Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Rebuilt character animation; bundled with Before the Storm as the Remastered Collection.

games.title: Life is Strange 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A new cast entirely, following two brothers on the road in late 2016. Only loosely tied to the first game; the free prologue Captain Spirit introduces one supporting character and takes about two hours.

editions.name: Life is Strange 2
editions.note: Episodic release across 2018 and 2019.

editions.name: Life is Strange 2: Complete Season
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: All five episodes in one purchase.

games.title: Life is Strange: True Colors
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Standalone story with Alex Chen in Haven Springs, released as one complete game rather than episodically. The Wavelengths DLC is a side story starring a character from Before the Storm and is where the two connect.

editions.name: Life is Strange: True Colors
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: The Deluxe edition adds the Wavelengths DLC and cosmetics.

games.title: Life is Strange: Double Exposure
games.note: The only direct sequel to the first game: Max, roughly a decade on, at a university in Vermont. It asks which ending you chose in the original, so it lands very differently if you have not played that.

editions.name: Life is Strange: Double Exposure
editions.note: One release; the Ultimate edition unlocks the later chapters early.

name: Little Nightmares
scope: The three mainline games. The Secrets of the Maw DLC chapters are treated as part of the first game, and the mobile spin-off Very Little Nightmares is excluded.
caveat: Little Nightmares II was released second but its ending reveals it takes place before the first game, tying Mono's fate to the figure who hunts Six later. That reveal is the whole point of the sequence, so playing in release order is the better experience even though the timeline reads the other way. Little Nightmares III has no stated position relative to the other two; it is placed last here for want of anything firmer.

games.title: Little Nightmares II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Earliest in the timeline, following Mono and a Six who has not yet reached the Maw. Its final scene only means anything if you have played the first game, so this position is timeline information rather than a play order.

editions.name: Little Nightmares II
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Little Nightmares II Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Rebuilt lighting and effects for current hardware; free upgrade for owners.

games.title: Little Nightmares
games.note: Six aboard the Maw, and the game the sequel's ending points back at. Start here. The Complete Edition includes the three Secrets of the Maw chapters, which run alongside the main story with a different child.

editions.name: Little Nightmares
editions.note: Base game without the DLC chapters.

editions.name: Little Nightmares Complete Edition
editions.note: Base game plus all three Secrets of the Maw chapters.

games.title: Little Nightmares III
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch / Switch 2
games.note: A new pair of children, Low and Alone, in a region called the Spiral, made by a different studio than the first two. Built around two-player co-op with an AI partner as the solo option; its relationship to the earlier games is left open.

editions.name: Little Nightmares III
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch / Switch 2
editions.note: One release; online co-op only, with no local split-screen.

name: Lost Planet
scope: The three Capcom games set on E.D.N. III. The free-to-play spin-off E.X. Troopers, released only in Japan, is excluded.
caveat: Two of the three follow release order, but Lost Planet 3 came last and is a prequel set decades before the first game, back when the planet was still being surveyed. The series has also become hard to buy: the PC versions have been pulled from sale, so console copies and Xbox backward compatibility are the practical routes.

games.title: Lost Planet 3
games.note: A prequel set during the first colonisation effort, long before the first game's Snow Pirates exist. Made by a Western studio as a slower narrative game, which makes it the odd one out mechanically as well as chronologically.

editions.name: Lost Planet 3
editions.note: The only version; the PC release has been delisted.

games.title: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition
games.version: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition Colonies Edition
games.query: Lost Planet Extreme Condition Colonies Edition
games.note: Wayne Holden's story and the introduction of the Akrid, thermal energy and Vital Suits that the sequels build on. Colonies Edition adds extra missions and modes and is the version to look for.

editions.name: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition
editions.note: Original release; the PC version used Games for Windows Live.

editions.name: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition Colonies Edition
editions.note: Adds first-person view, extra weapons and new missions.

games.title: Lost Planet 2
games.note: Set ten years after the first game, with the planet partly terraformed and the story split across several unrelated squads rather than one protagonist. It was designed around four-player co-op, and playing it alone with bots is noticeably worse.

editions.name: Lost Planet 2
editions.note: The only version; official online servers are long gone.

name: Mafia
scope: The four Mafia games: The Old Country, Mafia, Mafia II and Mafia III. Each Definitive Edition is treated as the current version of its game rather than as a separate entry.
caveat: Release order and chronology disagree at both ends. The Old Country came out last but is set earliest, in 1900s Sicily, and the 2020 Definitive Edition of the first game is a full remake rather than a remaster, with rewritten scenes. The games are largely standalone stories in different cities, but Vito Scaletta carries over from Mafia II into Mafia III, so those two are worth playing in order.

games.title: Mafia: The Old Country
games.note: Early 1900s Sicily, showing the world the American families came out of. It is the earliest point on the timeline and shares no characters with the other three, so it works as a standalone.

editions.name: Mafia: The Old Country
editions.note: Current-generation only; no PS4 or Xbox One version.

games.title: Mafia
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Tommy Angelo in Lost Heaven, 1930 to 1938. The Definitive Edition rebuilt the game from scratch and reworked several scenes, so it is not the same script as the 2002 original, but it is the version on sale and the best place to start the series.

editions.name: Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven
editions.note: Original release; delisted digitally.

editions.name: Mafia: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Full remake with new voice work and expanded story scenes.

games.title: Mafia II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Vito Scaletta in Empire Bay, from 1943 into the early 1950s. This one is a straight remaster rather than a remake, and it includes the three DLC packs. Playing it makes Vito's role in Mafia III far clearer.

editions.name: Mafia II
editions.note: Original release; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Mafia II: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Remaster with all three DLC packs included.

games.title: Mafia III
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: New Bordeaux in 1968, following Lincoln Clay, with an older Vito as an ally. The latest point on the timeline and the most repetitive of the four; the Definitive Edition folds in all three story expansions.

editions.name: Mafia III
editions.note: Original release; capped at 30fps at launch.

editions.name: Mafia III: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Includes Faster Baby, Stones Unturned and Sign of the Times.

name: Marvel's Spider-Man
scope: Insomniac Games' Spider-Man continuity only: Marvel's Spider-Man, Miles Morales and Spider-Man 2. Older licensed Spider-Man games and the movie tie-ins are a separate, unrelated set of stories and are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order exactly. Miles Morales is a shorter standalone chapter set roughly a year after the first game, and Spider-Man 2 assumes you know how both ended.

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man
games.note: The starting point: Peter Parker eight years into the job, and the origin of every relationship the later games lean on. The Remastered version includes the three-part City That Never Sleeps DLC, which sets up Black Cat and Silver Sable threads.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man
editions.note: Original release; base game only unless you buy the DLC.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Bundles the City That Never Sleeps DLC.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered
editions.note: Higher framerate, rebuilt assets, all DLC included.

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales
games.note: Set about a year after the first game, over one Harlem winter, while Peter is out of the city. Short, but it establishes Miles as a co-lead and Spider-Man 2 opens from here.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales
editions.note: Console release; the PS5 version adds ray tracing and faster loads.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales (PC)
editions.note: Same content with uncapped framerate and PC graphics options.

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.note: Picks up roughly ten months after Miles Morales with both Spider-Men active. It pays off character arcs from both earlier games and ends on a deliberate hook.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
editions.note: Original console release.

editions.name: Marvel's Spider-Man 2 (PC)
editions.note: PC port with the post-launch New Game Plus and accessibility updates included.

name: Mass Effect
scope: The three Shepard games and Andromeda; the mobile, browser and card-game spin-offs are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order exactly. Andromeda is not a sequel to Mass Effect 3 in the usual sense: its colony ships leave the Milky Way between Mass Effect 2 and 3, then arrive 634 years later, so it sits last on the timeline but tells a separate story.

arcs.name: Shepard Trilogy
arcs.blurb: Commander Shepard's three-game fight against the Reapers in the Milky Way.

arcs.name: Andromeda
arcs.blurb: A separate cast settling the Andromeda galaxy centuries after the Reaper war.

games.title: Mass Effect
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The start of the timeline and the trilogy. The Legendary Edition rebuilds its combat and vehicle handling, which were the original's weakest parts.

editions.name: Mass Effect
editions.note: Original release; stiff combat and a locked low frame rate.

editions.name: Mass Effect Legendary Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Remaster of all three games with nearly all DLC.

games.title: Mass Effect 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Picks up two years after the first game. Save imports carry decisions forward, so playing it out of order loses most of its weight.

editions.name: Mass Effect 2
editions.note: Original release; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Mass Effect Legendary Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Includes Lair of the Shadow Broker, Overlord, Arrival and the rest.

games.title: Mass Effect 3
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The end of the Reaper war and the payoff for two games of choices. The Legendary Edition ships the Extended Cut ending by default.

editions.name: Mass Effect 3
editions.note: Original release; needed the Extended Cut patch and had a multiplayer mode tied to the ending.

editions.name: Mass Effect Legendary Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Single-player only, with the story DLC and Extended Cut folded in.

games.title: Mass Effect: Andromeda
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A clean entry point with a new cast; the Andromeda Initiative departs before Mass Effect 3, but the game itself is set 634 years later. No story DLC was ever released.

editions.name: Mass Effect: Andromeda
editions.note: Base game.

editions.name: Mass Effect: Andromeda Deluxe Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Adds cosmetic and multiplayer extras; runs on current consoles via back-compat.

name: Max Payne
scope: All three. Nothing else in the series exists.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree — three games, in order, no branches, no flashback structure that moves anything.

games.title: Max Payne
games.note: Needs community patches for widescreen and frame pacing on modern displays. Remedy is remaking 1 and 2 as a single title — announced 2022, still unreleased as of August 2026.

editions.name: Max Payne
editions.note: Original release and still the most complete, easiest version to run.

editions.name: Max Payne Mobile
editions.note: Touch port of the full game; controls are the obvious compromise.

games.title: Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne
games.note: Shorter and tighter than the first. Same caveats about modern displays.

games.title: Max Payne 3
games.note: Rockstar-developed, nine years later, São Paulo instead of New York. Requires the Rockstar launcher. Tonally a different game; still the same man.

editions.name: Max Payne 3
editions.note: Base game; DLC packs sold separately through the Rockstar Pass.

editions.name: Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles every DLC pack; the single-player story itself is unchanged.

name: Mega Man
scope: A selection of the story-load-bearing entries from the five series that share one timeline: Classic, X, Zero, ZX and Legends. Battle Network and Star Force sit in a separate parallel continuity and are excluded, as are the many spin-offs and the Game Boy side games.
caveat: Capcom's official timeline threads five series across thousands of years: Classic in the 20XXs, X roughly a century later, Zero about a century after that, ZX around two hundred years later again, and Legends in a far future where the oceans have swallowed most of the land. Within each series chronology equals release order, but the series themselves were not released in timeline order, and the last two both trail off without conclusions.

arcs.name: Classic
arcs.blurb: Dr. Light's robot boy against Dr. Wily, in the 20XXs.

arcs.name: X
arcs.blurb: A century later, X and Zero fight the Maverick outbreaks among self-aware Reploids.

arcs.name: Zero
arcs.blurb: Zero wakes a hundred years on into a world where humans persecute Reploids.

arcs.name: ZX
arcs.blurb: Two centuries after Zero, humans and Reploids merge biometal to fight Model W.

arcs.name: Legends
arcs.blurb: A flooded far future of diggers and ruins, told in 3D rather than as a platformer.

games.title: Mega Man
games.note: The first game and the introduction of Dr. Light and Dr. Wily, whose feud the whole timeline traces back to. It is also the roughest of the NES entries, with no password system and an unbalanced difficulty curve.

editions.name: Mega Man
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Legacy Collection
editions.note: Bundles the first six games with save states and rewind.

games.title: Mega Man 2
games.note: The entry that set the template the series ran on for two decades, and the usual recommendation for a first Mega Man game. Story content is thin; it matters more as the design reference point than as plot.

editions.name: Mega Man 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: Mega Man 3
games.note: Introduces Proto Man and the slide, both series fixtures afterwards. The X series later treats this era as ancient history rather than referencing it directly.

editions.name: Mega Man 3
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: Mega Man 11
games.note: The most recent Classic entry and the last point on that part of the timeline. Fully voiced and hand-drawn rather than pixel art, with a Double Gear system that changes how bosses are approached.

editions.name: Mega Man 11
editions.note: The only version.

games.title: Mega Man X
games.note: Set roughly a century after the Classic games, opening with Dr. Light's final creation being unearthed. Introduces Zero and the Maverick premise that carries through the next three series.

editions.name: Mega Man X
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man X Legacy Collection
editions.note: Bundles X1 through X4 with a timeline gallery.

games.title: Mega Man X4
games.note: The first entry with Zero as a full playable campaign, and the one that starts explaining his origin. The Repliforce conflict here is the plot most later X games refer back to.

editions.name: Mega Man X4
editions.note: Original release with anime cutscenes.

editions.name: Mega Man X Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the first X bundle.

games.title: Mega Man X5
games.note: Written as the intended end of the X series and the bridge into the Zero series, which is why its ending matters more than its gameplay. The Legacy Collection version restores the original Japanese boss names that the Western release replaced.

editions.name: Mega Man X5
editions.note: Western release renamed the bosses after Guns N' Roses members.

editions.name: Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2
editions.note: Bundles X5 through X8 with the original naming restored.

games.title: Mega Man X8
games.note: The last X game and the final point on that part of the timeline before the Zero series picks up. X6 and X7 sit between this and X5 but neither is required reading; X7 in particular is widely considered the low point of the series.

editions.name: Mega Man X8
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2
editions.note: Included in the second X bundle.

games.title: Mega Man Zero
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Set about a century after the X series, with Zero awakened into a world where the roles of hero and oppressor have inverted. Much harder than the X games and built around a mission ranking system.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: All four Zero games plus both ZX games, with an optional assist mode.

games.title: Mega Man Zero 2
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Continues a year after the first game. The four Zero games form one story with a single ending, so skipping any of them leaves gaps.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: Mega Man Zero 3
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Resolves the question of what Zero's body actually is, and ties the Zero series back to the X games directly. Usually cited as the strongest of the four.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero 3
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: Mega Man Zero 4
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Ends the Zero series and, with it, the storyline running from the first X game. Its ending is the setup the ZX games start from two centuries later.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero 4
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: Mega Man ZX
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Set roughly two hundred years after Zero 4, with humans and Reploids living together and merging with biometal. Structured as a connected map rather than a stage select, which is a large departure from the Zero games.

editions.name: Mega Man ZX
editions.note: Original release; used the second screen for the map.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: Single-screen presentation with the map on a toggle.

games.title: Mega Man ZX Advent
games.query: Mega Man Zero ZX Legacy Collection
games.note: Set four years after ZX with new protagonists. It ends on an unresolved hook that no later game has picked up, so the ZX branch of the timeline simply stops here.

editions.name: Mega Man ZX Advent
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection
editions.note: Included in the six-game bundle.

games.title: The Misadventures of Tron Bonne
games.note: A prequel to Mega Man Legends following the Bonne family before they meet Volnutt. Original PS1 copies are among the most expensive Capcom discs, and it has never had a wide digital rerelease.

editions.name: The Misadventures of Tron Bonne
editions.note: The only version; a puzzle and management game rather than a platformer.

games.title: Mega Man Legends
games.note: Set in a far future where the surface is mostly water and the past is buried in ruins; the link to the earlier series is deliberately left implicit. A full 3D action adventure rather than a platformer.

editions.name: Mega Man Legends
editions.note: The reference version; N64 and PC ports also exist and are rarer.

games.title: Mega Man Legends 2
games.note: Continues directly and answers most of what the first game left open about the world's origins, then ends on a cliffhanger. Mega Man Legends 3 was cancelled in 2011, so this is where the timeline stops.

editions.name: Mega Man Legends 2
editions.note: The only version; a PC port shipped in Japan only.

name: Metal Gear
scope: The mainline Hideo Kojima games from the MSX2 originals through Metal Gear Solid V, plus Metal Gear Rising as a sequel to MGS4. Metal Gear Survive, the Ac!d card games, Ghost Babel and the mobile spin-offs are excluded.
caveat: In-universe chronology is nearly the reverse of release order: the series began with Solid Snake in the 1990s and spent its second half telling Big Boss's story from 1964 onward. Playing chronologically works, but MGS3 and MGS5 are built to pay off reveals from games released earlier, so a first-time player loses several twists that way.

arcs.name: Big Boss Saga
arcs.blurb: Naked Snake becomes Big Boss and builds his own army, from 1964 Soviet Russia to 1984 Afghanistan.

arcs.name: Solid Snake Saga
arcs.blurb: Big Boss's cloned son fights a run of Metal Gear crises from 1995 to 2014, with Raiden carrying the story past it.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater
games.version: Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater
games.query: Metal Gear Solid Delta Snake Eater
games.note: Set in 1964, the earliest point in the timeline and the origin of Big Boss. Delta is a rebuilt version of the same script and level design, so it replaces rather than supplements the original.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater / Subsistence
editions.note: Subsistence added the free camera the original lacked.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Ports the HD Collection version, capped at 720p/30.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater
editions.note: Full remake in Unreal Engine 5 with the original voice tracks.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops
games.note: Set in 1970 and bridges Snake Eater to Peace Walker, but Peace Walker restates most of what matters. It has never been rereleased and is absent from the Master Collection.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops
editions.note: The only version; playable on PSP or Vita only.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker
games.note: Set in 1974 and introduces the base-building and mission structure MGS5 runs on; its ending leads directly into Ground Zeroes. Only on PSP and the PS3/360 HD Collection, so it is the hardest mainline entry to play today.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker
editions.note: Original handheld release.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid HD Collection
editions.note: Console version with dual-stick controls and higher resolution.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes
games.version: Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience
games.query: Metal Gear Solid V The Definitive Experience
games.note: A single mission set in 1975 that resolves Peace Walker's cliffhanger and sets up The Phantom Pain. Short enough that buying it separately is rarely worth it over the bundle.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Sold standalone.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience
editions.note: Bundles Ground Zeroes, The Phantom Pain and all DLC.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
games.version: Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience
games.query: Metal Gear Solid V The Definitive Experience
games.note: Set in 1984 and closes the Big Boss arc, connecting directly to the opening of the 1987 Metal Gear. The story is unfinished by design; a planned Chapter 3 was cut and survives only as unused footage.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Standalone release.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience
editions.note: Same game plus Ground Zeroes and the DLC packs.

games.title: Metal Gear
games.version: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1
games.note: Set in 1995 and the first Solid Snake mission. The MSX2 original is included with the Master Collection rather than sold on its own; the NES port is a different, worse game and is not the one to play.

editions.name: Metal Gear (MSX2)
editions.note: The original and the version all later games treat as canon.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Bundles the MSX2 version with save states.

games.title: Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake
