games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1
games.note: Set in 1999 and the direct setup for Metal Gear Solid, including Snake's relationship with Big Boss and Gray Fox. MGS1 recaps it in dialogue, so it is skippable but short.

editions.name: Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake
editions.note: Japan-only until the 2006 Subsistence rerelease.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Included alongside the first Metal Gear.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid
games.version: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1
games.note: Set in 2005 on Shadow Moses and the cleanest entry point to the whole series. The GameCube remake, The Twin Snakes, is not in the Master Collection and has never been rereleased.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes
editions.note: Remake with MGS2 mechanics and restaged cutscenes; unavailable today.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: The PS1 version with the VR Missions disc and the two MSX2 games.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
games.version: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1
games.note: Opens in 2007 with a Snake prologue, then jumps to 2009 with Raiden as the player character. The Master Collection uses the HD Edition build, which is the Substance version with the extra missions.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid 2: Substance
editions.note: Adds VR and snake tale missions to the original.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: HD Edition port; runs at 1080p but locked to 30fps.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
games.version: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
games.query: Metal Gear Solid 4 Guns of the Patriots
games.note: Set in 2014 and the ending of both Snake's story and most of the series' loose threads. Still PS3-exclusive and not in the Master Collection, which makes it the biggest availability gap in the series.

editions.name: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
editions.note: The only version ever released.

games.title: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
games.note: Set in 2018, four years after MGS4, with Raiden as the lead. Made by PlatinumGames as an action game rather than a stealth game, and it closes no threads the main series left open.

editions.name: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
editions.note: Console release.

editions.name: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance (PC)
editions.note: Includes all three DLC chapters and runs uncapped.

name: Metro
scope: The three Artyom games and their story DLC; the Dmitry Glukhovsky novels the series adapts are outside scope.
caveat: Chronology and release order are the same. The one thing worth knowing is that each game treats the previous game's better ending as what happened, so reaching the good ending in Metro 2033 is what Last Light assumes, and both earlier games carry into Exodus.

games.title: Metro 2033
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Artyom's first trip through the Moscow metro, and the starting point. Redux rebuilds it in the Last Light engine and adds a stealth-friendly Spartan mode; the 2010 original is still on Steam but is stiffer to play.

editions.name: Metro 2033
editions.note: Original build; harsher checkpointing and dated handling.

editions.name: Metro 2033 Redux
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Engine remake with reworked stealth and difficulty options.

games.title: Metro: Last Light
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Picks up directly from Metro 2033's good ending. Redux includes all the original DLC chapters, several of which are played as characters other than Artyom.

editions.name: Metro: Last Light
editions.note: Original release; DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Metro: Last Light Redux
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: All DLC included plus the survival-focused difficulty modes.

games.title: Metro Exodus
games.note: Leaves Moscow and crosses Russia by train over a year, with much larger open areas than the first two. The Enhanced Edition is a free upgrade but requires a ray-tracing capable GPU; the standard build is the fallback on older hardware.

editions.name: Metro Exodus
editions.note: Original release; PC version was Epic-exclusive for its first year.

editions.name: Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Free upgrade with full ray tracing; needs supporting hardware.

editions.name: Metro Exodus Gold Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Adds The Two Colonels and Sam's Story expansions.

name: Metroid
scope: The single-player Metroid games including the Prime sub-series. Metroid Prime: Federation Force, Metroid Prime Pinball and the fan remake AM2R are excluded. Where a remake exists it is listed as an edition of the original rather than as its own row.
caveat: Chronology and release order diverge badly. The Prime games came out between 2002 and 2007 but are set between the 1986 original and Metroid II from 1991, so the whole sub-series is an inserted flashback block. Everything after Super Metroid then runs in release order again. Availability is the other problem: several entries are stranded on Wii, DS and 3DS.

games.title: Metroid
games.version: Metroid: Zero Mission (Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.note: Samus's first mission to Zebes and the destruction of Mother Brain. Play the Zero Mission remake rather than the NES original: it keeps the same story, adds a map and an extra final section, and is included in the Game Boy Advance library on Nintendo Switch Online plus the Expansion Pack.

editions.name: Metroid
editions.note: Original release; no map and password saves.

editions.name: Metroid: Zero Mission
editions.note: Remake with modern controls and an added Zero Suit sequence.

editions.name: Metroid: Zero Mission (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Expansion Pack tier, with save states.

games.title: Metroid Prime
games.note: Set on Tallon IV shortly after the first game, and the best entry point the series currently has: rebuilt visuals, modern dual-stick controls, and a story that assumes nothing.

editions.name: Metroid Prime
editions.note: Original release; lock-on aiming only.

editions.name: Metroid Prime Trilogy
editions.note: All three Prime games with pointer controls; the Wii U re-release is delisted.

editions.name: Metroid Prime Remastered
editions.note: Full visual rebuild with several control schemes; the default now.

games.title: Metroid Prime Hunters
games.note: A handheld side story set between Prime and Echoes that introduces the rival bounty hunters. Never re-released, stylus-aimed, and nothing later depends on it.

editions.name: Metroid Prime Hunters
editions.note: Only version; requires DS hardware and a cartridge.

games.title: Metroid Prime 2: Echoes
games.note: Aether, the Ing, and Dark Samus continuing from Prime's ending. The only good version is inside Metroid Prime Trilogy, which means Wii hardware or a used disc since the Wii U store closed.

editions.name: Metroid Prime 2: Echoes
editions.note: Original release; steep difficulty and ammo-based beams.

editions.name: Metroid Prime Trilogy
editions.note: Pointer controls and rebalanced difficulty; the version to find.

games.title: Metroid Prime 3: Corruption
games.note: Closes the Dark Samus and Phazon story started in Prime. Sold inside Metroid Prime Trilogy alongside Echoes, with the same availability problem.

editions.name: Metroid Prime 3: Corruption
editions.note: Original release, built around pointer aiming.

editions.name: Metroid Prime Trilogy
editions.note: Same game with widescreen and trilogy-wide unlocks.

games.title: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond
games.note: Follows the Prime trilogy, on the planet Viewros. Nintendo has not spelled out exactly where it lands relative to Metroid II, only that it continues from Corruption, so its slot here follows the Prime sub-series rather than a stated date.

editions.name: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond
editions.note: One purchase covering both systems; Switch 2 runs at higher resolution and framerate.

games.title: Metroid II: Return of Samus
games.version: Metroid II: Return of Samus (Game Boy - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.note: Samus exterminating the Metroids on SR388 and taking the hatchling that Super Metroid opens with. The 3DS remake Samus Returns is the better game, but that store is closed, so the Switch Online Game Boy version is the practical option.

editions.name: Metroid II: Return of Samus
editions.note: Original release; monochrome with a very limited view.

editions.name: Metroid: Samus Returns
editions.note: Full remake with a melee counter and free aim; eShop closed.

editions.name: Metroid II (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Game Boy library, with save states.

games.title: Super Metroid
games.version: Super Metroid (Super Nintendo - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.note: Opens directly on the Metroid hatchling from Metroid II and returns to Zebes. Included in the Super Nintendo library on Nintendo Switch Online at the base tier, so it is the easiest older entry to reach.

editions.name: Super Metroid
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Super Metroid (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated with save states and rewind.

games.title: Metroid: Other M
games.note: Set between Super Metroid and Fusion, aboard the Bottle Ship. Never re-released and widely disliked for its handling of Samus; Fusion works fine without it.

editions.name: Metroid: Other M
editions.note: Only version; sideways Wii Remote controls throughout.

games.title: Metroid Fusion
games.version: Metroid Fusion (Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.note: Samus infected by the X parasite and rebuilt with Metroid DNA, on the BSL station. This is the direct setup for Dread, which starts from its ending. Included in the Game Boy Advance library on Nintendo Switch Online plus the Expansion Pack.

editions.name: Metroid Fusion
editions.note: Original cartridge.

editions.name: Metroid Fusion (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Expansion Pack tier, with save states.

games.title: Metroid Dread
games.note: The latest point on the timeline, following straight on from Fusion on planet ZDR. It opens with a recap of the whole 2D series, but the X parasite and Metroid DNA material lands much harder if you have played Fusion.

editions.name: Metroid Dread
editions.note: Only version; runs with improved performance on Switch 2.

name: Middle-earth
scope: Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War only. The wider Lord of the Rings games are excluded — see the note at the top of the page.
caveat: Two games, in order, both set between The Hobbit and The Fellowship of the Ring. No divergence between chronology and play order.

games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor
games.note: Game of the Year Edition. Introduces the Nemesis system. Loose with Tolkien canon, and knowingly so.

editions.name: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor
editions.note: Original release; the PS3 and Xbox 360 versions cut the Nemesis system.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds The Bright Lord and Lord of the Hunt story DLC and all extras.

games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of War
games.query: Middle-earth Shadow of War Definitive Edition
games.note: Buy the Definitive Edition (2018), not the original release. It removed the loot boxes and real-money market and rebalanced the Act IV grind the 2017 launch was pilloried for. All DLC included.

editions.name: Middle-earth: Shadow of War
editions.note: Launched with loot boxes and a real-money market, patched out in 2018.

editions.name: Gold Edition
editions.note: Base game plus the expansion pass; superseded by the Definitive Edition.

editions.name: Definitive Edition
editions.note: No loot boxes or market, and bundles both story expansions and all DLC.

name: Mortal Kombat
scope: The main-line fighting games that carry the story across three timelines. The spin-offs Mythologies: Sub-Zero, Special Forces and Shaolin Monks are excluded, as is the crossover Mortal Kombat vs. DC Universe, which the series treats as outside continuity.
caveat: The series has been rebooted twice by in-fiction time travel rather than by starting over. Mortal Kombat (2011) opens at the end of Armageddon and sends Raiden's memories back to the first tournament, restarting the story with different outcomes; Mortal Kombat 11 ends with Liu Kang remaking the timeline from scratch, which is where Mortal Kombat 1 begins. Each timeline is therefore its own self-contained order, and only the transitions between them require the previous one.

arcs.name: Original Timeline
arcs.blurb: The 1992 to 2006 run, from the first tournament to the world-ending battle of Armageddon.

arcs.name: Rebooted Timeline
arcs.blurb: Raiden's warning to his past self replays the first three tournaments with different casualties.

arcs.name: New Era
arcs.blurb: Liu Kang, now a god, builds a fresh timeline and finds it going wrong anyway.

games.title: Mortal Kombat
games.note: The first Shaolin tournament and the introduction of Liu Kang, Raiden, Scorpion and Sub-Zero. Story here is a paragraph per character rather than a mode, so its value is context for the 2011 reboot, which retells it.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat
editions.note: The SNES version censored the blood and fatalities.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 1+2+3
editions.note: The DOS conversions bundled with DOSBox; the simplest legal purchase.

games.title: Mortal Kombat II
games.note: Moves the tournament to Outworld and introduces Shao Kahn, Kitana and Mileena, the cast the series has used ever since. The strongest of the three arcade games and the easiest of them to pick up cold.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat II
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 1+2+3
editions.note: Included in the three-game bundle.

games.title: Mortal Kombat 3
games.note: Shao Kahn's invasion of Earthrealm, and the point where the original timeline's body count starts mounting. Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 and Mortal Kombat Trilogy are expanded versions of the same game with larger rosters.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 3
editions.note: Original release; omitted several returning characters.

editions.name: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3
editions.note: Restores the missing cast; the preferred arcade version.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 1+2+3
editions.note: The bundled DOS version; the only one currently on sale.

games.title: Mortal Kombat 4
games.note: The first 3D entry, introducing the fallen elder god Shinnok and the Netherrealm plot that later games return to. Mechanically the weakest of the early games, and its story beats are restated in Mortal Kombat X.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 4
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 4 (GOG)
editions.note: Prepatched PC version; the only current purchase.

games.title: Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance
games.note: Opens with Shang Tsung and Quan Chi killing Liu Kang, which sets the tone for the rest of the original timeline. Never rereleased; the three PS2-era games are the least available part of the series.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance
editions.note: The only version; the Game Boy Advance port is a different, lesser game.

games.title: Mortal Kombat: Deception
games.note: Follows directly from Deadly Alliance's ending, with the Dragon King Onaga as the threat. Its Konquest mode is a full adventure campaign and carries most of the story.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat: Deception
editions.note: The GameCube version, subtitled Mortal Kombat: Deception, arrived later with an extra character.

games.title: Mortal Kombat: Armageddon
games.note: Ends the original timeline with every character fighting at once and almost all of them dying. The opening minutes of the 2011 reboot are this game's final scene, so it is the one original-timeline entry that later games depend on.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat: Armageddon
editions.note: The Wii version adds a Konquest mode but plays worse.

games.title: Mortal Kombat (2011)
games.note: Begins at the end of Armageddon and retells the first three games with different outcomes, which makes it a clean entry point despite being the ninth game. The first entry with a full cinematic story mode.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat
editions.note: Base release; a Vita version added extra modes.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat Komplete Edition
editions.note: Adds all four DLC characters; the PC port has no online population left.

games.title: Mortal Kombat X
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set twenty-five years after the 2011 game, introducing the next generation of fighters alongside the survivors. Requires the 2011 game, since half the cast is dead or corrupted because of it.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat X
editions.note: Base game.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat XL
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Includes both Kombat Packs.

games.title: Mortal Kombat 11
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Picks up immediately after Mortal Kombat X and brings past versions of the cast forward through time. The Aftermath expansion contains the ending that leads into Mortal Kombat 1, so the Ultimate edition is the one that matters.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 11
editions.note: Base game; ends before the Aftermath chapters.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 11 Ultimate
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Bundles Aftermath and both Kombat Packs.

games.title: Mortal Kombat 1
games.note: Set in the timeline Liu Kang builds at the end of Mortal Kombat 11, with familiar characters in unfamiliar roles. The title restarts the numbering rather than continuing it, and the Khaos Reigns expansion continues the story.

editions.name: Mortal Kombat 1
editions.note: The Switch version runs at a much lower visual quality; Khaos Reigns is sold separately.

name: Mount & Blade
scope: The Calradia games: the 2008 original, its standalone expansion Warband, and Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord. With Fire & Sword, set in 17th-century Eastern Europe rather than Calradia, is excluded.
caveat: The chronology is inverted: Bannerlord, released last, is set roughly 200 years before the original game and Warband, during the collapse of the Calradic Empire whose successor kingdoms you fight over in Warband. These are sandbox games, so the connection is setting and faction history rather than a continuing plot, and the listed lengths are only for the optional main quests.

games.title: Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Earliest in the timeline despite being the newest game: the empire is still standing and the factions Warband players know are its provinces. Released in 2020 into early access and left it in 2022; the 1.0 build is the one being sold.

editions.name: Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord (Early Access)
editions.note: Two years of early access builds, no longer relevant.

editions.name: Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The 1.0 release with the full campaign and official mod tools.

games.title: Mount & Blade
games.note: The original Calradia sandbox, set two centuries after Bannerlord. Warband is the same game with an added sixth faction, multiplayer and better balance, so there is almost no reason to play this version now.

editions.name: Mount & Blade
editions.note: Only release; superseded in practice by Warband.

games.title: Mount & Blade: Warband
games.note: A standalone expansion of the 2008 game and the definitive version of that era, with the Sarranid Sultanate added and the option to found your own kingdom. Its modding scene is the main reason it is still played.

editions.name: Mount & Blade: Warband
editions.note: Standalone; does not require the original game.

editions.name: Mount & Blade: Warband (console)
editions.note: Controller-adapted port without mod support.

name: NieR / Drakengard
scope: The three Drakengard games and the two NieR games, which share one continuity created by Yoko Taro. The mobile title NieR Reincarnation, shut down in 2024, and the various stage plays and novellas are excluded.
caveat: These games branch off each other's alternate endings rather than following one line. Each game has several lettered endings, and a later game picks one of them as the canonical outcome: Drakengard 2 continues Drakengard's Ending A, while the entire NieR series grows out of Drakengard's Ending E, in which a dragon and its rider fall into modern-day Tokyo. Drakengard 3 released last but is a prequel to all of it.

arcs.name: Drakengard
arcs.blurb: Medieval fantasy about pact-bound humans and dragons, told across three PS2 and PS3 games.

arcs.name: NieR
arcs.blurb: The far-future branch that grows out of Drakengard's fifth ending, following the collapse and replacement of humanity.

games.title: Drakengard 3
games.note: A prequel to the first Drakengard, explaining where the Intoners and the world's magic came from. Released only on PS3 and never remastered; the frame rate is poor even on original hardware.

editions.name: Drakengard 3
editions.note: The only version; DLC prologue chapters were sold separately.

games.title: Drakengard
games.note: The origin of everything, and the game whose fifth ending starts the NieR branch. Only its Ending E matters to NieR players, and it takes several full playthroughs to reach.

editions.name: Drakengard
editions.note: The only version; no digital rerelease exists.

games.title: Drakengard 2
games.note: Continues Drakengard's Ending A, a branch the NieR games never touch, and is the one entry Yoko Taro did not direct. Nothing in NieR depends on it.

editions.name: Drakengard 2
editions.note: The only version; PS2 disc only.

games.title: NieR Replicant
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set roughly a thousand years after Drakengard's Ending E and thousands of years before Automata. The 2021 version is a rebuild of the Japanese Replicant release, not the Western Gestalt version, so the protagonist is a brother rather than a father.

editions.name: NieR Gestalt / NieR
editions.note: The original Western release, with an older protagonist.

editions.name: NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139...
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Rebuilt combat, new voice work, and an extra ending E.

games.title: NieR: Automata
games.version: NieR: Automata Game of the YoRHa Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: NieR Automata Game of the YoRHa Edition
games.note: Set thousands of years after Replicant and written to be readable without it, which is why most people start here. Endings A through E form a single story and must all be played; stopping at the first credits means seeing about a third of the game.

editions.name: NieR: Automata
editions.note: Launch PC port had persistent resolution and crash issues.

editions.name: NieR: Automata Game of the YoRHa Edition
editions.note: Bundles the 3C3C1D119440927 DLC; the PC version received an official patch in 2021.

editions.name: NieR: Automata The End of YoRHa Edition
editions.note: Portable version with all DLC, running at a lower resolution.

name: Ninja Gaiden
scope: The modern 3D Ryu Hayabusa line that began with the 2004 Xbox game. The NES trilogy, the 2025 side-scroller Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound and the Dead or Alive crossovers are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order; each game follows the last with no prequels or flashbacks. The complication is versions rather than order: nearly every entry exists in two or three substantially different cuts, and the one a collection ships is not always the best-regarded one.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Ryu's first modern outing and the start of the Fiend storyline the sequels continue. The Master Collection includes the PS3-derived Sigma version; Ninja Gaiden Black, which many prefer for its difficulty balance and enemy design, is only playable through Xbox backward compatibility.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden Black
editions.note: The definitive original-line version; runs on Xbox One and Series through backward compatibility.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden: Master Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Bundles Sigma, Sigma 2 and Razor's Edge; the only current purchase.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden II
games.note: Follows the first game directly, with the Archfiend plot escalating. Three versions exist: the bloodier Xbox 360 original, the reworked Sigma 2 in the Master Collection, and the 2025 Unreal Engine 5 remake, which restores the 360 version's gore and enemy counts.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden II
editions.note: Original; playable via Xbox backward compatibility.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden Sigma 2
editions.note: Reduced gore and enemy counts, added playable characters; the version in the Master Collection.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden 2 Black
editions.note: Unreal Engine 5 remake using the original's combat balance.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden 3: Razor's Edge
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The weakest entry in the line and the one nothing later depends on. Razor's Edge is a substantial revision of the poorly received 2012 release, restoring dismemberment and the upgrade system; the plain Ninja Gaiden 3 is not worth seeking out.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden 3
editions.note: Original release; removed weapon variety and upgrades.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden 3: Razor's Edge
editions.note: Revised version that put back most of what was cut.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden: Master Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Includes Razor's Edge; not sold on its own.

games.title: Ninja Gaiden 4
games.note: Set after Razor's Edge, with a new lead named Yakumo and Ryu in a supporting playable role. Co-developed by Team Ninja and PlatinumGames, so the combat feel differs from the earlier entries.

editions.name: Ninja Gaiden 4
editions.note: Single release; also available through Game Pass.

name: Onimusha
scope: The four main action-adventure games, from Warlords through Dawn of Dreams. The fighting spin-off Blade Warriors and the strategy game Onimusha Tactics are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order, moving forward through the Sengoku period from the 1560s to the 1590s. The one wrinkle is Onimusha 3, which cuts between feudal Japan and modern Paris; its Japanese half is where it sits on the timeline. The first two games have modern remasters, the last two do not.

games.title: Onimusha: Warlords
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Samanosuke's story and the origin of the Oni Gauntlet, set around 1560. The remaster adds analogue movement, a widescreen option and the Japanese audio track that the original Western release lacked.

editions.name: Onimusha: Warlords
editions.note: Original release with tank controls and fixed camera angles.

editions.name: Genma Onimusha
editions.note: Expanded version with extra areas; never rereleased.

editions.name: Onimusha: Warlords (2019)
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Remaster of the PS2 version with modern controls.

games.title: Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Follows Jubei Yagyu roughly a decade after Warlords, with Nobunaga still the antagonist. Its gift system changes which allies join you, so a single playthrough sees only part of the story.

editions.name: Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny
editions.note: Original release; PS2 only for over twenty years.

editions.name: Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny (2025)
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Remaster with modern controls and an easier difficulty option.

games.title: Onimusha 3: Demon Siege
games.note: Brings Samanosuke back for the confrontation at Honnoji in 1582, alternating with a French soldier displaced into the present day. Never remastered; a 2005 European PC port exists but is long out of print.

editions.name: Onimusha 3: Demon Siege
editions.note: The reference version; features Jean Reno as Jacques.

editions.name: Onimusha 3: Demon Siege (PC)
editions.note: Europe-only port, out of print and awkward on modern systems.

games.title: Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams
games.note: Set fifteen years after Nobunaga's death with an entirely new cast led by Soki, and structured as a party-based action game rather than a survival horror one. It is the longest entry and the only one never rereleased in any form.

editions.name: Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams
editions.note: Two-disc PS2 release; the only version.

name: Ori
scope: The two Moon Studios games: Ori and the Blind Forest and Ori and the Will of the Wisps.
caveat: Two games, chronology equals release order. Will of the Wisps opens on the owl egg that Blind Forest ends with, so playing them in reverse gives away the first game's ending and leaves the second one's premise unexplained.

games.title: Ori and the Blind Forest
games.version: Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition
games.platform: PC / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Ori and the Blind Forest Definitive Edition
games.note: Ori, Naru and the withering of Nibel. Get the Definitive Edition rather than the 2015 original: it adds two areas, fast travel and a difficulty option, and it is the only version still sold.

editions.name: Ori and the Blind Forest
editions.note: Original release; no fast travel, delisted.

editions.name: Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition
editions.platforms: PC / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Adds two areas, new abilities and easier difficulty settings.

games.title: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
games.version: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
games.platform: PC / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
games.note: Picks up immediately after Blind Forest, following Ku beyond Nibel into Niwen. Bigger, with a reworked combat system, and it resolves the story rather than leaving it open.

editions.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
editions.platforms: PC / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Only version; runs at 120fps on Xbox Series and is on Game Pass.

name: Outlast
scope: The two mainline games, the Whistleblower expansion and the multiplayer prequel The Outlast Trials. Nothing else exists in the series.
caveat: Ordered by in-universe date, which puts the newest release first: The Outlast Trials is a Cold War prequel decades before the rest. Whistleblower is the ordering trap. Waylon's story actually starts just before the first game, since he is the one who leaks the tip that sends Miles to Mount Massive, but most of it runs alongside and then past the first game's ending, so it belongs after it and is written to be played that way.

games.title: The Outlast Trials
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A Cold War-era prequel showing Murkoff's early human experiments, decades before Mount Massive. Built as a co-op roguelite rather than a linear campaign, so it tells its story through environments and briefings; playable solo but tuned for four.

editions.name: The Outlast Trials (Early Access)
editions.note: Year-long early access build.

editions.name: The Outlast Trials
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: The 1.0 release with the full trial roster and console versions.

games.title: Outlast
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Mount Massive Asylum, a camcorder with a dying battery, and no way to fight back. Short and the clearest entry point; on console the Outlast Trinity bundle pairs it with Whistleblower and Outlast 2.

editions.name: Outlast
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Whistleblower is a separate purchase on PC.

editions.name: Outlast Trinity
editions.note: Outlast, Whistleblower and Outlast 2 in one console package.

games.title: Outlast: Whistleblower
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Overlaps the first game from another character's perspective and continues past its ending, which is why it sits here rather than before. It also supplies the setup Outlast 2 assumes; requires the base game on PC.

editions.name: Outlast: Whistleblower
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: DLC for the base game; included in Outlast Trinity on console.

games.title: Outlast 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The latest point on the timeline, in the Arizona desert with a new cast and no returning characters. The connection to the first game is Murkoff and the technology behind it, revealed in documents rather than plot.

editions.name: Outlast 2
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: One release; a patch added difficulty options for its harder chase sequences.

name: Persona
scope: The Persona 2 duology and the three modern numbered entries. The fighting games, dancing games, Persona Q dungeon crawlers and Persona 5 Strikers are excluded, as is the 1996 original, which shares characters with Persona 2 but is not needed to follow it.
caveat: Persona 3, 4 and 5 are close to standalone: they share a setting, the Velvet Room and Igor, and almost nothing else. You can start with any of them and lose nothing. The Persona 2 duology is the exception — Eternal Punishment is a direct sequel to Innocent Sin in an altered timeline, and playing it first ruins both. Release order and chronology match throughout.

arcs.name: Persona 2
arcs.blurb: Two halves of one story about rumours becoming real in Sumaru City.

arcs.name: Modern Persona
arcs.blurb: Three separate school-year stories that share a structure and a mythology, not a plot.

games.title: Persona 2: Innocent Sin
games.note: Never released in the West on PlayStation — the 2011 PSP remake was its first English version and remains the only one. Several characters from the 1996 Persona return here, but the game explains them.

editions.name: Persona 2: Innocent Sin
editions.note: Japan-only; no official English release.

editions.name: Persona 2: Innocent Sin (PSP)
editions.note: First English version, with an added arranged soundtrack.

games.title: Persona 2: Eternal Punishment
games.note: Picks up directly from Innocent Sin's ending and spends its whole length on the consequences, so the order is not negotiable. The 2012 PSP remake was never translated, leaving the PS1 version as the only English option.

editions.name: Persona 2: Eternal Punishment
editions.note: Sold digitally as a PSone Classic.

editions.name: Persona 2: Eternal Punishment (PSP)
editions.note: Japan-only remake; no English version exists.

games.title: Persona 3
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Standalone; nothing before it is required. Reload remakes the original but drops the female protagonist route from Persona 3 Portable, and the epilogue chapter The Answer is sold as the separate Episode Aigis DLC.

editions.name: Persona 3 FES
editions.note: Original plus The Answer epilogue.

editions.name: Persona 3 Portable
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: The only version with the female protagonist route.

editions.name: Persona 3 Reload
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Full remake with modern combat; The Answer sold as DLC.

games.title: Persona 4
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set two years after Persona 3 and gestures at it once or twice, but tells a completely separate murder mystery. Golden adds an extra term, a new party member and a true ending route.

editions.name: Persona 4
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Persona 4 Golden
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Extended version, originally on Vita, now on everything.

games.title: Persona 5
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Shares no plot with Persona 3 or 4 and is the easiest entry point to find and run. Royal adds a third semester and a new confidant, and replaces the base game everywhere — do not buy the original Persona 5 alongside it.

editions.name: Persona 5
editions.note: Base version, superseded and no longer sold.

editions.name: Persona 5 Royal
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Adds a full extra semester and revised endgame.

name: Pikmin
scope: The four main games. The 3DS side-scroller Hey! Pikmin, the mobile app Pikmin Bloom and the Pikmin Short Movies are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. The only thing to know is that Pikmin 4 contains a side campaign, Olimar's Shipwreck Tale, that retells the premise of the first game from Olimar's side; the main campaign itself sits after Pikmin 3, though Nintendo has never been precise about the gap.

games.title: Pikmin
games.note: Olimar crashes on the planet, finds the Pikmin and has thirty in-game days to recover his ship's parts. That hard time limit is unique to this entry and is the main reason people bounce off it.

editions.name: Pikmin
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: New Play Control! Pikmin
editions.note: Pointer-control re-release.

editions.name: Pikmin 1+2
editions.note: Both GameCube games in one purchase, also sold individually.

games.title: Pikmin 2
games.note: Olimar returns to pay off his employer's debt, this time with Louie and no day limit. Adds the randomised underground caves, which make it much longer than the first game.

editions.name: Pikmin 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: New Play Control! Pikmin 2
editions.note: Pointer-control re-release.

editions.name: Pikmin 1+2
editions.note: Sold inside the two-game bundle or on its own.

games.title: Pikmin 3
games.note: A new crew from a starving planet arrives looking for food, and the search for Olimar ties it back to the first two games. Deluxe adds the side stories and co-op that the Wii U version lacked.

editions.name: Pikmin 3
editions.note: Original release; store closed.

editions.name: Pikmin 3 Deluxe
editions.note: Adds all DLC missions, side stories and two-player co-op campaign.

games.title: Pikmin 4
games.note: The Rescue Corps goes looking for Olimar, with a custom player character and a dog. Much gentler onboarding than the older games and the best place to start, even though it is chronologically last.

editions.name: Pikmin 4
editions.note: Only version; includes the Olimar's Shipwreck Tale side campaign.

name: Pillars of Eternity
scope: The two Obsidian party-based RPGs, with the White March expansions folded into the first game's row. The first-person Avowed, set in the same world but a different series, is excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. Deadfire begins with the direct consequences of the first game's ending and can import a save, so playing them out of order costs you the setup for the sequel's opening scene. The White March expansions slot into the first game's mid-campaign rather than after it.

games.title: Pillars of Eternity
games.note: Introduces Eora's soul mechanics and the Watcher, both of which Deadfire assumes you understand. The Definitive Edition includes both White March expansions, which are designed to be played partway through the main campaign.

editions.name: Pillars of Eternity
editions.note: Base game without the White March content.

editions.name: Pillars of Eternity: Complete Edition
editions.note: The console packaging of the same content; controller-adapted interface.

editions.name: Pillars of Eternity: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Base game plus White March Parts I and II and all bonus content.

games.title: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire
games.version: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire - Ultimate Edition
games.query: Pillars of Eternity II Deadfire Ultimate Edition
games.note: Opens moments after the first game's epilogue and moves the Watcher to the Deadfire Archipelago. The Ultimate Edition bundles the three story DLC; the console version ships with the turn-based combat mode as an option.

editions.name: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire
editions.note: Base game; the three DLC are sold separately.

editions.name: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire - Ultimate Edition
editions.note: Base game plus Beast of Winter, Seeker Slayer Survivor and The Forgotten Sanctum.

name: Portal
scope: The two mainline games; the Xbox Live Arcade re-release Portal: Still Alive, the free Aperture Desk Job short, and community mods are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order: Portal, then Portal 2 after an unspecified long stretch of Chell in stasis. Both share a universe with Half-Life, with Aperture Science positioned as Black Mesa's rival; the crossover is background detail, not required reading.

games.title: Portal
games.note: Short and self-contained, and the only sensible starting point. Portal with RTX is a free separate Steam entry for the same game with path-traced lighting and heavy hardware demands.

editions.name: Portal
editions.note: Originally in The Orange Box; the Steam version is the standard one.

editions.name: Portal: Companion Collection
editions.note: Bundles both games for Switch.

games.title: Portal 2
games.note: Set long after the first game, with a facility that has decayed in the meantime; it fills in Aperture's history through the underground test shafts. Includes a separate two-player co-op campaign.

editions.name: Portal 2
editions.note: Base release; the PC version supports the Perpetual Testing Initiative workshop levels.

editions.name: Portal: Companion Collection
editions.note: Switch bundle of both games, with split-screen co-op.

name: Prince of Persia
scope: The Sands of Time continuity and the modern revival, The Lost Crown. The 1989 and 1993 originals, the 3D Realms-era games and the 2008 reboot with its Epilogue DLC are excluded as separate continuities.
caveat: The Sands of Time games run in release order, with one insertion: The Forgotten Sands, released in 2010, is set between The Sands of Time and Warrior Within rather than after the trilogy. The 2008 game called simply Prince of Persia is a reboot with a different prince and no link to these, and The Lost Crown is a separate story again with a new protagonist, so it needs nothing from the earlier games.

arcs.name: Sands of Time
arcs.blurb: One prince, one dagger and the consequences of rewinding time, across four connected games.

arcs.name: Modern Revival
arcs.blurb: The Lost Crown, a standalone metroidvania with its own cast and no ties to the Sands continuity.

games.title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
games.version: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
games.query: Prince of Persia The Sands of Time
games.note: Where the Dagger of Time, Farah and the whole continuity begin. The PC port is old and needs compatibility settings; the HD console collections that once carried it are delisted.

editions.name: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
editions.note: The PC build is the only version still sold digitally.

editions.name: Prince of Persia Trilogy HD
editions.note: Upscaled bundle of all three; no longer purchasable.

games.title: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands
games.version: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands
games.query: Prince of Persia The Forgotten Sands
games.note: Released last of the four but set between The Sands of Time and Warrior Within, with the Prince visiting his brother's kingdom. A film tie-in and the least essential of the run; the Wii and PSP versions are different games entirely.

editions.name: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands
editions.note: The console and PC version; the Wii, PSP and DS releases share only the title.

games.title: Prince of Persia: Warrior Within
games.note: Seven years after The Sands of Time, with the Dahaka hunting the Prince for cheating death. A sharp tonal turn to heavy metal and gore; its true ending is the one The Two Thrones continues from.

editions.name: Prince of Persia: Warrior Within
editions.note: PC version still sold; unlocking the true ending requires collecting all life upgrades.

games.title: Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
games.version: Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
games.query: Prince of Persia The Two Thrones
games.note: Follows Warrior Within's true ending back to a besieged Babylon and closes the trilogy. Splits play between the Prince and the Dark Prince, and reconciles the tone of the first two games.

editions.name: Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
editions.note: PC version is the one still sold.

games.title: Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
games.version: Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: Prince of Persia The Lost Crown
games.note: A separate story with a new lead, Sargon, in a metroidvania structure rather than linear platforming. Nothing from the Sands games carries over; it is a clean starting point.

editions.name: Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: One release; the Mask of Darkness Divided DLC adds a post-game area.

name: Ratchet & Clank
scope: The Insomniac-developed main line: the four PS2 games, the 2016 remake, the four Future-era games and Rift Apart. The handheld and co-op spin-offs made by other studios (Size Matters, Secret Agent Clank, All 4 One, Full Frontal Assault, QForce) are excluded.
caveat: Chronology follows release order within each era. The one trap is the 2016 game: it is a remake of the 2002 original that follows the animated film rather than the original script, so it covers the same period with a different version of events. Insomniac has since treated the original 2002 story as what happened.

arcs.name: Original Run
arcs.blurb: Ratchet and Clank meet and build their partnership across four PS2 games.

arcs.name: Future Saga
arcs.blurb: The PS3 arc about Ratchet's Lombax heritage and Clank's origins.

arcs.name: Modern Era
arcs.blurb: The PS5 continuation, with Rivet and the dimensional threads left over from the Future saga.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank
games.note: The origin: Ratchet finds Clank and the two chase Chairman Drek across the Solana galaxy. Everything the PS2 arc does with their friendship starts from how badly they get along here.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Collection
editions.note: HD remasters of the first three games in one box.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank (PS2 Classic)
editions.note: Emulated original, the easiest modern purchase.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank (2016)
games.note: Retells the 2002 story as a framed flashback narrated by Captain Qwark, following the film's version of events rather than the original's. Modern controls and presentation make it the smoothest way in, but treat the 2002 game as the one the series follows.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank
editions.note: Runs at higher framerate on PS5 via backward compatibility.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando
games.note: Moves the pair to the Bogon galaxy shortly after the first game. Released as Locked and Loaded in Europe, which makes it easy to miss when searching a store.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando
editions.note: Original release; titled Locked and Loaded in PAL regions.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Collection
editions.note: HD remaster in the three-game collection.

editions.name: Going Commando (PS2 Classic)
editions.note: Emulated original, sold on its own.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal
games.version: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (PS2 Classic)
games.note: Back in Solana against Dr Nefarious, who becomes the series' recurring villain and returns in the Future arc and Rift Apart. The Qwark material here is set up by the first two games.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal
editions.note: Original release; Ratchet: Gladiator in PAL regions.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Collection
editions.note: HD remaster in the three-game collection.

editions.name: Up Your Arsenal (PS2 Classic)
editions.note: Emulated original, sold on its own.

games.title: Ratchet: Deadlocked
games.note: Ratchet is abducted into a televised deathmatch circuit; Clank sits the game out as a voice on the radio. It closes the PS2 era but the plot barely connects forward, so it is skippable if you want to move on to the Future arc.

editions.name: Ratchet: Deadlocked
editions.note: Original release; Ratchet: Gladiator in PAL regions.

editions.name: Ratchet: Deadlocked HD
editions.note: HD remaster; the only re-release, and PS3-bound.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction
games.version: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction
games.query: Ratchet & Clank Future Tools of Destruction
games.note: Starts the Lombax-heritage story and introduces Emperor Tachyon and the Zoni. Never remastered, so it is a PS3 purchase or a PS Plus Premium cloud stream.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction
editions.note: Only version; also streamable through PS Plus Premium.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: Quest for Booty
games.version: Ratchet & Clank Future: Quest for Booty
games.note: A short download-sized chapter about Ratchet searching for Clank after the Tools of Destruction ending. A Crack in Time recaps enough that you can skip it, but it is the direct bridge.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Future: Quest for Booty
editions.note: Digital-only; sold as a budget-priced short chapter.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time
games.version: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time
games.query: Ratchet & Clank A Crack in Time
games.note: The payoff for the Future arc: Clank's origin, the Great Clock, and the last word on Ratchet's search for the Lombaxes. Only assumes Tools of Destruction, not Quest for Booty.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time
editions.note: Only version; never remastered.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus
games.note: A short epilogue to the Future arc, set after A Crack in Time, dealing with the dimensional rifts that Rift Apart later picks up. Sold at a reduced price on release because of its length.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank: Into the Nexus
editions.note: Only version; PS3-bound like the rest of the Future arc.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart
games.note: Set after Into the Nexus, with Nefarious tearing holes between dimensions and Rivet as a second playable Lombax. It explains its own backstory well enough to work as a first game, though the Nefarious history lands harder after Up Your Arsenal.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart
editions.note: Original release, built around the PS5 SSD and DualSense.

editions.name: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart (PC)
editions.note: PC port with ray tracing and uncapped framerate; needs an SSD.

name: Red Dead
scope: Red Dead Redemption 2 then Red Dead Redemption. Red Dead Revolver shares a name and nothing else.
caveat: Chronology and play order agree, and both run backwards from release order: RDR2 (1899) precedes RDR (1911). RDR2’s epilogue hands you straight to RDR’s opening situation.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
games.note: 1899. Excellent PC version. The epilogue is effectively RDR1’s prologue — do not stop at the credits.

editions.name: Standard Edition
editions.note: Complete single-player story; the pricier editions add no story content.

editions.name: Special Edition
editions.note: Bank robbery mission and gameplay bonuses, not a real story expansion.

editions.name: Ultimate Edition
editions.note: Special Edition extras plus Online cosmetics and bonuses; no added story.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption 2 (PC)
editions.note: Same story with extra bounties, weapons and photo mode; best fidelity.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption
games.note: 1911. The 2024 PC release is a port of the 2023 console conversion, not a remaster — 4K and uncapped frame rate over 2010 assets, and widely criticised for the price. Undead Nightmare is included and is non-canon.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption
editions.note: Original release; Undead Nightmare arrived later as paid DLC.

editions.name: Undead Nightmare Collection
editions.note: Standalone disc of the DLC packs; does not include the main story.

editions.name: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Base game plus Undead Nightmare and the multiplayer packs on one disc.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption (2023 port)
editions.note: Straight port with Undead Nightmare; 30fps, no online, criticised as minimal.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption (PC)
editions.note: First PC version; includes Undead Nightmare, high framerates and resolutions.

editions.name: Red Dead Redemption (current-gen version)
editions.note: Native 4K60 with Undead Nightmare included; free upgrade from PS4 and Switch.

name: Resident Evil
scope: Mainline numbered entries plus RE0, Code: Veronica, RE7 and Village. No Revelations, Outbreak, Umbrella Corps or spin-off shooters.
caveat: RE3 and RE2 overlap. Nemesis begins 28 September 1998, a day before RE2, and ends after it — so RE3 sorts first by chronological start. Recommended play order is the reverse: RE2 then RE3, because RE3 assumes you have already seen the Raccoon City outbreak from Leon and Claire’s side.

arcs.name: The Umbrella Years
arcs.blurb: Raccoon City and the corporation that made it.

arcs.name: The Bioterror Decade
arcs.blurb: Umbrella is gone; the weapons it built are not.

arcs.name: The Winters Arc
arcs.blurb: First-person horror on a much smaller scale, with a new family at the centre.

games.title: Resident Evil 0
games.note: 23 July 1998, hours before RE1. HD Remaster (2016) on PC. A prequel written long after the fact and the easiest mainline entry to drop.

editions.name: Resident Evil Zero
editions.note: Original release, GameCube exclusive.

editions.name: Wii port
editions.note: Straight port with Wii controls; no added content.

editions.name: HD Remaster
editions.note: HD rework plus optional modern controls and Wesker Mode.

games.title: Resident Evil
games.note: Play the 2002 GameCube remake, sold on PC as the HD Remaster (2015) — not the 1996 original. Tank controls are optional in this version.

editions.name: Resident Evil
editions.note: Original release; tank controls and dated FMV.

editions.name: Director's Cut
editions.note: Adds Arrange mode, new camera angles and an auto-aim option.

editions.name: Resident Evil (REmake)
editions.note: Ground-up remake; adds the Lisa Trevor subplot.

editions.name: Wii Edition
editions.note: REmake with pointer aiming; no other content changes.

editions.name: HD Remaster
editions.note: REmake in HD with modern controls; the definitive way to play.

games.title: Resident Evil 3
games.note: Starts a day before RE2 and ends after it. The 2020 remake cuts large parts of the 1999 original — the clock tower, the park, most of the Nemesis encounters. Six hours, and the one remake with a real asterisk.

editions.name: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
editions.note: Original release; adds the live-selection choice system.

editions.name: GameCube port
editions.note: Straight port of the 1999 game.

editions.name: Resident Evil 3 (remake)
editions.note: RE Engine remake bundled with Resistance; cuts some 1999 content.

editions.name: Next-gen update
editions.note: Free upgrade to the remake; best-looking version of the story.

games.title: Resident Evil 2
games.note: 29 September 1998, mid-way through RE3’s timeline. The 2019 remake is the series benchmark. Two campaigns; the second run is a variant, not a sequel.

editions.name: Resident Evil 2
editions.note: Original two-disc release with the A/B scenario structure.

editions.name: GameCube port
editions.note: Late console port of the 1998 game; no new content.

editions.name: Resident Evil 2 (remake)
editions.note: RE Engine remake; superseded by the free next-gen update.

editions.name: Next-gen update
editions.note: Free upgrade to the remake with ray tracing and 4K/high frame rate.

games.title: Resident Evil – Code: Veronica X
games.note: Never released on PC. The 2011 HD version is Xbox 360, playable on Xbox One and Series via backward compatibility — the cleanest way to play it today. Closes the Wesker and Redfield threads the earlier games open.

editions.name: Code: Veronica
editions.note: Original release; lacks the added Wesker cutscenes.

editions.name: Code: Veronica X
editions.note: Adds roughly ten minutes of new Wesker cutscenes.

editions.name: GameCube port
editions.note: Port of Code: Veronica X; no further content changes.

editions.name: Code: Veronica X HD
editions.note: Widescreen HD version of Veronica X; the best available today.

games.title: Resident Evil 4
games.note: The 2023 remake is definitive. Separate Ways (paid DLC) runs Ada’s parallel route through the same events and is worth the add-on.

editions.name: Resident Evil 4
editions.note: Original release; no Separate Ways side campaign.

editions.name: PS2 version
editions.note: Adds the Separate Ways side campaign; visually downgraded.

editions.name: Ultimate HD Edition
editions.note: Proper HD rework of the 2005 game with all bonus content.

editions.name: Resident Evil 4 (remake)
editions.note: RE Engine remake; Separate Ways sold separately.

editions.name: Gold Edition
editions.note: Remake plus the Separate Ways DLC; the complete story package.

games.title: Resident Evil 5
games.note: Gold Edition on PC. Built around co-op; the solo AI partner is genuinely bad. Pays off the Wesker arc.

editions.name: Resident Evil 5
editions.note: Original release; missing both story episodes.

editions.name: Gold Edition
editions.note: Adds Lost in Nightmares and Desperate Escape; the full story.

editions.name: PS4 / Xbox One release
editions.note: Gold Edition content at 1080p60; no extra story.

editions.name: Switch port
editions.note: Gold Edition content, lowest-fidelity version.

games.title: Resident Evil 6
games.note: Four interlocking campaigns and the series’ low point. Nothing after it depends on it.

editions.name: Resident Evil 6
editions.note: Original release; extra modes arrived later as paid DLC.

editions.name: PC release
editions.note: Later PC port with improved visuals and mouse aiming.

editions.name: PS4 / Xbox One release
editions.note: Bundles every DLC mode at 1080p60; no story is left out.

editions.name: Switch port
editions.note: Same all-DLC content, weakest performance.

games.title: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard
games.note: Soft reboot, first-person, mostly self-contained. A legitimate alternative starting point if the 90s entries put you off.

editions.name: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard
editions.note: Original release; End of Zoe and Banned Footage sold separately.

editions.name: Gold Edition
editions.note: Adds Banned Footage Vol. 1-2, Not a Hero and End of Zoe.

editions.name: Next-gen update
editions.note: Free visual upgrade; content identical to Gold Edition.

games.title: Resident Evil Village
games.note: Direct sequel to RE7. The Gold Edition adds the Shadows of Rose epilogue, which later material builds on.

editions.name: Resident Evil Village
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Original release; ends before the Rose epilogue chapter.

editions.name: Gold Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Bundles Winters' Expansion with the Shadows of Rose story DLC.

games.title: Resident Evil Requiem
games.note: Ninth mainline entry, released 27 February 2026. Returns to Raccoon City with a new protagonist. Runtime left blank — the figures are still settling.

name: Resistance
scope: The three Insomniac console games plus the handheld side story Retribution. The Vita entry Burning Skies, made by another studio, is excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order except for Retribution, which shipped after Resistance 2 but is set in the gap between Fall of Man and Resistance 2. The whole series is stranded on PS3 and PSP with no remasters, so availability is the real problem, not the order.

games.title: Resistance: Fall of Man
games.note: 1951, with Nathan Hale landing in a Britain already lost to the Chimera. Sets up Hale's infection, which is the thread all three games hang on.

editions.name: Resistance: Fall of Man
editions.note: Only version; a PS3 launch title, never remastered.

games.title: Resistance: Retribution
games.note: Follows James Grayson through Western Europe in the months after Fall of Man, so it fills the gap before Resistance 2 despite coming out later. Skippable, though it explains parts of the Chimeran conversion process the console games gloss over.

editions.name: Resistance: Retribution
editions.note: PSP release; the digital version also downloads to PS3 and PS Vita.

games.title: Resistance 2
games.note: Two years on, with the Chimera in America and Hale's infection progressing. Its ending is the direct setup for Resistance 3 and is the one thing you cannot skip.

editions.name: Resistance 2
editions.note: Only version; the online co-op servers are long shut down.

games.title: Resistance 3
games.note: Four years after Resistance 2, with humanity beaten and Joseph Capelli as the lead instead of Hale. It closes the story, and the switch of protagonist only makes sense if you have seen how Resistance 2 ends.

editions.name: Resistance 3
editions.note: Only version; supported 3D and Move at launch, both optional.

name: Risen
scope: The three Piranha Bytes Risen RPGs. The studio's later Elex games, which share design DNA but no setting, are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order and each game follows on from the last. The lead changes: the first two star the same nameless hero, while Risen 3 hands the role to a different character and keeps the earlier protagonist as a supporting figure, which is the one thing that trips people up when they jump in at the third game.

games.title: Risen
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Faranga, the Inquisition and the titan ruins that the sequels build on. Closest in structure to the Gothic games the same studio made, and the tightest of the three; the 2023 console port is a straight conversion with modern controls.

editions.name: Risen
editions.note: Original release; still the standard version on PC.

editions.name: Risen (console port)
editions.platforms: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Same game with controller support and modern resolutions.

games.title: Risen 2: Dark Waters
games.note: Picks up years after the first game with the titans loose and the setting shifted to a pirate archipelago. The Gold Edition includes the Air Temple and Treasure Isle add-ons, which are otherwise separate purchases.

editions.name: Risen 2: Dark Waters
editions.note: Base game without the two add-ons.

editions.name: Risen 2: Dark Waters Gold Edition
editions.note: Base game plus Air Temple and Treasure Isle.

games.title: Risen 3: Titan Lords
games.note: Set after Risen 2 with a new protagonist whose soul is torn out in the opening. The Enhanced Edition improves textures and lighting and bundles all four DLC packs.

editions.name: Risen 3: Titan Lords
editions.note: Original release, DLC sold separately.

editions.name: Risen 3: Titan Lords - Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Visual overhaul plus all DLC in one package.

name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.
scope: The three original GSC games and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl; standalone mod projects such as Anomaly and Call of Chernobyl are excluded, since they are free community builds rather than releases.
caveat: Chronology is not release order: Clear Sky came out second but is a prequel set about a year before Shadow of Chernobyl. Call of Pripyat follows directly on from Shadow of Chernobyl's ending, and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 is set after all three. Playing in release order is still the common recommendation because Clear Sky is the roughest of the three.

games.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky
games.note: A prequel set a year before Shadow of Chernobyl, explaining how Strelok reached the centre of the Zone. It shipped in the worst state of the three and its faction war system rarely behaves; community patches are close to mandatory.

editions.name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky
editions.note: The GOG build is pre-patched to the final official version.

editions.name: Legends of the Zone Trilogy
editions.platforms: PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Console bundle of all three originals; no mod support.

games.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl
games.note: The starting point despite Clear Sky preceding it in-universe, since it introduces the Zone on its own terms. Most players add the ZRP patch or a light overhaul mod for stability on modern systems.

editions.name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl
editions.note: GOG and Steam versions are the 1.0006 final patch.

editions.name: Legends of the Zone Trilogy

games.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat
games.note: Follows on from Shadow of Chernobyl's ending, with a military investigation into the Zone. The most stable and best-structured of the three, and the base most large mod projects build on.

editions.name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat
editions.note: Final official patch on GOG and Steam.

editions.name: Legends of the Zone Trilogy

games.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl
games.note: Set after the original trilogy in a much larger single open Zone. It launched with substantial performance and A-Life problems that later patches worked through; check the current state before buying on lower-end hardware.

editions.name: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl
editions.note: Only version; also on Game Pass.

name: Saints Row
scope: The four numbered games, the standalone expansion Gat out of Hell, and the 2022 reboot. Mobile spin-offs and the Saints Row 2 mobile tie-in are excluded.
caveat: Chronology is release order within each continuity, but the 2022 game is a reboot: different characters, different city, no connection to the earlier arc. The original series also drifts hard in tone, from a straight crime story in the first two games to alien invasion and superpowers by the fourth, which is a deliberate escalation rather than a change of continuity.

arcs.name: Original Saints
arcs.blurb: Playa's rise from Stilwater gang leader to president, across four games and one expansion.

arcs.name: 2022 Reboot
arcs.blurb: A restart with a new crew in Santo Ileso, sharing nothing with the original continuity.

games.title: Saints Row
games.note: Stilwater, and the founding of the Third Street Saints. It never came to PC or PlayStation and never got a remaster, so Xbox backward compatibility is the only way to play it. Saints Row 2 recaps enough that skipping it is reasonable.

editions.name: Saints Row
editions.note: Only version; playable on Xbox One and Series through backward compatibility.

games.title: Saints Row 2
games.note: Picks up five years after the first game with the Saints scattered and Stilwater rebuilt. The story most fans rate highest, but the PC port is a poor conversion with known frame-pacing problems; community patches are effectively required.

editions.name: Saints Row 2
editions.note: The console versions run better; the PC version needs community fixes.

games.title: Saints Row: The Third
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The Saints move to Steelport as celebrities, and the series turns comic. It explains its own setup well enough to start here, which is what most people do given the state of the first two games.

editions.name: Saints Row: The Third
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Saints Row: The Third Remastered
editions.note: Rebuilt lighting and assets, with all DLC included.

games.title: Saints Row IV
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Follows The Third with the Boss as US president and most of the game inside an alien simulation. Started life as an expansion to The Third, which shows in the reused Steelport map.

editions.name: Saints Row IV
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Saints Row IV: Re-Elected
editions.note: Includes all 25 DLC packs and the two story expansions.

games.title: Saints Row: Gat out of Hell
games.version: Saints Row: Gat out of Hell
games.query: Saints Row Gat out of Hell
games.note: A short standalone set after Saints Row IV, with Johnny Gat in Hell. It closes out the original continuity and offers three endings, none of which the 2022 reboot follows up on.

editions.name: Saints Row: Gat out of Hell
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / PS3 / Xbox 360
editions.note: Standalone; does not require Saints Row IV.

games.title: Saints Row (2022)
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A clean restart in Santo Ileso with a new crew founding a new Saints. It shares a name and a logo with the earlier games and nothing else, so it can be played first or not at all.

editions.name: Saints Row
editions.note: Launched with significant bugs, patched since.

editions.name: Saints Row: Boss Factory Edition
editions.note: Post-patch version bundling the expansions and character creator content.

name: Science Adventure
scope: The five main Science Adventure visual novels released in English: Chaos;Head Noah, Steins;Gate, Steins;Gate 0, Chaos;Child and Robotics;Notes Elite. The spin-offs Steins;Gate: Linear Bounded Phenogram, Steins;Gate: My Darling's Embrace and Robotics;Notes DaSH are excluded.
caveat: Ordered by in-universe date, which is not release order. The series runs on worldlines: small changes push reality onto a different branch, and the games sit on different branches rather than in one clean line. Steins;Gate 0 is the sharpest case, being a midquel that plays out the branch created by one specific Steins;Gate ending before folding back into that game's true ending, so it only works after you have finished Steins;Gate.

games.title: Chaos;Head Noah
games.note: The first game in the series and the earliest in the timeline, set in 2009 Shibuya during the New Generation killings. Noah is the expanded version and the only one localised; the 2008 original never left Japan in English.

editions.name: Chaos;Head
editions.note: Japan-only original, without the added heroine routes.

editions.name: Chaos;Head Noah
editions.note: Expanded version; the English release arrived in 2022.

games.title: Steins;Gate
games.note: Set in Akihabara across July and August 2010, and the entry point for the whole series: it explains the worldline rules the others assume. Steins;Gate Elite replaces the sprite art with animated footage and cuts some scenes, so the standard version is the better first read.

editions.name: Steins;Gate
editions.note: The original visual novel; the 2016 Steam release is the usual PC version.

editions.name: Steins;Gate Elite
editions.note: Fully animated retelling; loses some interior monologue in the conversion.

games.title: Steins;Gate 0
games.note: Begins in late 2010 on the branch where Okabe gives up, and runs into 2011. It is a midquel, not a sequel: its ending leads directly into the true ending of Steins;Gate, and it spoils that game completely if read first.

editions.name: Steins;Gate 0
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Switch / PS Vita
editions.note: One version; the Steam release arrived in 2018.

games.title: Chaos;Child
games.note: Set in 2015, six years after Chaos;Head, in a Shibuya rebuilt after the earthquake that game ends with. It expects you to know Chaos;Head Noah's premise but not Steins;Gate.

editions.name: Chaos;Child
editions.platforms: Xbox One / PS4 / PS Vita / PC / Switch
editions.note: The English release reached PS4 and Vita in 2017 and Steam in 2019.

games.title: Robotics;Notes
games.note: The latest point on the timeline, in 2019 on Tanegashima, with a high school robotics club. Its ties to the other games are background documents and one recurring organisation; the sequel Robotics;Notes DaSH continues it a year later.

editions.name: Robotics;Notes
editions.note: Japan-only original.

editions.name: Robotics;Notes Elite
editions.note: Expanded version; the English release arrived in 2020.

name: Shenmue
scope: The three games following Ryo Hazuki. The anime adaptation and the Dreamcast-era Shenmue Passport disc are excluded.
caveat: One continuous story told in release order, with each game picking up almost exactly where the last ended. The important thing to know is that it is unfinished: Shenmue III ends mid-journey and no fourth game exists, so the story has no conclusion.

games.title: Shenmue
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Winter 1986 in Yokosuka, beginning with the murder of Ryo's father. The HD collection is a light port rather than a remaster, so the original's pacing and voice acting are intact.

editions.name: Shenmue
editions.note: Original release, spread over four discs.

editions.name: Shenmue I & II
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Both games in one purchase with widescreen and a choice of English or Japanese audio.

games.title: Shenmue II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Continues directly in Hong Kong and Guilin, and is much larger than the first game. The Dreamcast version never released in North America; the Xbox port did, with an English dub the HD version also carries.

editions.name: Shenmue II
editions.note: Japan and Europe only.

editions.name: Shenmue II (Xbox)
editions.note: The North American release; adds an English dub.

editions.name: Shenmue I & II
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Bundled with the first game; not sold separately.

games.title: Shenmue III
games.note: Picks up immediately after Shenmue II in rural China, eighteen years after that game shipped. It advances the plot very little and ends without resolution, which is the main complaint against it.

editions.name: Shenmue III
editions.note: Crowdfunded; both story DLC packs are sold separately.

name: Shin Megami Tensei
scope: The mainline numbered entries, the Digital Devil Saga duology and the Raidou Kuzunoha pair. Persona, Devil Survivor, Soul Hackers and the Devil Children spin-offs have their own pages or no shared continuity, and are excluded.
caveat: Almost nothing in this series connects. Each mainline game is a separate apocalypse in a separate world, and the recurring elements are demons, the demon negotiation system and the same set of law-versus-chaos questions. Only three pairings are genuinely continuous: Shin Megami Tensei I into II, Digital Devil Saga 1 into 2, and Raidou 1 into 2. Availability is the real ordering trap — the first two mainline games have no current English release at all, and both 3DS entries died with the eShop.

arcs.name: Mainline
arcs.blurb: The numbered games, each a self-contained apocalypse except for the first two.

arcs.name: Digital Devil Saga
arcs.blurb: One story split across two games about tribes who devour each other to survive.

arcs.name: Raidou Kuzunoha
arcs.blurb: A demon-summoning detective in a Taisho-era Japan, across two connected cases.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei
games.note: Sets the law-chaos template the whole series runs on. An English iOS port existed briefly and was delisted, so there is currently no official way to buy it in English.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei
editions.note: The base version; every later port is Japanese-only or delisted.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei II
games.note: A direct sequel set decades after the first game in the same ruined Tokyo, and the only mainline entry that requires its predecessor. Never officially released in English in any form.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei II
editions.note: No official English release on any platform.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne
games.version: Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne HD Remaster
games.query: Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne HD Remaster
games.note: A separate world with no link to the first two games. The HD Remaster is based on the Maniax edition, and the Dante guest content from the original Western release is now paid DLC alongside a Raidou alternative.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei: Nocturne
editions.note: Western release was the Maniax version with Dante.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne HD Remaster
editions.note: Higher resolution, added voice acting, optional easier difficulty.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei IV
games.note: Its own world again, unconnected to Nocturne. The 3DS eShop has closed, so a cartridge is the only way to get it.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei IV
editions.note: Only ever released on 3DS; digital version delisted.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse
games.note: Begins partway through Shin Megami Tensei IV with a new protagonist and continues past its ending, so it only works after IV. Same 3DS-only availability problem.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse
editions.note: 3DS cartridge only; eShop closed.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei V
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Standalone and the easiest entry to actually buy and run. Vengeance contains the original 2021 storyline and a longer alternative route, and fully replaces the Switch-only release.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei V
editions.note: Original release; one storyline only, with frame rate problems.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Both routes, revised map and much better performance.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga
games.query: Shin Megami Tensei Digital Devil Saga
games.note: The first half of a single story that stops mid-plot; treat the two games as one purchase. Uses the Nocturne engine but shares no world with it.

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga
editions.note: Original disc release.

editions.name: Digital Devil Saga (PS2 Classic)

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga 2
games.query: Shin Megami Tensei Digital Devil Saga 2

editions.name: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga 2
editions.note: Original disc release.

editions.name: Digital Devil Saga 2 (PS2 Classic)
