games.query: Raidou Remastered The Mystery of the Soulless Army

editions.note: Original release with stiff real-time combat.

editions.name: Raidou Remastered: The Mystery of the Soulless Army
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox Series / Switch

games.title: Devil Summoner 2: Raidou Kuzunoha vs. King Abaddon
games.version: Devil Summoner 2: Raidou Kuzunoha vs. King Abaddon
games.query: Devil Summoner 2 Raidou Kuzunoha vs King Abaddon

editions.name: Devil Summoner 2: Raidou Kuzunoha vs. King Abaddon

name: Silent Hill
scope: The eight main-line survival horror games from Silent Hill through Silent Hill f. The Book of Memories spin-off, the Shattered Memories reimagining, the mobile titles and the P.T. demo are excluded.
caveat: Most entries are self-contained stories that share a town and a mythology rather than a cast, so chronology matters less here than in most series. The two real links are Origins, a prequel to the first game, and Silent Hill 3, a direct sequel to it. Silent Hill f is set in 1960s Japan, which puts it earliest by date while connecting to nothing else.

games.title: Silent Hill f
games.note: Set in a rural Japanese town in the 1960s, the earliest date in the series. It shares the series' underlying mythology but none of its characters or locations, so it can be played at any point.

editions.name: Silent Hill f
editions.note: Single release; written by Ryukishi07.

games.title: Silent Hill: Origins
games.note: A prequel set shortly before the first game, covering how Alessa came to be burned. It explains events the first game already implies, so it works better as a follow-up than an opener, and it has no modern rerelease.

editions.name: Silent Hill: Origins
editions.note: Original handheld release.

editions.name: Silent Hill: Origins (PS2)
editions.note: Console port with better controls; still the easiest copy to find.

games.title: Silent Hill
games.note: Harry Mason's search for his daughter, and the only entry Silent Hill 3 requires you to know. Still PS1-only; the PS3 and PSP digital versions were delisted, so emulation or a disc are the options.

editions.name: Silent Hill
editions.note: The only version; the PS Store classic release is no longer sold.

games.title: Silent Hill 2
games.note: Standalone: James Sunderland's story shares no characters with the first game, which makes it the usual entry point. The 2024 Bloober Team remake keeps the script and restages everything else, and it is the only version currently sold.

editions.name: Silent Hill 2
editions.note: Original; the PC port is out of print and needs community patches.

editions.name: Silent Hill HD Collection
editions.note: Reworked from incomplete source code; widely regarded as the worst version.

editions.name: Silent Hill 2 (2024)
editions.note: Full remake with over-the-shoulder combat; the Xbox version arrived in 2025.

games.title: Silent Hill 3
games.note: A direct sequel to the first game, set seventeen years later, and the one entry that genuinely requires playing another first. The HD Collection version has recast voices and rendering faults, so the PS2 disc or the out-of-print PC release are the better options.

editions.name: Silent Hill 3
editions.note: The reference version.

editions.name: Silent Hill 3 (PC)
editions.note: Out of print; needs fan patches to run on modern hardware.

editions.name: Silent Hill HD Collection
editions.note: Fog and lighting errors plus a recast Heather.

games.title: Silent Hill 4: The Room
games.note: Set mostly in an apartment in nearby Ashfield rather than the town itself, and connected to the others only through Walter Sullivan, who is named in passing in Silent Hill 2. GOG relisted the PC version in 2020, making it the most available older entry.

editions.name: Silent Hill 4: The Room
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Silent Hill 4: The Room (GOG)
editions.note: Prepatched to run on modern Windows; the only entry sold digitally at a low price.

games.title: Silent Hill: Homecoming
games.note: The first entry made by a Western studio, set in Shepherd's Glen rather than Silent Hill and leaning on combat over dread. It touches the cult from the earlier games but adds nothing the later entries build on.

editions.name: Silent Hill: Homecoming
editions.note: Steam version is the only one still sold; needs a controller.

games.title: Silent Hill: Downpour
games.note: The last game before the series went dormant, following a convict named Murphy Pendleton; entirely standalone. Never ported past the PS3 and 360, and the frame rate was rough on both.

editions.name: Silent Hill: Downpour
editions.note: The only version; no digital rerelease.

name: Sly Cooper
scope: The four main games: Thievius Raccoonus, Band of Thieves, Honor Among Thieves and Thieves in Time. The Vita minigame compilation Bentley's Hackpack is excluded.
caveat: Chronology is release order, and each game picks up directly from the last one's ending. Thieves in Time sends Sly back through his ancestors' eras, but its frame story sits after Honor Among Thieves, so it stays last. It also ends on an unresolved cliffhanger that has never been followed up.

games.title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
games.note: Introduces the Cooper family history, the Thievius Raccoonus itself and the Fiendish Five. Short and much more linear than the later games, but the family lore it sets up drives all three sequels.

editions.name: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
editions.note: Original release; Sly Raccoon in PAL regions.

editions.name: The Sly Collection
editions.note: HD remasters of the first three games in one purchase.

editions.name: The Sly Collection (Vita)
editions.note: Handheld port with some performance compromises.

games.title: Sly 2: Band of Thieves
games.note: Two years after the first game, chasing the scattered parts of Clockwerk. This is where the series switches to open hub levels with all three characters playable, and it is the one most people rate highest.

editions.name: Sly 2: Band of Thieves
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Sly Collection
editions.note: HD remaster, sold inside the three-game collection.

games.title: Sly 3: Honor Among Thieves
games.note: Follows straight on from Sly 2, with the gang recruiting for the Cooper Vault job. Its prologue is a flash-forward that the game returns to later, so the opening is deliberately out of sequence.

editions.name: Sly 3: Honor Among Thieves
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Sly Collection
editions.note: HD remaster, sold inside the three-game collection.

games.title: Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time
games.note: Made by Sanzaru rather than Sucker Punch, set after Honor Among Thieves and built around time-travelling to Cooper ancestors. It assumes you remember how Sly 3 ended, and its own ending is left hanging.

editions.name: Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time
editions.note: Released on both at once with cross-buy and cross-save.

name: Sonic the Hedgehog
scope: The story-relevant main-line games across the Genesis era, the Dreamcast-era Adventure games and the modern 3D entries. The handheld Advance and Rush series, the racing games, Sonic 4, the Storybook games and the Boom sub-series are excluded.
caveat: Continuity here is loose by design: most games open with the world reset and only a handful reference each other directly. Playing in release order works, and that is what this list does within each era. Two ordering traps: Sonic CD's place among the Genesis games has never been settled, and Sonic the Hedgehog (2006) ends by erasing its own events from the timeline, so nothing after it acknowledges that game happened.

arcs.name: Classic Era
arcs.blurb: The Genesis games and their modern sequel, built around the Chaos Emeralds and Angel Island.

arcs.name: Adventure Era
arcs.blurb: The Dreamcast-era shift to 3D and voiced story, running through to the 2006 reboot attempt.

arcs.name: Modern Era
arcs.blurb: The post-2008 games, which mostly drop the serialised plotting for standalone stories.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The original, and the only appearance of the Green Hill and Chaos Emerald ideas everything later reuses. Origins is the current way to buy it; the older standalone Genesis ports were pulled from sale when it launched.

editions.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
editions.note: Original release; no spin dash.

editions.name: Sonic Origins Plus
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Widescreen remasters of four Genesis games plus playable Amy and the Game Gear library.

games.title: Sonic CD
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Introduces Amy Rose and Metal Sonic, both series regulars afterwards. Where it belongs among the Genesis games has been argued for thirty years; it is placed after the first game here, which is the most common reading.

editions.name: Sonic CD
editions.note: Original release; two different soundtracks by region.

editions.name: Sonic Origins Plus
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Includes both soundtracks as a toggle.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Adds Tails and the spin dash, and is the most approachable of the Genesis games for a newcomer. Its ending leads straight into Sonic 3.

editions.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Sonic Origins Plus
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Includes the Hidden Palace zone cut from the original.

games.title: Sonic 3 & Knuckles
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles were split halves of one game and are best played joined, which is how Origins presents them. Introduces Knuckles and the Master Emerald, both central to the Adventure games.

editions.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 3 / Sonic & Knuckles
editions.note: Two cartridges; the second locked onto the first to combine them.

editions.name: Sonic Origins Plus
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Presents the combined game; some original music was replaced for licensing reasons.

games.title: Sonic Mania
games.note: A new Genesis-style game set after Sonic 3 & Knuckles, made by developers from the fan-remaster scene. Its ending connects to Sonic Forces, which released the same year.

editions.name: Sonic Mania
editions.note: Base release.

editions.name: Sonic Mania Plus
editions.note: Adds Mighty and Ray plus an Encore mode with remixed stages.

games.title: Sonic Adventure
games.note: The first 3D entry and the start of the voiced, multi-character storytelling the series kept for a decade. The DX port available today has worse lighting and character models than the Dreamcast original, and the PC version needs community patches to look right.

editions.name: Sonic Adventure
editions.note: Original release; still the best-looking version.

editions.name: Sonic Adventure DX
editions.note: Port of the GameCube version; the only one still sold.

games.title: Sonic Adventure 2
games.note: Introduces Shadow and the backstory around Gerald Robotnik that later games keep returning to, which makes it the most load-bearing entry in the series. Splits into hero and dark campaigns that converge.

editions.name: Sonic Adventure 2
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Sonic Adventure 2
editions.note: HD port of the GameCube version; Battle mode content is paid DLC.

games.title: Sonic Heroes
games.note: Follows Adventure 2 and sets up Shadow's amnesia plot, but the story is thin and most of the game is the same four stages replayed with different teams. Never rereleased on a modern platform.

editions.name: Sonic Heroes
editions.note: The GameCube and Xbox versions run better than the PS2 one.

games.title: Shadow the Hedgehog
games.note: Resolves Shadow's origin from Adventure 2 across a branching path structure with ten endings, only one of which is canon. Never rereleased, and the 2024 Shadow Generations campaign covers the same character ground more cleanly.

editions.name: Shadow the Hedgehog
editions.note: The only version; the branching structure requires many replays to see the true ending.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog (2006)
games.note: An attempted reboot released unfinished, with long loading screens and frequent bugs. Its ending undoes the entire game within the fiction, so nothing afterwards refers to it; safe to skip entirely.

editions.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
editions.note: The only version; never patched, never rereleased.

games.title: Sonic Unleashed
games.note: Introduces the boost-style daytime stages that the next several games are built on, alternating with slower night-time combat sections. The PS3 and 360 version is the real one; the Wii and PS2 release is a different, smaller game.

editions.name: Sonic Unleashed
editions.note: The HD version; playable on Xbox consoles through backward compatibility.

editions.name: Sonic Unleashed (Wii / PS2)
editions.note: Separate build with different stages and no hub exploration.

games.title: Sonic Colors
games.note: A lighter, standalone story set on an amusement park in orbit, and the point where the series moved away from serialised plotting. Ultimate is the only current version; it launched with a number of visual bugs that were later patched.

editions.name: Sonic Colors
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Sonic Colors: Ultimate
editions.note: Remaster at 60fps with an added Rival Rush mode.

games.title: Sonic Generations
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: An anniversary game that revisits stages from across the series with both Genesis-style and boost-style Sonic, which makes it a reasonable summary for a newcomer. The 2024 release pairs it with a substantial new Shadow campaign.

editions.name: Sonic Generations
editions.note: Original release; the 3DS version is a separate, smaller game.

editions.name: Sonic X Shadow Generations
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Remaster bundled with Shadow Generations, a new campaign of comparable length.

games.title: Sonic Forces
games.note: Follows on from Sonic Mania's ending and features a custom character alongside Sonic. Very short, and the story it sets up has not been continued.

editions.name: Sonic Forces
editions.note: The only version; the Episode Shadow prologue is included.

games.title: Sonic Frontiers
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The most recent main-line entry and the first to use open zones instead of linear stages. It leans on the supporting cast's history from the Adventure games more than the games immediately before it did.

editions.name: Sonic Frontiers
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Three free content updates added a harder final story chapter.

name: Splatoon
scope: The three main games and their story content, including the Octo Expansion for Splatoon 2 and Side Order for Splatoon 3. The mobile companion app and the Splatoon manga are excluded.
caveat: Chronology is release order, with roughly two years passing between each game in-universe. The story only exists in the single-player Hero Mode and the paid expansions; the multiplayer that most people play carries none of it, so the plot is easy to miss entirely.

games.title: Splatoon
games.note: Hero Mode introduces the Great Zapfish theft, Callie and Marie, and the DJ Octavio conflict the sequels keep returning to. Wii U only, the store is closed and the online services ended in 2024, so it is a used disc and the campaign alone.

editions.name: Splatoon
editions.note: Only version; multiplayer servers are shut down.

games.title: Splatoon 2
games.note: Two years on, with Callie missing and Marie recruiting you. The Octo Expansion DLC is the part that matters most for the story: it introduces Eight and the material Splatoon 3 builds directly on.

editions.name: Splatoon 2
editions.note: Base game; Hero Mode only.

editions.name: Splatoon 2 + Octo Expansion
editions.note: Adds the 80-stage Octo Expansion, which carries the important story beats.

games.title: Splatoon 3
games.note: Set in the Splatlands two years after Splatoon 2, though the campaign returns to the Octavio thread and resolves it. The Side Order DLC follows Eight from the Octo Expansion, so that expansion is close to required reading for it.

editions.name: Splatoon 3
editions.note: Base game with the Return of the Mammalians campaign.

editions.name: Splatoon 3: Expansion Pass
editions.note: Adds Inkopolis as a hub and the Side Order roguelike campaign.

name: Splinter Cell
scope: The six console and PC games starring Sam Fisher, from the 2002 original through Blacklist. The handheld-only Essentials, the 3DS remake of Chaos Theory and the mobile entries are excluded.
caveat: Chronology follows release order; each game is a new Third Echelon assignment a year or two after the last. The one real trap is Double Agent, which shipped as two different games in 2006: the Xbox 360 and PC version and the PlayStation 2 and original Xbox version have different missions and a different ending, and the 360 version is the one the series treats as canon.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
games.note: Sam Fisher's recruitment into Third Echelon and the template for the whole series. Strict checkpointing and no way to move bodies quickly; playable on Xbox hardware through backwards compatibility.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
editions.note: The PC build is the version still sold; the Xbox original is the better-looking one.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
games.version: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
games.note: Follows the first game with an Indonesian bioterrorism plot. The hardest entry to obtain legitimately: it was never sold on Steam or the Ubisoft store, so a disc or Xbox backwards compatibility is the only route.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
editions.note: Only release; no digital PC version exists.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory
games.version: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory
games.note: The best entry point: it opens with enough briefing to stand alone and has the series' most flexible level design and its knife. Story-wise it continues the Third Echelon thread but does not depend on the first two games.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory
editions.note: PC version, still sold; needs a compatibility fix for widescreen.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Double Agent
games.version: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Double Agent
games.note: Sam goes undercover after a personal loss, and the fallout drives Conviction. Two different games shipped under this title in 2006; the Xbox 360 and PC version, which is the one sold digitally, is the canonical one.

editions.name: Splinter Cell: Double Agent (version 1)
editions.note: Different missions and ending, built on the older engine.

editions.name: Splinter Cell: Double Agent (version 2)
editions.note: The canonical version, with the trust meter and the JBA HQ hub.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction
games.note: Sam off the leash and hunting the people behind Double Agent's loss. A deliberate turn towards action, with mark-and-execute and cover shooting replacing much of the patience; the co-op prologue is a separate campaign set before the main story.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction
editions.note: Only release; runs on Xbox consoles via backwards compatibility.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Blacklist
games.note: The last full game in the series, with Sam running the new Fourth Echelon after Conviction. It restores stealth options Conviction dropped and scores each mission on how quietly you played; Sam is voiced by a different actor here.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Blacklist
editions.note: One release; the Deluxe version adds gear and a bonus mission.

name: Star Wars Jedi
scope: The two Cal Kestis games from Respawn. Other Star Wars action titles, including the older Jedi Knight series, are unrelated and excluded.
caveat: Two games, release order, five in-universe years apart, with the same protagonist and most of the same crew. Fallen Order is set five years after Revenge of the Sith and Survivor five years after that. Survivor opens on the assumption you know who everyone is and picks up unresolved threads immediately, and it can import a Fallen Order save for cosmetics. A third game has been confirmed in development but has not been released.

games.title: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The starting point, and it needs no Star Wars knowledge beyond the films. Runs on last-generation consoles, unlike its sequel.

editions.name: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
editions.note: Original release, with frame rate issues on base consoles.

editions.name: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Free current-generation update added 60fps and faster loading.

games.title: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
games.note: Direct sequel set five years later, larger and more open than Fallen Order. Current-generation only, and its PC release had serious performance problems at launch that were patched over the following year.

editions.name: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
editions.note: The only release; no last-generation version exists.

name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
scope: The two single-player BioWare and Obsidian games. The MMO Star Wars: The Old Republic continues the same era but is a live service game and is excluded.
caveat: Two games, in release order, five in-universe years apart — there is no ordering trap here. The Sith Lords opens by referencing the first game's ending and lets you set which of its outcomes happened, so playing it first costs you that. The larger caveat is The Sith Lords itself: it shipped unfinished, with a rushed final act, and the community restoration mod is the usual fix on PC. A remake of the first game was announced in 2021 and has since changed developers with no release date; treat it as unreleased and uncertain.

games.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
games.version: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
games.platform: PC / Switch / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic
games.note: Set roughly four thousand years before the films, with no connection to them beyond the setting. The PC version is the most flexible thanks to widescreen and interface mods; the 2021 Switch port is the most convenient.

editions.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
editions.note: Original release; the Xbox version runs on Xbox One and Series via backward compatibility.

editions.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
editions.platforms: PC / Switch / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Aspyr's maintained version; the Switch port added touch and gyro controls.

games.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
games.version: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
games.platform: PC / Switch / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II The Sith Lords
games.note: Set five years after the first game and it asks you to define how that game ended, so play them in order. Cut from the original release is a substantial chunk of the ending, restored on PC by a long-running community mod; the Switch version cannot use it.

editions.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
editions.note: Original release, shipped with the final act largely unfinished.

editions.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
editions.platforms: PC / Switch / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Updated PC release with widescreen and mod support; Switch port followed in 2022.

name: StarCraft
scope: StarCraft and Brood War, the three StarCraft II campaigns and the Nova Covert Ops mission packs; the cancelled console spin-off StarCraft: Ghost and the co-op-only Commanders content are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order throughout, and every entry continues the previous one's plot directly with the same cast. The only oddity is packaging: StarCraft II was sold as three separate campaign releases rather than three games, each following one of the three races.

games.title: StarCraft
games.note: Three campaigns introducing the Terrans, Zerg and Protoss. Blizzard made the original free in 2017; Remastered is the paid upgrade that adds widescreen and high-resolution art without changing the balance.

editions.name: StarCraft
editions.note: Free from Blizzard, but limited to the original 640x480 presentation.

editions.name: StarCraft: Remastered
editions.note: Widescreen, 4K art and matchmaking; includes Brood War.

games.title: StarCraft: Brood War
games.note: Picks up immediately after the base campaigns and finishes their story; StarCraft II assumes its ending, not the original's. Bundled with Remastered rather than sold on its own.

editions.name: StarCraft: Brood War
editions.note: Original expansion, free alongside the base game.

editions.name: StarCraft: Remastered
editions.note: Brood War is included in the Remastered purchase.

games.title: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
games.note: Four years after Brood War, following Jim Raynor. Free since 2017, which makes it the easiest entry point, and it recaps enough of the first game to stand alone.

editions.name: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
editions.note: Free campaign; multiplayer and co-op are part of the same client.

games.title: StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm
games.version: StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm
games.query: StarCraft II Heart of the Swarm
games.note: Continues straight from Wings of Liberty's ending with Kerrigan as the lead. Requires no separate base game any more, since the client is free.

editions.name: StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm
editions.note: Campaign unlock; also sold in the Campaign Collection bundle.

games.title: StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void
games.version: StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void
games.query: StarCraft II Legacy of the Void
games.note: The Protoss campaign and the conclusion of the story begun in 1998. Includes a short prologue set of missions and an epilogue that closes out all three races' arcs.

editions.name: StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void
editions.note: Campaign unlock; the Campaign Collection bundles it with the other two.

games.title: StarCraft II: Nova Covert Ops
games.note: Nine missions across three packs, set after Legacy of the Void and the latest point on the timeline. Self-contained and skippable, but it is the only continuation the series has had.

editions.name: StarCraft II: Nova Covert Ops
editions.note: Sold as a bundle of all three mission packs.

name: Suikoden
scope: The five numbered entries, which share one world, one set of True Runes and a handful of very long-lived recurring characters. Suikoden Tactics, Tierkreis and the mobile games are excluded, as is the spiritual successor Eiyuden Chronicle.
caveat: Release order and in-universe order diverge sharply: Suikoden IV is set roughly 150 years before the first game and Suikoden V about six years before it. Only I, II and III form a tight sequence — II follows I by three years and can import its save, and III is fifteen years after II. Playing in release order works fine because the prequels are written to be read after the fact. The 2025 HD Remaster fixed the biggest availability problem, but III, IV and V are still PS2-era and have never been re-released.

games.title: Suikoden IV
games.note: Set about 150 years before the first game and connected mainly through the Rune of Punishment. Widely considered the weakest entry, largely because of its sea travel and encounter rate, and the easiest to skip.

editions.name: Suikoden IV
editions.note: The only release; no remaster.

games.title: Suikoden V
games.note: Set six years before the first game in a different country, and a return to the political scale of Suikoden II. Long, and PS2-only with no digital release.

editions.name: Suikoden V
editions.note: The only release; loading times are slow on original hardware.

games.title: Suikoden
games.version: Suikoden I & II HD Remaster: Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Short by the standards of the genre and the intended starting point. The HD Remaster redraws the sprites and backgrounds, adds auto-battle and a new translation, and carries your completed save into Suikoden II.

editions.name: Suikoden
editions.note: Original release; the PSP and Saturn ports were Japan-only.

editions.name: Suikoden I & II HD Remaster
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Both games remastered together with save transfer intact.

games.title: Suikoden II
games.version: Suikoden I & II HD Remaster: Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set three years after the first game, with its protagonist as a recruitable character if you import a clear save. The save transfer is the main reason to play them in order rather than jumping straight here.

editions.name: Suikoden II
editions.note: Original release; long one of the most expensive PS1 games to buy secondhand.

editions.name: Suikoden I & II HD Remaster
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Sold only as a pair with Suikoden.

games.title: Suikoden III
games.note: Fifteen years after Suikoden II and the direct continuation of its story, told through three protagonists whose chapters interleave. Never re-released, which leaves the trilogy's ending stranded on PS2.

editions.name: Suikoden III
editions.note: The only release; not part of the HD Remaster.

name: Tales of
scope: The two Tales sub-series that are genuine direct sequels: Symphonia with Dawn of the New World, and Xillia with Xillia 2. Tales of Phantasia is excluded even though Symphonia is set in its distant past — the link is background lore, and Phantasia's only English versions are a GBA cartridge and a phone port.
caveat: Tales games are almost all standalone; the series name is a brand, not a timeline. Only these two pairs continue directly, and in both cases the sequel follows the original by a few years with returning characters. Release order matches in-universe order. The bigger problem is hardware: three of the four games below are stuck on PS3 or Wii with no modern release.

arcs.name: Symphonia
arcs.blurb: Two worlds joined, and the mess left behind two years later.

arcs.name: Xillia
arcs.blurb: Two protagonists across one story, and a sequel set a year on in a parallel world.

games.title: Tales of Symphonia
games.note: Self-contained and the most widely played Tales game. The PC release is the HD version and runs well after patching; the 2023 console Remastered is the same content but locked to 30fps.

editions.name: Tales of Symphonia
editions.note: The PS2 version added content but was Japan-only.

editions.name: Tales of Symphonia (PC)
editions.note: HD version with all the PS2 additions; rough at launch, since patched.

editions.name: Tales of Symphonia Remastered
editions.note: Console port of the same HD version, capped at 30fps.

games.title: Tales of Symphonia: Dawn of the New World
games.note: Set two years after Symphonia with a new lead and the original cast as guests. Left out of the 2023 Remastered, so the PS3 Chronicles collection or a Wii disc are the only ways to play it.

editions.name: Tales of Symphonia: Dawn of the New World
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Tales of Symphonia Chronicles
editions.note: Bundles both games in HD; the only modern-ish version of the sequel.

games.title: Tales of Xillia
games.note: Two selectable protagonists whose routes cover the same events from different angles; one playthrough is enough for the story. Never released on anything but PS3.

editions.name: Tales of Xillia
editions.note: The only release; English version arrived in 2013.

games.title: Tales of Xillia 2
games.note: Set a year after Xillia with a new protagonist and the full returning cast, and it spoils the first game constantly. Also PS3-only.

editions.name: Tales of Xillia 2
editions.note: The only release; English version arrived in 2014.

name: Tekken
scope: The eight numbered games, which together tell the Mishima family story. The Tag Tournament games are exhibition titles outside continuity and are excluded, as are the handheld spin-offs and Tekken Revolution.
caveat: Chronology matches release order, each game following the last King of Iron Fist Tournament. The one thing to know is that the story is told in fragments: pre-2015 entries deliver it through short per-character endings rather than a single narrative, and Tekken 7 fills in decades of Mishima backstory through flashbacks placed long before every other game.

games.title: Tekken
games.note: The first tournament, won by Kazuya, who then throws his father Heihachi off a cliff. Story exists only as short character endings, and later games restate what happened here.

editions.name: Tekken
editions.note: The PS1 version added extra modes; some PlayStation subscription tiers carry it as a classic.

games.title: Tekken 2
games.note: Heihachi returns and throws Kazuya into a volcano, reversing the first game. Introduces Jun Kazama, whose disappearance drives the next several entries.

editions.name: Tekken 2
editions.note: The PS1 release is the common version; also offered on some PlayStation subscription tiers.

games.title: Tekken 3
games.note: Set nineteen years after Tekken 2 and shifts the lead to Jin Kazama, who remains the protagonist through Tekken 8. Widely held to be the best of the PS1 fighting games.

editions.name: Tekken 3
editions.note: The PS1 conversion added Tekken Force and Tekken Ball modes.

games.title: Tekken 4
games.note: Brings Kazuya back and puts the three generations of Mishimas in the same tournament. Unpopular at the time for its uneven stages and wall mechanics, and never rereleased.

editions.name: Tekken 4
editions.note: The only home version.

games.title: Tekken 5
games.note: Introduces Jinpachi Mishima and the Devil Gene plot the later games run on. Dark Resurrection is the expanded version with a larger roster; the PS3 digital release has been delisted.

editions.name: Tekken 5
editions.note: The PS2 disc also includes emulated versions of the first three games.

editions.name: Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection
editions.note: Extra characters and stages; the PS3 download is no longer sold.

games.title: Tekken 6
games.note: Jin now runs the Mishima Zaibatsu and has declared war on the world. Its Scenario Campaign is the longest story content in the series before Tekken 7, though it plays as a repetitive beat-em-up.

editions.name: Tekken 6
editions.note: The console versions include the Bloodline Rebellion update.

games.title: Tekken 7
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The first entry with a single narrative story mode, resolving the Heihachi and Kazuya feud that started the series. Much of it is flashback covering events decades before Tekken 1, so it doubles as the saga's backstory.

editions.name: Tekken 7
editions.note: Base game; three season passes were sold on top.

editions.name: Tekken 7 Definitive Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Includes every DLC character and stage.

games.title: Tekken 8
games.note: Continues directly from Tekken 7 with Jin against Kazuya, and includes a recap of the earlier games, which makes it the practical starting point today. It is also the only entry with a modern training suite for new players.

editions.name: Tekken 8
editions.note: Season pass characters are sold separately from the base game.

name: The Elder Scrolls
scope: The five numbered games plus The Elder Scrolls Online; the side games Battlespire and Redguard, and the mobile spin-off Blades, are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order for the numbered games, but The Elder Scrolls Online sits roughly 800 years before all of them despite arriving in 2014. None of the games continues another's plot directly, so this ordering is about the history of Tamriel rather than a story you have to follow in sequence.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls Online
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set in 2E 582, centuries before Arena and the earliest point in the series. It is an MMO with a subscription-optional model and a decade of expansions, so treat it as a parallel branch rather than a step in the sequence.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls Online
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game includes the original zones; chapters are sold separately or via ESO Plus.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls: Arena
games.note: Set in 3E 389. Bethesda has given it away free for twenty years, but it is a DOS game that needs DOSBox and has almost nothing in common with the modern entries.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls: Arena
editions.note: Free download from Bethesda, run through DOSBox.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall
games.note: Set in 3E 405, sixteen years after Arena, and enormous but procedurally generated. The free Daggerfall Unity rebuild is the only practical way to play it now.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall
editions.note: Original release; free but heavily bugged.

editions.name: Daggerfall Unity - GOG Cut
editions.note: Free, community-built engine port with mouse look and modern resolutions.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind
games.version: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind Game of the Year Edition
games.query: Morrowind Game of the Year Edition
games.note: 3E 427, on the island of Vvardenfell. Its combat uses dice rolls behind the scenes, which trips up newcomers; the free OpenMW engine replacement fixes stability and adds modern display support.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind
editions.note: Base game without expansions.

editions.name: Morrowind Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Includes Tribunal and Bloodmoon; works with OpenMW.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
games.version: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
games.note: 3E 433, six years after Morrowind, and the game whose ending sets up Skyrim's political situation. The 2025 remaster rebuilds the visuals in Unreal Engine 5 while keeping the original systems and includes both expansions.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Original with Shivering Isles and Knights of the Nine.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
editions.note: Unreal Engine 5 remaster with all expansions included.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
games.version: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Anniversary Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: 4E 201, roughly two hundred years after Oblivion, and the standard entry point. The Anniversary Edition adds Creation Club content on top of Special Edition; many long-running PC mods still target Special Edition instead.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
editions.note: Original 32-bit release.

editions.name: Skyrim Special Edition
editions.note: 64-bit rebuild with all three expansions; the main mod target.

editions.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Anniversary Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Special Edition plus the Creation Club catalogue.

name: The Evil Within
scope: Both Tango Gameworks games and the story DLC for the first. The Executioner DLC, which is a first-person combat mode with no bearing on the plot, is noted but not listed separately.
caveat: Two games, in release order, with a three-year gap in the story. The only ordering detail is the first game's two-part DLC, The Assignment and The Consequence, which retells the first game from Juli Kidman's perspective and sets up her role in the sequel; play it after the base game and before the sequel.

games.title: The Evil Within
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Sebastian Castellanos inside the STEM system, and the setup for everything in the sequel. It shipped with black bars and a 30fps cap; both can be turned off in the PC version's settings, and later console patches removed them too.

editions.name: The Evil Within
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Base game only.

editions.name: The Evil Within with the Season Pass
editions.note: Adds The Assignment and The Consequence, which lead directly into the sequel.

games.title: The Evil Within 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set three years later and assumes you know who Kidman and Mobius are, so the first game and its DLC come first. Trades the corridor structure for semi-open districts and adds a first-person option.

editions.name: The Evil Within 2
editions.note: The only version; runs on current consoles through backward compatibility.

name: The Last of Us
scope: Part I, Left Behind, Part II. The HBO series is not a game and is not tracked.
caveat: Left Behind splits across the timeline — its Riley chapters precede Part I, its Ellie chapters sit inside Part I’s winter section. It is listed after Part I because that is where its framing puts you, and because playing it first spoils Part I’s third act.

games.title: The Last of Us Part I
games.version: The Last of Us Part I
games.query: The Last of Us Part I
games.note: Full remake (2022) of the 2013 original. The 2023 PC port launched badly and has since been patched into decent shape.

editions.name: The Last of Us
editions.note: Original release; Left Behind sold separately later.

editions.name: The Last of Us Remastered
editions.note: 1080p/60fps port bundling Left Behind.

editions.name: The Last of Us Part I
editions.note: Full remake including Left Behind; best way to play.

authored.version: The Last of Us Part I

games.title: The Last of Us: Left Behind
games.version: The Last of Us Part I
games.query: The Last of Us Part I
games.note: Bundled with Part I. Two hours, and the strongest character writing in the first game.

editions.name: Left Behind (DLC)
editions.note: Standalone story DLC for the original game.

editions.name: The Last of Us Remastered
editions.note: Includes Left Behind with the base campaign.

editions.name: The Last of Us Part I
editions.note: Left Behind fully remade and bundled in.

authored.version: The Last of Us Part I

games.title: The Last of Us Part II
games.version: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.query: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.note: PC release in 2025, based on the 2024 Remastered edition — includes the No Return mode and the unfinished Lost Levels.

editions.name: The Last of Us Part II
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
editions.note: Adds No Return roguelike and cut Lost Levels.

authored.version: The Last of Us Part II Remastered

name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails
scope: The Trails series proper, from Trails in the Sky through the Calvard arc. The earlier Legend of Heroes games that predate Trails, and the Ys crossover Ys vs. Trails in the Sky, are excluded.
caveat: This is one continuous story with the strictest play order in the medium — characters, political fallout and running plot threads carry across every game, and starting in the middle means walking into a decade of spoilers. In-universe order is release order with one wrinkle: the Crossbell games run roughly in parallel with the first two Cold Steel games, and each pair references the other. Play by release order and you get the intended sequence.

arcs.name: Liberl
arcs.blurb: Estelle and Joshua's trilogy, and the foundation everything after it stands on.

arcs.name: Crossbell
arcs.blurb: Lloyd Bannings and a police unit in a city-state squeezed between two empires.

arcs.name: Erebonia
arcs.blurb: Rean Schwarzer across four games and a war, ending in a crossover epilogue.

arcs.name: Calvard
arcs.blurb: Van Arkride's spriggan agency in the republic next door, with a partial reset for newcomers.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky
games.note: The start of everything, and the only sensible place to begin. The 2025 remake rebuilds it in 3D with voice acting and a faster combat system; the 2011 PC version is still sold and still fine if you prefer sprites.

editions.name: Trails in the Sky FC
editions.note: Original sprite version; the 2011 English PC release is the definitive one of these.

editions.name: Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter
editions.note: 3D remake with full voice acting and reworked combat.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky SC
games.note: Resolves the first game's cliffhanger and is the larger half of a single story. No remake yet, so the first game's remake and this do not visually match.

editions.name: Trails in the Sky SC
editions.note: The 2015 English PC release is the standard version.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky the 3rd
games.note: Structured as a dungeon crawl with optional story vignettes attached, which makes it look skippable. It is not — several of those vignettes set up the Crossbell and Erebonia arcs directly.

editions.name: Trails in the Sky the 3rd
editions.note: The 2017 English PC release is the standard version.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails from Zero
games.note: New cast and city, and the closest the series has to a second starting point — though it still assumes the Sky trilogy. Waited twelve years for an English release, which is why so many people played the Cold Steel games first.

editions.name: Trails from Zero
editions.note: Japanese release; no official English version until 2022.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero
editions.note: Official English release built on the enhanced PC version.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails to Azure
games.note: Direct sequel to Trails from Zero, and its ending is the single biggest load-bearing event in the series so far. Cold Steel III and IV are close to unreadable without it.

editions.name: Trails to Azure
editions.note: Japanese release only until 2023.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure
editions.note: Official English release.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails of Cold Steel
games.note: Runs roughly in parallel with Trails from Zero, in the empire next door. It was many Western players' first Trails game by accident of release timing, but it leans on the Sky trilogy from the start.

editions.name: Trails of Cold Steel
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel
editions.note: PC and PS4 versions add turbo mode and higher frame rates.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails of Cold Steel II
games.note: Begins the instant the first game ends and carries a save over for bonuses. Overlaps with Trails to Azure, and its epilogue chapter matters for the rest of the arc.

editions.name: Trails of Cold Steel II
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II
editions.note: Modern versions with save import from Cold Steel I.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails of Cold Steel III
games.note: Set eighteen months later with a new class, and the point where the Crossbell and Liberl threads all converge. Skipping the Crossbell games before this one costs you most of the plot.

editions.name: Trails of Cold Steel III
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel III
editions.note: PC version runs uncapped and is the smoothest.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails of Cold Steel IV
games.note: Picks up from Cold Steel III's cliffhanger and pulls in cast members from every earlier arc. It closes the Erebonia story but not the series.

editions.name: Trails of Cold Steel IV
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV
editions.note: PC version is the technical best.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails into Reverie
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails into Reverie
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails into Reverie
games.note: An epilogue to both the Crossbell and Erebonia arcs, told across three switchable routes. It is the single worst possible entry point and the last game before the Calvard arc begins.

editions.name: Trails into Reverie
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails into Reverie
editions.note: English release across all four platforms.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails through Daybreak
games.note: New country, new cast, new engine, and a deliberate soft reset — the most forgiving entry point since Trails from Zero. It still assumes you know the shape of what came before, and returning characters appear without introduction.

editions.name: Kuro no Kiseki
editions.note: Japanese release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak
editions.note: English release.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak II
games.version: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak II
games.query: The Legend of Heroes Trails through Daybreak II
games.note: Direct sequel with the same cast, built around a repeating-day structure. The Calvard arc is still ongoing in Japan, so this is not an ending.

editions.name: Kuro no Kiseki II
editions.note: Japanese release.

editions.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails through Daybreak II
editions.note: English release.

name: The Legend of Zelda
scope: The mainline Zelda games as placed on Nintendo's own timeline, from Skyward Sword through Echoes of Wisdom. Spin-offs are excluded: Hyrule Warriors, Cadence of Hyrule, Tri Force Heroes, the Tingle games, the CD-i titles and the Game & Watch collections.
caveat: Release order and chronology have almost nothing to do with each other here. Nintendo's own timeline splits into three branches at Ocarina of Time depending on how that game ended, and those branches are the arcs below. Two honest gaps: Nintendo has never pinned down exactly where Breath of the Wild sits, saying only that it is far after all three branches, and it has given Echoes of Wisdom no placement at all.

arcs.name: Era of the Sky and the Hero of Time
arcs.blurb: The founding of Hyrule and the Master Sword, up to the point where the timeline splits.

arcs.name: Child Timeline
arcs.blurb: The branch where Link is sent back to his childhood and Ganondorf is stopped before he rises.

arcs.name: Adult Timeline
arcs.blurb: The branch where the Hero of Time vanishes and Hyrule is left to flood.

arcs.name: Downfall Timeline
arcs.blurb: The branch where the Hero of Time loses, containing the original NES games and their lead-up.

arcs.name: The Wild Era
arcs.blurb: A Hyrule thousands of years later, too far ahead to be pinned to any one branch.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Skyward Sword HD
games.note: The earliest point on the timeline: the origin of the Master Sword, of Demise's curse, and of the Link and Zelda cycle everything else repeats. The HD version drops the mandatory motion controls, which was the original's biggest obstacle.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
editions.note: Original release; motion controls are required.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD
editions.note: Higher framerate, button-only control option, faster tutorial dialogue.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap
games.version: The Minish Cap (Game Boy Advance - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda The Minish Cap
games.note: Set long after Skyward Sword, it explains where the Four Sword and Vaati come from. Not sold on its own; it is part of the Game Boy Advance library included with Nintendo Switch Online plus the Expansion Pack.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap
editions.note: Original cartridge.

editions.name: The Minish Cap (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Expansion Pack tier, with save states and rewind.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Four Swords
games.note: A short multiplayer-only mode that shipped alongside the GBA port of A Link to the Past, and the point where Vaati is sealed. There is no current release: the standalone Anniversary Edition was a limited-time DSi and 3DS download that has been delisted.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords
editions.note: Bundled with A Link to the Past; needs two linked systems.

editions.name: Four Swords Anniversary Edition
editions.note: Free limited-time download, now delisted.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
games.version: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo 64 - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time
games.note: The hinge of the whole timeline: its ending is what splits the series into three branches. Sold only as part of the Nintendo 64 library on Nintendo Switch Online plus the Expansion Pack; the 3DS remake is the better-playing version but that store is closed.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Ocarina of Time 3D
editions.note: Remade visuals and touch-screen item swapping; eShop closed.

editions.name: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated N64 version included with the Expansion Pack tier.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Majora's Mask
games.note: A direct sequel to Ocarina of Time, following the same Link after he is returned to childhood, which is why it starts the Child branch. It opens assuming you know who he was looking for, so it is the one game here you should not play first.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
editions.note: Original release; needed the Expansion Pak accessory.

editions.name: Majora's Mask 3D
editions.note: Reworked boss fights and save system; eShop closed.

editions.name: Majora's Mask (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated N64 version included with the Expansion Pack tier.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Twilight Princess HD
games.note: Set generations after Majora's Mask and the clearest sequel to Ocarina of Time's Child branch, with the Hero's Shade explaining the connection outright. The catch is availability: the HD version is trapped on Wii U with that store closed, so it is disc-and-hardware only.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
editions.note: The Wii version mirrors the world and uses motion aiming.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD
editions.note: Higher resolution, reworked Twilight Realm sections, amiibo support.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Four Swords Adventures
games.note: The last entry on the Child branch, dealing with Ganondorf's return and a second sealing of Vaati. It has never been re-released, and its intended multiplayer needs a GameCube plus Game Boy Advances and link cables.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures
editions.note: Only version; single-player works without the link cables.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker
games.version: The Wind Waker (GameCube - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda The Wind Waker
games.note: Centuries after Ocarina of Time on the branch where the hero never came back and Hyrule was flooded. Part of the GameCube library on Nintendo Switch Online plus the Expansion Pack for Switch 2; the Wii U HD version is the other option if you still have one.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker
editions.note: Original release; the Triforce hunt near the end is much longer here.

editions.name: The Wind Waker HD
editions.note: Shortened Triforce hunt, faster sailing, better lighting; store closed.

editions.name: The Wind Waker (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated GameCube version included with the Expansion Pack tier.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Phantom Hourglass
games.note: A direct sequel to The Wind Waker with the same Link and Tetra, months later. Entirely stylus-controlled, and with the Wii U eShop closed it is a DS cartridge or nothing.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass
editions.note: Only playable version; the Wii U re-release is delisted.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Spirit Tracks
games.note: Roughly a century after Phantom Hourglass, in the new land the Wind Waker cast founded, closing the Adult branch. Same availability problem as Phantom Hourglass: DS cartridge only.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks
editions.note: Only playable version; the Wii U re-release is delisted.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
games.version: A Link to the Past (Super Nintendo - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda A Link to the Past
games.note: The first game on the branch where the Hero of Time lost, and the template most 2D Zeldas follow. Included in the Super Nintendo library on Nintendo Switch Online, so no separate purchase.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: A Link to the Past / Four Swords
editions.note: Port with an extra dungeon, bundled with Four Swords.

editions.name: A Link to the Past (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated SNES version with save states, included in the base tier.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons
games.version: Oracle of Seasons (Game Boy - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Oracle of Seasons
games.note: One half of a pair released the same day; Seasons and Ages take place in different lands and can be played in either order, then linked by password for a combined ending. Both sit after A Link to the Past.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons
editions.note: Original cartridge; links to Oracle of Ages by password.

editions.name: Oracle of Seasons (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Game Boy library; linking still works via password.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages
games.version: Oracle of Ages (Game Boy - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Oracle of Ages
games.note: The other half of the pair, built around time travel rather than season shifting. Finishing one and carrying the password into the other unlocks the true final confrontation, so play both or neither.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages
editions.note: Original cartridge; links to Oracle of Seasons by password.

editions.name: Oracle of Ages (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Included with the Game Boy library; linking still works via password.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening (2019)
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Link's Awakening Switch
games.note: Placed after the Oracle games, with Link shipwrecked on Koholint after leaving Hyrule. It is entirely self-contained, so timeline position matters less here than anywhere else in the series.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
editions.note: Original monochrome release.

editions.name: Link's Awakening DX
editions.note: Colour version with an extra dungeon; on the Nintendo Switch Online Game Boy library.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
editions.note: Full remake with a new art style and a dungeon builder mode.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
games.query: The Legend of Zelda A Link Between Worlds
games.note: A sequel to A Link to the Past set generations later in the same Hyrule, reusing its map deliberately. Never ported off the 3DS, and that store is closed, so it needs the handheld and a cartridge.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
editions.note: Only version; the stereoscopic depth is optional.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda
games.version: The Legend of Zelda (NES - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.note: Chronologically late despite being the first game made: it sits well after A Link to the Past on the Downfall branch. Included in the NES library on Nintendo Switch Online, with rewind, which helps a lot with its unmarked secrets.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated with save states and rewind, included in the base tier.

games.title: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
games.version: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link (NES - Nintendo Switch Online)
games.query: Zelda II The Adventure of Link
games.note: A direct sequel to the NES original and the last entry on the Downfall branch. A side-scrolling action RPG rather than a top-down adventure, and notoriously punishing; the Switch Online rewind makes it survivable.

editions.name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Zelda II (Nintendo Switch Online)
editions.note: Emulated with save states and rewind, included in the base tier.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild
games.note: Set thousands of years after everything above. Nintendo has said only that it comes after all three branches and has deliberately avoided saying which one it descends from, so anyone claiming a definite placement is guessing.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
editions.note: Launch version; the Wii U release is the weaker of the two.

editions.name: Breath of the Wild - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
editions.note: Higher resolution and framerate; a paid upgrade if you own the Switch version.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom
games.note: A direct sequel to Breath of the Wild with the same Link, same map and consequences from its ending, plus long flashbacks to Hyrule's founding. Those flashbacks sit far in the past but the game itself belongs here.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
editions.note: Original release; framerate dips in busy areas.

editions.name: Tears of the Kingdom - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
editions.note: Higher resolution and a stable framerate; paid upgrade path from the Switch version.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom
games.version: The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom
games.query: The Legend of Zelda Echoes of Wisdom
games.note: The first mainline game with Zelda herself as the playable lead. Nintendo has given it no timeline placement at all, so it is listed last here only because it is the most recent release; treat its position as unresolved rather than settled.

editions.name: The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom
editions.note: Only version; runs with better performance on Switch 2.

name: The Witcher
scope: The three main Witcher games by CD Projekt Red. The standalone Thronebreaker and the Gwent card game are excluded, as are the Netflix adaptations.
caveat: In-universe chronology matches release order exactly: each game picks up after the last. All three games are a sequel to Andrzej Sapkowski's novels rather than an adaptation of them, so the books sit before game one; you can start at any game, but Geralt's amnesia in the first game is the story's own way of catching newcomers up.

games.title: The Witcher
games.version: The Witcher: Enhanced Edition Director's Cut
games.query: The Witcher Enhanced Edition Director's Cut
games.note: Opens five years after the novels end, with Geralt found alive and memoryless. The Enhanced Edition fixes the worst of the original's loading times and translation; the combat is still a rhythm-clicking system from 2007.

editions.name: The Witcher
editions.note: Original release; long loads and a rough English script.

editions.name: The Witcher: Enhanced Edition Director's Cut
editions.note: Re-translated, re-cut and far better paced; the only version still sold.

games.title: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings
games.version: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings Enhanced Edition
games.query: The Witcher 2 Assassins of Kings Enhanced Edition
games.note: Directly follows the first game's regicide plot and sets up the Nilfgaardian invasion that frames the third. Its branching second act splits into two largely different chapters, so one playthrough sees roughly half the content.

editions.name: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings
editions.note: Original release, superseded by the free Enhanced update.

editions.name: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings Enhanced Edition
editions.note: Adds a new prologue and epilogue and reworks the tutorial.

games.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
games.version: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.query: The Witcher 3 Wild Hunt Complete Edition
games.note: Best entry point despite being third: it recaps what matters and imports save choices only cosmetically. The Complete Edition bundles Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, both of which sit after the main story.

editions.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
editions.note: Base game only, no expansions.

editions.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Base game plus both expansions; includes the 2022 next-gen update on current hardware.

name: Thief
scope: The three Looking Glass and Ion Storm games about Garrett, plus the 2014 reboot. The fan-made standalone The Dark Mod and community campaigns are excluded.
caveat: The original trilogy runs in release order as one continuous story about the same Garrett. The 2014 game is a reboot with a different Garrett and no connection to the earlier plot, so it is a separate continuity rather than a fourth chapter, and can be played at any point or not at all.

arcs.name: Original Trilogy
arcs.blurb: Garrett, the Keepers and the Hammerites across three connected games from 1998 to 2004.

arcs.name: 2014 Reboot
arcs.blurb: A self-contained retelling with a new Garrett and no ties to the original story.

games.title: Thief: The Dark Project
games.note: Introduces Garrett, the Keepers and the pagan-versus-Hammerite conflict the sequel builds on. Buy Thief Gold, the 1999 re-release with three extra missions; the fan patch TFix is the usual fix for modern displays.

editions.name: Thief: The Dark Project
editions.note: Original release, missing three missions.

editions.name: Thief Gold
editions.note: Adds The Thieves' Guild, Song of the Caverns and Mage Towers; the only version sold.

games.title: Thief II: The Metal Age
games.note: Follows on directly from the first game with the Mechanists rising out of the Hammerite order. Leans further into pure city heists than its predecessor's undead levels, and is the one most players rate highest.

editions.name: Thief II: The Metal Age
editions.note: Only release; the fan patch T2Fix handles modern resolutions.

games.title: Thief: Deadly Shadows
games.note: Closes the Keeper storyline the first two games set up, adding hub city districts and a third-person option. Built for the original Xbox as well as PC, so the levels are smaller; the Sneaky Upgrade patch restores loading behaviour and resolution support.

editions.name: Thief: Deadly Shadows
editions.note: Only release; needs the Sneaky Upgrade to run properly today.

games.title: Thief
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: A separate continuity: same name and profession, different Garrett, no story links to the trilogy. Modern controls and presentation, but a more guided level design than the games it reboots.

editions.name: Thief
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: One release; The Bank Heist DLC mission is bundled in most current listings.

name: Titanfall
scope: The two Titanfall games. Apex Legends is set in the same universe roughly thirty years later and reuses its characters and lore, but it is a battle royale with no campaign, so it is not listed here.
caveat: Chronology matches release order: Titanfall covers a stretch of the Frontier War and Titanfall 2 is set a few years afterwards. The practical problem is availability rather than order, since the first game was delisted and its servers were shut down, and its story only existed inside multiplayer matches anyway.

games.title: Titanfall
games.note: Delisted from sale in 2021 with its online services since shut down, which makes it effectively unplayable. Its campaign was a scripted layer over multiplayer matches, so almost nothing is lost by starting with the sequel.

editions.name: Titanfall
editions.note: Only version; no longer purchasable or playable online.

games.title: Titanfall 2
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: The entry point and the only one with a proper single-player campaign, which requires no knowledge of the first game. Its multiplayer has been unreliable for years because of server attacks; the campaign is unaffected.

editions.name: Titanfall 2
editions.note: Original release, Origin-only on PC.

editions.name: Titanfall 2: Ultimate Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Adds the cosmetic packs; the standard listing on Steam since 2020.

name: Tom Clancy's The Division
scope: The two mainline games and their expansions; the cancelled spin-off Heartland and the mobile game Resurgence are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order: the first game covers the weeks after the Green Poison outbreak in New York, and the sequel is set about seven months later in Washington. One thing catches people out: The Division 2's Warlords of New York expansion returns to Manhattan and is set after the DC campaign, not alongside the first game.

games.title: Tom Clancy's The Division
games.version: Tom Clancy's The Division - Gold Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Tom Clancy's The Division Gold Edition
games.note: Winter New York in the weeks after the outbreak. No longer receiving content, and the sequel recaps enough that this is optional; its expansions, particularly Survival, are the reason to bother.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's The Division
editions.note: Base game; the three Underground, Survival and Last Stand expansions are separate.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's The Division - Gold Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Season pass included; current consoles run it through back-compat.

games.title: Tom Clancy's The Division 2
games.version: Tom Clancy's The Division 2 - Warlords of New York Edition
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: The Division 2 Warlords of New York
games.note: Seven months after the first game, in Washington DC, and the better entry point because it is still supported and explains its own setup. The Warlords of New York edition bundles the expansion that continues the story after the base campaign.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's The Division 2
editions.note: Base game only.

editions.name: Tom Clancy's The Division 2 - Warlords of New York Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game plus the New York expansion and its level cap increase.

name: Tomb Raider
scope: The three Lara Croft continuities: the Core Design classics I to V, the Crystal Dynamics Legend trilogy, and the Survivor trilogy. The Angel of Darkness, the isometric Lara Croft spin-offs and the mobile games are excluded.
caveat: There is no single timeline. Each of the three arcs reboots Lara from scratch, so chronology only means anything inside an arc. Within the classics, release order is chronological. The Legend arc is the exception worth knowing: Anniversary is a retelling of the first game's Peru expedition and sits earliest in that continuity even though it came out after Legend, and Underworld follows Legend while referring back to Anniversary.

arcs.name: Classic (Core Design)
arcs.blurb: The original 1996-2000 run, a confident Lara raiding tombs with tank controls.

arcs.name: Legend Trilogy
arcs.blurb: Crystal Dynamics' first reboot, built around the disappearance of Lara's mother.

arcs.name: Survivor Trilogy
arcs.blurb: The 2013 origin reboot, following an inexperienced Lara becoming the raider she is elsewhere.

games.title: Tomb Raider
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The original Peru-to-Atlantis expedition and the start of the classic continuity. The 2024 remaster bundles the first three games with optional modern graphics and controls, and includes their expansion levels.

editions.name: Tomb Raider
editions.note: Original release; needs emulation or a source port today.

editions.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: All three games, toggleable new visuals, original geometry untouched.

games.title: Tomb Raider II
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: The Dagger of Xian, and the first game to put Lara's manor and human enemies at the centre. Sold only inside the I-III remaster listed on the previous row.

editions.name: Tomb Raider II
editions.note: Original release plus the Golden Mask expansion.

editions.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered

games.title: Tomb Raider: Legend
games.note: Starts the Excalibur and Amelia Croft thread that Underworld finishes, and is the natural entry point to this continuity. Short, linear and much faster-moving than the classics.

editions.name: Tomb Raider: Legend
editions.platforms: PC / PS2 / PSP / Xbox / Xbox 360 / GameCube
editions.note: PC version, still sold; the next-gen build has better lighting.

games.title: Tomb Raider: Underworld
games.note: Direct sequel to Legend, resolving the search for Lara's mother. The Xbox 360 version had two exclusive DLC chapters that are not part of the PC release.

editions.name: Tomb Raider: Underworld
editions.note: PC version; the Beneath the Ashes and Lara's Shadow DLC were Xbox 360 only.

games.title: Tomb Raider
games.version: Tomb Raider: Game of the Year Edition
games.query: Tomb Raider Game of the Year Edition
games.note: A full reboot: Lara's first expedition, on Yamatai, with no connection to either earlier continuity. On console the equivalent is the Definitive Edition, which rebuilt the character models for PS4 and Xbox One.

editions.name: Tomb Raider
editions.note: Original release.

editions.name: Tomb Raider: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Console remaster with a rebuilt Lara model and all DLC.

editions.name: Tomb Raider: Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: PC package with the Tomb of the Lost Adventurer and multiplayer content.

games.version: Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Celebration
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.query: Rise of the Tomb Raider 20 Year Celebration

editions.name: Rise of the Tomb Raider: 20 Year Celebration

games.query: Shadow of the Tomb Raider Definitive Edition
