editions.note: Base game without the DLC tombs.

editions.name: Shadow of the Tomb Raider: Definitive Edition
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game plus all seven DLC challenge tombs.

name: Uncharted
scope: Drake tetralogy plus The Lost Legacy. Golden Abyss (Vita) and the Fight for Fortune spin-offs are out of scope.
caveat: Present-day chronology matches release order. The flashbacks in Uncharted 3 (young Drake in Cartagena) and Uncharted 4 (the orphanage, Panama) are the earliest events in the series, but they sit inside games that come later, so the games stay in this order. Play order and chronology agree here.

games.title: Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune
games.note: Never released on PC. Sold only inside The Nathan Drake Collection (2015), which runs the three PS3 games at 1080p/60.

editions.name: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune
editions.note: Original release; stuck on PS3 hardware.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Bluepoint remaster at 1080p/60; only modern way to play it.

games.title: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
games.note: Still the high point of the series. Collection only; no PC release has ever happened.

editions.name: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
editions.note: Original release; PS3 only.

editions.name: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves - Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Adds multiplayer map and skin DLC; single-player story unchanged.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Remastered 1080p/60 campaign; best and only current-gen version.

games.title: Uncharted 3: Drake’s Deception
games.note: Chronology: opens on the earliest material in the franchise — a teenage Drake in Cartagena — but the present-day thread follows Uncharted 2 directly.

editions.name: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception
editions.note: Original release; PS3 only.

editions.name: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception - Game of the Year Edition
editions.note: Bundles multiplayer DLC; campaign identical to launch.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
editions.note: Remastered campaign at 1080p/60; multiplayer dropped.

games.title: Uncharted 4: A Thief’s End
games.note: On PC via the Legacy of Thieves Collection — a solid port. The MSRP covers this and Lost Legacy together. Multiplayer is cut from the PC version.

editions.name: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
editions.note: Original release; 30fps on base PS4.

editions.name: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection
editions.note: Remaster of 4 plus Lost Legacy; 60/120fps and the only PC version.

games.title: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
games.note: Chloe and Nadine, set shortly after Uncharted 4. Bundled into Legacy of Thieves, never sold alone. Skippable without losing the Drake story.

editions.name: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
editions.note: Original standalone release.

editions.name: Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection
editions.note: Remastered and paired with Uncharted 4; adds PC and 60/120fps modes.

name: Valkyria Chronicles
scope: The four numbered Valkyria Chronicles games, all set during the Second Europan War. Valkyria Revolution is a different setting with a different system and is excluded.
caveat: Three of the four games cover the same year of the same war from different fronts, so their order relative to each other barely matters — Valkyria Chronicles, 3 and 4 are parallel, and only Valkyria Chronicles 2 is clearly later, set two years on. Each has its own squad and its own arc, and cameos aside, none of them requires another. The real obstacle is availability: Valkyria Chronicles 3 never received an English release, and 2 and 3 are both PSP-only.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles
games.note: Squad 7's campaign in Gallia, and the entry point by default. The PC version is the most available and runs well; the PS4 Remastered is the same game with trophies and the DLC missions bundled.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles
editions.note: Original release; DLC missions sold separately.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles
editions.note: PC port with all DLC included; the Switch version followed in 2018.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles Remastered
editions.note: PS4 version with the DLC included.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles 4
games.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Runs alongside the first game on the eastern front of the same war, with a separate squad. Mechanically the most refined of the four, and it stands entirely on its own.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles 4
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: The only release; a Complete Edition bundles the DLC squad stories.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles 3: Unrecorded Chronicles
games.note: A penal unit operating during the same period as the first game. Never released in English on any platform, which makes it the one entry most people genuinely cannot play.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles 3: Unrecorded Chronicles
editions.note: Japan-only; an Extra Edition reissue was also Japanese.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles 2
games.note: Set two years after the first game and the only entry clearly later in the timeline. Its military-academy framing and small PSP-scale maps make it the odd one out tonally as well as technically.

editions.name: Valkyria Chronicles 2
editions.note: The only release; never ported off PSP.

name: Warcraft
scope: The three real-time strategy games and their campaign expansions, plus World of Warcraft as the continuation of the storyline. Hearthstone and Warcraft Rumble are excluded — neither advances the plot.
caveat: In-universe order and release order are the same, and each game's campaign follows on from the last. The expansions matter: Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal and especially Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne carry story that the base campaigns set up and do not finish. After Warcraft III the story continues only inside World of Warcraft, which is a subscription MMO with twenty years of expansions — it is a genuine continuation, not a spin-off, but it is not something you finish, and the plot arrives in fragments rather than as a campaign.

games.title: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans
games.note: The First War, and the least essential of the three — Warcraft II recaps everything that matters. The 2024 remaster redraws the art and adds modern unit controls, with a toggle back to the original look.

editions.name: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans
editions.note: Original release; also sold unmodified on GOG.

editions.name: Warcraft: Remastered
editions.note: Redrawn art, modern controls, original-graphics toggle.

games.title: Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness
games.note: The Second War, and the direct setup for Warcraft III's opening. The remaster includes the Beyond the Dark Portal expansion campaign, which continues the story past the base game's ending.

editions.name: Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness
editions.note: Original release; Beyond the Dark Portal sold separately.

editions.name: Warcraft II: Remastered
editions.note: Both campaigns, redrawn art and an original-graphics toggle.

games.title: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos
games.note: The Third War and the foundation for everything World of Warcraft does; The Frozen Throne expansion is included and contains the more important half of the story. Reforged launched badly in 2020 and replaced the original client outright, so there is no way to buy the 2002 version any more; later patches have repaired much of it.

editions.name: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos
editions.note: Original release, no longer sold.

editions.name: Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne
editions.note: Expansion continuing the story; now folded into Reforged.

editions.name: Warcraft III: Reforged
editions.note: Both campaigns with optional new models; heavily patched since launch.

games.title: World of Warcraft
games.note: Everything after Warcraft III happens here, but it is a subscription MMO rather than a campaign, and the story is spread across two decades of expansions delivered as quests. Included for completeness, not as something to play through — the base game is free to level twenty and the current expansion is a separate purchase on top of the subscription.

editions.name: World of Warcraft
editions.note: The original game; its content has been rewritten repeatedly since.

editions.name: World of Warcraft (current retail)
editions.note: The live service; subscription plus the latest expansion.

editions.name: World of Warcraft Classic
editions.note: Re-created older versions of the game, included with the same subscription.

name: Wasteland
scope: The three mainline Desert Rangers RPGs. The 1988 sequel-in-name Fountain of Dreams and the mobile game Wasteland: Rebels are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order, with large in-universe gaps: the first game is set in 2087, the second roughly fifteen years later, and the third shortly after that. Wasteland 2 opens with the first game's events treated as Ranger history, so the older game is context rather than a prerequisite.

games.title: Wasteland
games.note: The origin of the Desert Rangers and of the Guardians who recur in the sequels. The remaster updates the art and audio but keeps the 1988 design, including paragraph-book style text and unrecoverable party mistakes.

editions.name: Wasteland
editions.note: Original release; requires an emulator and the printed paragraph book.

editions.name: Wasteland Remastered
editions.note: Redrawn art, new score, quality-of-life fixes; also on Game Pass.

games.title: Wasteland 2
games.note: A direct sequel to the first game, set in Arizona and later Los Angeles, with the original's factions carried forward. The Director's Cut is the version to play: rebuilt in Unity 5, fully voiced, with a reworked perk system.

editions.name: Wasteland 2
editions.note: Launch version; superseded and free-upgraded to the Director's Cut.

editions.name: Wasteland 2: Director's Cut
editions.note: New engine, voice acting, precision strikes and rebalanced combat.

games.title: Wasteland 3
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Sends a Ranger squad from Arizona to frozen Colorado shortly after the second game, and recaps what it needs to. The tightest and most approachable of the three, which makes it the best place to start.

editions.name: Wasteland 3
editions.note: Base game; the two story DLC are sold separately.

editions.name: Wasteland 3: Colorado Collection
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: Base game plus The Battle of Steeltown and Cult of the Holy Detonation; on Game Pass as well.

name: Watch Dogs
scope: The three console and PC games: Watch Dogs, Watch Dogs 2 and Watch Dogs: Legion, including their story DLC. Mobile spin-offs are excluded.
caveat: Chronology matches release order. Each game has a new protagonist and a new city, and none of them requires the previous one, so the connection is DedSec and the ctOS surveillance premise rather than a continuing plot. Legion's Bloodline expansion is the exception: it brings back Aiden Pearce from the first game and Wrench from the second, so it reads much better last.

games.title: Watch Dogs
games.note: Chicago under ctOS, following Aiden Pearce. The grimmest of the three and the one that dates worst, but it establishes ctOS, Blume and the DedSec setup the sequels use. The Complete Edition includes the Bad Blood story DLC.

editions.name: Watch Dogs
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / PS3 / Xbox 360 / Wii U
editions.note: Base game; the last-gen versions are heavily cut down.

editions.name: Watch Dogs Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles the Bad Blood campaign and the season pass content.

games.title: Watch Dogs 2
games.note: San Francisco a couple of years later with Marcus and the DedSec cell, and a much lighter tone. It stands entirely on its own, which makes it the easiest place to start despite being the middle game.

editions.name: Watch Dogs 2
editions.note: Base game.

editions.name: Watch Dogs 2 Gold Edition
editions.note: Adds the Human Conditions and No Compromise mission packs.

games.title: Watch Dogs: Legion
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Near-future London with no fixed protagonist; you recruit and play as any NPC. The Bloodline expansion is a prequel within this game that puts Aiden and Wrench together, so buy the version that includes it.

editions.name: Watch Dogs: Legion
editions.note: Base game; the online mode was discontinued.

editions.name: Watch Dogs: Legion Gold Edition
editions.note: Includes the Bloodline expansion with Aiden Pearce and Wrench.

name: Wolfenstein
scope: The three classic-continuity games and the four MachineGames entries; Spear of Destiny, the 1981 original Castle Wolfenstein, the Enemy Territory multiplayer spin-offs and the VR title Cyberpilot are excluded.
caveat: Two continuities, not one line. The classic games run 1992 to 2009 and are set during the war. MachineGames restarted the story in 2014 with the same B.J. Blazkowicz but a rewritten history where the Nazis won; within that group The Old Blood is a prequel released after The New Order, so chronology and release order disagree there.

arcs.name: Classic Continuity
arcs.blurb: The id and Gray Matter games, set during the Second World War as it actually ended.

arcs.name: MachineGames Continuity
arcs.blurb: The 2014 restart, in an alternate history where the Nazis won and occupied America.

games.title: Wolfenstein 3D
games.note: The 1943 escape from Castle Wolfenstein, and historically the reason the series exists. There is no story continuity to protect here; it is worth playing as a curiosity rather than as setup.

editions.name: Wolfenstein 3D
editions.note: The Steam and GOG listings are the DOS game bundled with a modern launcher.

games.title: Return to Castle Wolfenstein
games.note: The best entry in the classic line and a full reworking of the 1943 premise with occult SS experiments. Runs on modern hardware, though the community iortcw build handles high resolutions better.

editions.name: Return to Castle Wolfenstein
editions.note: The PC version is the complete one; console versions cut and rearranged levels.

games.title: Wolfenstein
games.note: A direct sequel to Return to Castle Wolfenstein and the end of the classic line. It was pulled from digital storefronts over licensing, so a used disc is the only reliable way to get it.

editions.name: Wolfenstein
editions.note: Only version; delisted from digital sale.

games.title: Wolfenstein: The Old Blood
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Standalone prequel set in 1946, ending where The New Order's prologue begins. Released second, and it works better as a follow-up than as an introduction.

editions.name: Wolfenstein: The Old Blood
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
editions.note: No copy of The New Order required.

games.title: Wolfenstein: The New Order
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Opens in 1946 and then jumps to a 1960 where the Nazis won the war. The clearest starting point for the modern series, and an early choice permanently changes which of two characters appears throughout.

editions.name: Wolfenstein: The New Order
editions.platforms: PC / PS3 / PS4 / Xbox 360 / Xbox One
editions.note: Current-generation versions run via back-compat.

games.title: Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Continues from The New Order's ending in 1961, moving the fight to occupied America. It assumes you know who lived and died in the previous game.

editions.name: Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: The Switch port is playable but visually cut down.

games.title: Wolfenstein: Youngblood
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set in 1980 with B.J.'s twin daughters in occupied Paris. Built for two-player co-op with a level-scaled enemy structure, and the weakest-received entry; it ends the modern arc on an unresolved note.

editions.name: Wolfenstein: Youngblood
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
editions.note: Deluxe listing includes a second copy to give a co-op partner.

name: XCOM
scope: Firaxis's reboot line: XCOM: Enemy Unknown, XCOM 2 and Chimera Squad, with their expansions. The 1990s X-COM games are a separate series with no shared continuity, and the shooter The Bureau: XCOM Declassified is excluded.
caveat: Chronology and release order match. The trap is the premise: XCOM 2 is set twenty years after Enemy Unknown and canonically assumes you lost that game — the aliens won, XCOM was disbanded, and the sequel starts from occupation. Winning Enemy Unknown does not carry over in any form. Chimera Squad follows five years after XCOM 2 with a different structure and a much smaller scope.

games.title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
games.note: The starting point, and the Complete Edition includes Enemy Within — a substantial expansion that adds units, a second enemy faction and new missions throughout the campaign rather than after it. Play with Enemy Within enabled.

editions.name: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
editions.note: Base game without the expansion.

editions.name: XCOM: Enemy Unknown Complete Edition
editions.note: Bundles Enemy Within and the smaller DLC.

games.title: XCOM 2
games.note: Opens with Earth already lost and XCOM as a guerrilla force. The Collection includes War of the Chosen, which rewrites enough of the campaign that it is effectively the default version — start there rather than with the base game.

editions.name: XCOM 2
editions.note: Base game; superseded by the expansion.

editions.name: XCOM 2 Collection
editions.note: Includes War of the Chosen and all DLC packs.

games.title: XCOM: Chimera Squad
games.note: Set five years after XCOM 2 in a city where humans and former invaders live together. Named characters instead of disposable recruits, interleaved turn order, and a much shorter campaign — a side entry, not XCOM 3, and PC only.

editions.name: XCOM: Chimera Squad
editions.note: The only release; never ported to consoles.

name: Xenoblade Chronicles
scope: The five Xenoblade games and the Future Redeemed story expansion. Xenosaga and Xenogears are separate series with their own continuities and are not included here.
caveat: Xenoblade Chronicles and Xenoblade Chronicles 2 take place in two worlds created by the same experiment and run in parallel, so their relative order is a formality rather than a sequence — either one works first. Xenoblade Chronicles 3 is where those two worlds converge, and it is the only entry that genuinely requires the others. Torna is set five hundred years before Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and is listed there for accuracy, but playing it first spoils a central reveal; play it after. Xenoblade Chronicles X's place in the timeline was left open until Future Redeemed, and is still not fully pinned down.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles
games.note: Standalone and the natural entry point. The Definitive Edition redraws the character models, rewrites the interface and adds Future Connected, an epilogue set a year later.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles
editions.note: Original release; the 3DS port was New 3DS only.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Remaster with new models, a rearranged score and the Future Connected epilogue.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles X
games.note: The odd one out — a survey-driven open world with a created protagonist, and no shared cast with the numbered games. The Definitive Edition adds a new final chapter that ties it to the rest of the series.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles X
editions.note: Original release, stranded on Wii U for a decade.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles X: Definitive Edition
editions.note: Remaster with an added epilogue chapter and reworked interface.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Torna – The Golden Country
games.version: Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Torna – The Golden Country
games.query: Xenoblade Chronicles 2 Torna The Golden Country
games.note: Set five hundred years before Xenoblade Chronicles 2, which is why it sits here — but it depicts events that game treats as a mystery, so play it second. Sold both as a standalone card and inside the Expansion Pass.

editions.name: Torna – The Golden Country
editions.note: Available standalone or via the Xenoblade Chronicles 2 Expansion Pass.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 2
games.note: A separate world from the first game with no returning characters; the connection is only visible at the very end. Its combat system takes roughly twenty hours to finish teaching itself.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles 2
editions.note: The only release; the Expansion Pass adds Torna and quality-of-life items.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 3
games.note: The convergence point: its world is the two earlier ones collapsed together, and its later chapters assume you have finished both. Playable cold, but most of the payoff will not land.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles 3
editions.note: The only release; the Expansion Pass adds Future Redeemed.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed
games.note: A short campaign that closes the whole series and explains how the three worlds relate, including Xenoblade Chronicles X. Sold only inside the Expansion Pass, never standalone, and it spoils everything before it.

editions.name: Xenoblade Chronicles 3 Expansion Pass
editions.note: Four waves of content; Future Redeemed is the last and the only story chapter.

name: Xenosaga
scope: The three PS2 episodes. The Japan-only DS compilation Xenosaga I & II and the mobile prequel Pied Piper are excluded because neither was ever released in English.
caveat: One story in three parts, in release order, with no prequels or side entries to work around. It was planned as six episodes and compressed into three, so Episode III covers far more ground than the others and the ending is abrupt. Despite the shared staff and themes, it has no continuity with Xenogears or Xenoblade. All three games are PS2-only and have never been re-released in any form.

games.title: Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht
games.version: Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht
games.query: Xenosaga Episode I Der Wille zur Macht
games.note: The only sensible starting point; the later episodes explain nothing. Roughly half its running time is cutscenes, which was the point of contention at release and still is.

editions.name: Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht
editions.note: The only English release; the Japanese Reloaded revision was never localised.

games.title: Xenosaga Episode II: Jenseits von Gut und Böse
games.version: Xenosaga Episode II: Jenseits von Gut und Böse
games.query: Xenosaga Episode II Jenseits von Gut und Bose
games.note: Continues directly from Episode I and imports its save for bonuses. It redesigned the entire cast between games, which makes the handover jarring even though the plot is continuous.

editions.name: Xenosaga Episode II: Jenseits von Gut und Böse
editions.note: The only release; includes a recap of Episode I as a bonus disc in some regions.

games.title: Xenosaga Episode III: Also sprach Zarathustra
games.version: Xenosaga Episode III: Also sprach Zarathustra
games.query: Xenosaga Episode III Also sprach Zarathustra
games.note: Compresses what was planned as three more games into one and ends the series. It includes an in-game database summarising the previous two, which is the closest thing to a shortcut the series offers.

editions.name: Xenosaga Episode III: Also sprach Zarathustra
editions.note: The only release; two discs.

name: Yakuza / Like a Dragon
scope: The main-line RGG Studio games about Kazuma Kiryu and Ichiban Kasuga. The Judgment detective games, the Kenzan and Ishin period spin-offs, the Dead Souls zombie game and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii are excluded.
caveat: Chronology and release order agree except at the ends. Yakuza 0 is a prequel released sixth, and it is where the timeline starts. Like a Dragon Gaiden came out after Yakuza: Like a Dragon but covers years that overlap it, filling the gap between Yakuza 6 and Infinite Wealth; it is placed at the end of the Kiryu arc here so that arc stays together. Yakuza 1 and 2 exist only as the Kiwami remakes on modern hardware.

arcs.name: Kiryu Saga
arcs.blurb: Kazuma Kiryu's life from 1988 to his supposed death and afterwards, across Kamurocho and half of Japan.

arcs.name: Ichiban Saga
arcs.blurb: Ichiban Kasuga's story, told as a turn-based RPG rather than a brawler, from Yokohama to Hawaii.

games.title: Yakuza 0
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series
games.note: Set in 1988, seventeen years before the first game, following a young Kiryu and Goro Majima. Released long after the games it precedes but written as an introduction, which is why it is the standard starting point.

name: Ys
scope: Adol Christin's adventures plus the prequel Ys Origin. Ys V: Kefin, Lost Kingdom of Sand is excluded because it has never been released in English, and the mobile and MMO spin-offs are excluded entirely.
caveat: Ys is a travelogue, not a serial: each game is a separate journal entry from Adol's life and almost all of them stand alone. The exception is Ys I and II, which are one story split in half. Chronology is worked out from Adol's stated age rather than from a published timeline, so the placement of the later games — Ys VIII and Ys X in particular — is inferred and not officially fixed. Release order and in-universe order have almost nothing to do with each other.

games.title: Ys Origin
games.platform: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch
games.note: Set seven hundred years before Ys I and the only game without Adol. It explains the backstory the first two games treat as legend, so it reads better after them than before.

editions.name: Ys Origin
editions.note: Japanese PC release; English version arrived in 2012.

editions.name: Ys Origin
editions.platforms: PC / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series / Switch

games.title: Ys I: Ancient Ys Vanished
games.note: Adol at seventeen, and the earliest of his journals. Chronicles+ is the 2009 PSP remake with three selectable soundtracks; it ends on a direct hand-off to Ys II.

editions.name: Ys I: Ancient Ys Vanished
editions.note: Decades of ports, most Japan-only.

editions.name: Ys I & II Chronicles+

games.title: Ys II: Ancient Ys Vanished – The Final Chapter
games.note: Continues from the exact moment Ys I ends and finishes its story; the two were designed as one game. The only pair in the series that must be played together.

editions.name: Ys I & II Chronicles+

games.title: Ys X: Nordics
games.note: Falcom places this early in Adol's travels, shortly after Ys II, despite it being the newest game in the series. Naval combat and a two-character party make it play unlike anything else here.

editions.name: Ys: Memories of Celceta

name: Zero Escape
scope: The three Zero Escape visual novels by Kotaro Uchikoshi. The unrelated AI: The Somnium Files games by the same writer are excluded.
caveat: In-universe order and release order disagree, and here the release order is the one to follow. 999 is set in 2027 and Virtue's Last Reward in 2074, but Zero Time Dilemma, released last, is a midquel set in 2028 between them. Playing Zero Time Dilemma second would spoil most of Virtue's Last Reward's central twists, since it was written assuming you already knew them.

games.title: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors
games.note: The first Nonary Game, in 2027, and the start of the series in every sense. The Nonary Games collection remasters it with voice acting and a flowchart, but its original DS version used both screens for a trick the remaster has to solve differently.

editions.name: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors
editions.note: Original release; the two-screen presentation is part of one puzzle.

editions.name: Zero Escape: The Nonary Games
editions.note: 999 remastered plus Virtue's Last Reward in one purchase.

games.title: Zero Escape: Zero Time Dilemma
games.note: Chronologically second, set in a Nevada shelter in 2028, and the origin of the outbreak that shapes Virtue's Last Reward. Released third and written to be played third; treat this position as timeline information, not a play order.

editions.name: Zero Escape: Zero Time Dilemma
editions.note: Later released for PS4; presentation moves to 3D cutscenes rather than sprites.

games.title: Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward
games.note: Set in 2074, decades after the other two, and the last point on the timeline. Sold only inside The Nonary Games collection listed on the 999 row; the original 3DS version has a save-corrupting bug that the remaster fixes.

editions.name: Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward
editions.note: Original release; the 3DS version can corrupt saves if you save at the wrong moment.

editions.name: Zero Escape: The Nonary Games
editions.note: Bundled with the remastered 999; the standard way to buy it.
